records.description: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI), in institutional cooperation with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment of the UAE, the Municipal Council of Khorfakkan, and the Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock, has opened the fifth annual Khorfakkan Mango Festival under the theme "Mango: Our Fruit, Our Wealth." Designed as a strategic marketing and commercial platform to align with the UAE National Food Security Strategy 2051, this year's edition recorded a 40% increase in participation and expanded its exhibition infrastructure by 70% to accommodate 55 domestic and regional farmers, including agricultural delegations from Oman, Qatar, Kuwait, and Uganda. Displaying more than 150 varieties of locally grown mangoes and citrus fruits, the state-backed initiative establishes direct public-private marketing channels to optimize smallholder financial returns, incentivize entrepreneurship in agro-processing value-added industries, and promote modern agrotech deployment to strengthen the nation's agricultural self-sufficiency and economic diversification.
records.institution: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI)

records.title: The Invest Oman agency, driving national food security priorities under the Oman Vision 2040 development framework, has structured a majo...
records.description: The Invest Oman agency, driving national food security priorities under the Oman Vision 2040 development framework, has structured a major public-private investment opportunity to construct the Al Salil Smart Agricultural Cluster in Quriyat, a specialized agrotech development requiring a capital expenditure of RO17 million. Spanning over 2.09 million square meters, the mega-cluster is engineered to consolidate multi-tiered farming operations combining open-field plots, shade-net facilities, climate-controlled smart greenhouses, and yield-intensive vertical farming systems to generate an estimated 62 million kilograms of annual crop output, targeting high-value commodities such as strawberries, cherry tomatoes, and water-efficient leafy greens. Utilizing optimized irrigation networks drawing from the Wadi Dayqah Dam and regional groundwater reserves, the phased infrastructure project is strategically positioned near the Muscat consumer market to scale up national fruit and vegetable self-sufficiency, generate rural technical employment, and significantly lower the country's international food import bill.
records.institution: The Invest Oman agency

records.title: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman, in institutional coord...
records.description: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman, in institutional coordination with architectural firm Foster + Partners and consulting firm Dar Al-Handasah, have launched the master plan for Al Najd Agricultural City in Dhofar, a 54 million-square-foot, zero-waste agricultural and urban settlement engineered to house 13,000 residents and generate 6,500 jobs in alignment with Oman Vision 2040. The self-sustaining development incorporates rectangular farm clusters ranging from 10 to 200 hectares dedicated to regionally optimized crops like date palms and greenhouse tomatoes, supported by an advanced, multi-source water strategy utilizing groundwater, mountain runoff dams, and desalinated seawater. Managed alongside broader national food security initiatives—including a separate agricultural city near Saham designed by the Surbana Jurong Group—the project is structured to scale agro-processing industries, produce organic fertilizers, and accelerate high-value food export pipelines.
records.institution: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning

records.title: The Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform of Syria, in coordination with the UAE's state-backed AD Po...
records.description: The Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform of Syria, in coordination with the UAE's state-backed AD Ports Group and agri-food conglomerate Silal Group, have advanced talks to establish a multimodal regional trade and logistics corridor. The infrastructure project is engineered to connect Syrian ports with Iraq’s port of Umm Qasr via a weekly shipping service running from Khalifa Port in the UAE, effectively linking the Gulf with Turkish and European commercial corridors while integrating dry ports across Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, and a strategic hub at the Al-Tanf border crossing. Simultaneously, the public-private partnership incorporates two major agricultural investment agreements with Silal Group establishing contract farming structures, direct procurement mechanisms, and sorting facilities to export at least 16,000 tons of local potatoes and seasonal crops to the UAE market.
records.institution: AD Ports Group, Silal Group

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture of Saudi Arabia, operating under its "Sweet in Season" campaign to promote localized crop diversification and improve agricultural marketing efficiency, has announced that domestic pomegranate production has reached over 39,700 tons annually. Cultivated across a national footprint of more than 1.3 million productive trees, the crop is concentrated in high-yield agricultural regions including Asir, Makkah, Tabuk, Qassim, and Al-Baha. By utilizing state-backed agricultural guidance, tailored financing facilities, and modern agrotech systems, local smallholders harvest diverse commercial varieties—such as Taif, Hijazi, Wonderful, and Eversweet—designed to thrive in the regional climate. This coordinated public-private supply chain optimization ensures that fresh local produce effectively reaches commercial agrifood processing and retail markets, maximizing smallholder financial returns while advancing the Kingdom's non-oil economic goals and domestic food security objectives.

Designed as a direct agrifood marketing platform and a local agricultural enterprise incubator, the three-day event integrates local farmers, productive families, and UAE agribusinesses to showcase premium domestic mangoes, citrus fruits, and seasonal crops. To incentivize high-quality production and agricultural transparency, the festival hosts five specialized categories—including crop beauty and innovation competitions—enforcing strict compliance measures such as mandatory land ownership verification and field inspection audits by a formal judging committee. By blending traditional heritage activities with scientific workshops on modern cultivation, pest control, and sustainable tree management, the state-backed initiative enhances smallholder commercial viability, drives technical optimization, and safeguards regional food security goals.

records.description: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion of Oman, operating through its export promotion framework alongside Algerian trade authorities, has finalized several strategic agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoUs) at the 57th Algiers International Fair. The bilateral frameworks establish direct trade channels and corporate partnerships across high-priority industrial sectors, including logistics, food processing, fisheries, downstream manufacturing, building materials, chemical fertilizers, and pharmaceuticals. Aligned with the non-oil export maximization and market diversification objectives of Oman Vision 2040, the state-backed trade offensive leverages direct business-to-business (B2B) networks to accelerate the penetration of national products across Algerian and broader continental African economic corridors. This report focuses on international trade diplomacy, bilateral investment mobilization, and macro-level export diversification frameworks; it is not related to the current Middle East conflict.

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, operating in alignment with the food security and agricultural localization targets of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 transformation agenda, has announced that domestic grape production has scaled to exceed 128,000 tons for the summer harvest season. Cultivated across more than 6.3 million productive grapevines, the geographic distribution of the crop spans premium agricultural basins including Tabuk, Qassim, Hail, Al-Jouf, Madinah, Aseer, and the Taif Governorate. By integrating modern agrotech systems and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), local smallholders systematically harvest diverse commercial varieties—such as Taifi, Helwani, Banati, Crimson Seedless, and Thompson Seedless—which effectively extends the seasonal harvest window from July through August. This state-supported output fulfills local fresh consumption demand, minimizes import reliance overheads, and anchors regional downstream fruit processing industries.

records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), operating in strategic collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the National Agriculture Centre, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), and the Gates Foundation, has celebrated the graduation of the fourth cohort of the Arab Women Leaders in Agriculture Fellowship Program (AWLA). The leadership and research capacity-building initiative adds 21 new fellows from across the Arab region, bringing the cumulative total to 79 graduates specializing in agricultural innovation, resource management, and food security. Executed against global frameworks recognizing women's contributions to sustainable food systems, the state-backed platform empowers female researchers and agriculturalists to deploy science-based, climate-smart crop solutions to combat compounding regional challenges including water scarcity, land degradation, and severe climate-induced pressures in arid environments.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.description: The Oman Flour Mills (OFM), in direct institutional partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR), has officially initiated its sixth consecutive national wheat procurement and purchase program for the 2026 harvest season. Designed as a key agricultural localization and smallholder empowerment initiative under the overarching framework of the Oman Vision 2040 development strategy, the program provides Omani farmers across multiple governorates with an organized, guaranteed marketing channel and standardized technical benchmarks for grain supply. By receiving, processing, and converting diverse domestic wheat varieties into added-value national food products, the enterprise has successfully accelerated local wheat output nearly 20-fold since 2021, thereby expanding strategic domestic grain reserves from an eight-month to a ten-month supply, reducing import dependency risks, and safeguarding localized rural livelihoods.
records.institution: The Oman Flour Mills (OFM)

records.description: The Oman Flour Mills Company, in direct integration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, has commenced its annual Omani Wheat Receiving and Purchasing Program for the domestic harvest. Serving as a strategic national mechanism to enhance food security and secure local food supply chains, the initiative provides smallholders and commercial growers with a stable, organized marketing channel and fair-market pricing to incentivize the expansion of wheat cultivation. The agricultural cycle has drawn active participation across multiple governorates, demonstrating stable farmer engagement, high diversification of indigenous wheat varieties, and projected yield increases relative to previous seasons. By processing the raw grain into value-added national food products, the enterprise drives local economic retention, elevates supply-chain resilience, and reinforces standardized technical benchmarks for domestic harvesting and supply logistics.
records.institution: The Oman Flour Mills Company

records.description: The Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI), in collaboration with the Falcon Training Institute, implemented the "Model Farm Management" programme across the Governorates of South Al Batinah, South Al Sharqiyah, and Dhofar to enhance local agricultural production, optimize resource efficiency, and stimulate sustainable agribusiness investments. Designed to align with the socioeconomic development goals of Oman Vision 2040, the specialized training initiative equipped agricultural entrepreneurs and model farm owners with advanced skills in supply chain optimization, modern marketing strategies, value-added food processing, and efficient resource management. The theoretical coursework was directly augmented by on-site field visits to leading regional agricultural enterprises, including the Agricultural and Fisheries Development Company and Dhofar Foods and Investment Company, where participants analyzed practical field applications of water-efficient irrigation, smart farming technologies, and collective exporting frameworks. This initiative represents one of five macro-sector operational training tracks orchestrated by the chamber to expand private sector capability, reduce industrial waste, and accelerate economic diversification across the Sultanate's governorates.

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) has revealed that watermelon has secured the top position in Saudi Arabia’s summer fruit sector, with total annual production surpassing 620,000 tons. Distributed across a highly diverse geographic matrix—including Riyadh, Makkah, the Eastern Region, Al-Jouf, Al-Baha, Madinah, Qassim, Tabuk, Hail, Aseer, and Jazan—the crop is highly valued both for fresh seasonal consumption and as a vital raw input for domestic food-processing industries. In alignment with Saudi Vision 2030 economic diversification and food security targets, public authorities are actively backing local growers by deploying targeted agricultural guidance, direct development financing, and modern water-efficient farming technologies while refining integrated marketing and supply-chain logistics to maximize local self-sufficiency during peak summer demand.

records.description: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion has organized the Sultanate of Oman’s official participation in the 57th Algiers International Fair at the Pins Maritime Exhibition Palace. Aligned with the economic diversification and non-oil export expansion targets of Oman Vision 2040, a delegation of 20 Omani companies is representing a diverse array of industrial sectors. records.title: Silal Group, Delphy join forces to elevate local capabilities across UAE's food, agriculture sector
records.description: The Silal Group, in direct coordination with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, has finalized a five-year strategic collaboration agreement with the Dutch agricultural consultancy Delphy to advance national training and capacity-building programs. Centered within Silal Group’s Innovation Oasis and Delphy Research Centres, the partnership integrates cutting-edge agricultural science with practical field applications to address localized food security challenges and scale up the domestic knowledge infrastructure. The technical curriculum focuses on optimizing high-efficiency open-field and protected-crop cultivation methodologies—such as advanced automated greenhouse and hydroponic systems—while simultaneously developing sustainable business models, feasibility frameworks, and commercialization pathways to enhance the profitability of local farming operations. Executed as a structural milestone for the agritech sector, this international knowledge-transfer initiative directly supports the UAE’s National Food Security Strategy 2051 by empowering local talent with specialized agronomic and commercial expertise.

records.description: The Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD), in a strategic bilateral partnership with the Government of Uzbekistan—represented by the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change and the Ministry of Agriculture—has financed the Agricultural Systems Development Project in Karakalpakstan with a total investment of AED 18.7 million. Executed in direct technical collaboration with the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), the International Innovation Center for the Aral Sea Basin (IICAS), and the Karakalpakstan Agricultural Research Institute (KARI), the project deploys integrated agricultural infrastructure to mitigate the severe environmental impacts of drought and desertification caused by the Aral Sea crisis. The climate-adaptive infrastructure introduces over 20 varieties of drought- and salinity-tolerant crops, modernizes localized irrigation and drainage networks, and establishes co-managed agriculture-aquaculture frameworks to maximize resource efficiency.

records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment and the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure are driving the execution of the UAE's National Strategy to Combat Desertification 2022–2030, a roadmap composed of 33 key initiatives built across five environmental pillars to target a 40% increase in local production efficiency, the restoration of 80% of applicable degraded lands, and a 60% treated water reuse rate. Supported by complementary frameworks like the National Biodiversity Strategy 2031 and the Blue Carbon Project, the nation has integrated advanced technological interventions including aerial agricultural mapping, dedicated saline agriculture research stations, and an extensive network of 109 dams that recently retained 72 million cubic metres of rainfall to supply critical irrigation. These structural measures are further reinforced by the newly launched National Agricultural Initiative for the Adoption of Climate-Smart Crops, transforming severe climate vulnerabilities into proactive, sustainable development pathways.

Focused on localizing the agricultural input sector, the initiative showcases technologies and protective treatments manufactured domestically from safe organic components. The industrial framework aims to reduce import dependencies, drive private investment, and encourage farmers to transition toward safer domestic alternatives to minimize chemical risks while expanding rural jobs. By creating a collaborative platform to present successful local agricultural models and technical guidance, public authorities aim to enhance agricultural modernization, support sustainable cultivation, and achieve national food self-sufficiency.

records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman, operating through its Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in the Al Dhahirah Governorate, has issued an official regulatory alert prohibiting the use of untreated sewage water for the irrigation of agricultural land. The regional enforcement directive underscores that the deployment of non-potable wastewater in primary crop production explicitly violates the statutory provisions and executive regulations of the national Agriculture System Law. Designed to insulate local aquifers from environmental contamination, uphold strict public food safety standards, and protect consumers from soil-borne pathogenic risks, this public health intervention reinforces the state's legal framework governing sustainable resource management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), in coordination with the Al-Ahsa Municipality, has launched a series of strategic marketing initiatives to manage the commencement of the annual fresh date harvest across the Al-Ahsa Oasis. Accelerated by high summer temperatures that drive early crop ripening, the region’s agricultural network is actively sorting and distributing over 20 distinct palm varieties, drawing from an expansive ecological matrix of more than two million palm trees that yield over 120,000 tons of dates annually. To optimize the supply chain and bolster economic returns for local farmers, public authorities have deployed specialized field teams to directly oversee commercial auction processes while establishing seasonal date festivals and integrated farmers' markets to connect local producers with domestic and regional trade networks.

records.title: The National Center for Palms and Dates, under the leadership of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, will represent Saudi...
records.description: The National Center for Palms and Dates, under the leadership of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, will represent Saudi Arabia as the guest of honor at the Fancy Food Show in New York City. This high-profile international deployment is strategically designed to expand the global market footprint and export channels of premium Saudi date varieties and their derived value-added products. Positioned as a major driver of agricultural economic diversification under Saudi Vision 2030, the kingdom's date export sector has achieved a commercial valuation of nearly SR2 billion, with distribution networks already spanning 1,500 retail outlets globally. The upcoming trade pavilion will enable a delegation of national agribusinesses to leverage a professional platform of over 30,000 international visitors and 2,400 exhibitors, facilitating direct B2B networking, bilateral commercial agreements, and supply-chain integration with global distributors.
records.institution: The National Center for Palms and Dates, Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, acting via direct directives from the Crown Prince and coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has o...
records.description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, acting via direct directives from the Crown Prince and coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has officially ordered the full resumption of Lebanese imports into its domestic markets, effectively dismantling a five-year economic blockade initially imposed in April 2021 due to regional Captagon narcotics smuggling networks. This major trade breakthrough was brokered following high-level diplomatic appeals from the state institutions of Lebanon, specifically the newly established presidency and prime ministerial cabinet. The diplomatic and trade normalization reflects growing regional institutional confidence in the Lebanese government's recent regulatory, customs, and security measures designed to rebuild credible state agencies, secure national border controls, and aggressively curb illicit transnational trafficking. The restoration of this strategic trade gateway is anticipated to inject up to $500 million annually into the Lebanese private sector, offering a substantial fiscal lifeline to domestic agricultural and manufacturing industries while systematically realigning Beirut's economic and political ties with the Arab Gulf states.
records.institution: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

records.description: The US-Qatar Business Council in Doha, in partnership with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), has launched a strategic investment roadmap designed to accelerate development in Qatar's agriculture and agrifood sector. Developed over a year-long consultative period with public and private stakeholders, the framework provides actionable guidance for policymakers and investors to strengthen food security, optimize supply chain logistics, and build resilient food systems through both localized production and targeted emerging international market assets. The initiative introduces specialized evaluation tools to help investors identify high-value agricultural commodities across various geographies, positioning Qatar as a regional hub for agrifood innovation, economic diversification, and sustainable commercial returns.

records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in collaboration with entities like Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), OQ, and the Oman Agriculture Development Company, has accelerated an integrated suite of smart agronomical and afforestation initiatives designed to curb carbon emissions across the country's plant, livestock, and aquaculture sectors. Driven by advanced technological transitions—such as AI-based precision fertilization systems that minimize input waste and pollution—the ministry has deployed and monitored multiple sustainability projects targeted at carbon sequestration, organic fertilizer production, and blue carbon ecosystems. Key structural developments include targeted commercial fruit and forestry initiatives—such as the OQ Green project, the cultivation of carbon-capturing hackberry trees, and expansive lemon and jojoba plantations across Shalim and Al Wusta designed to combat desertification while drastically boosting domestic fruit yields. Additionally, specialized research at the Animal Production Research Centre has successfully optimized livestock feed efficiency using local moringa and palm resources, lowering production costs by over 58% to harmonize national agricultural expansion with long-term climate sustainability targets.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA) oversaw the signing of 13 strategic bilateral agreements between Saudi Arabia...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA) oversaw the signing of 13 strategic bilateral agreements between Saudi Arabia and Russia, totaling SR4.8 billion in investments, on the sidelines of the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum. Orchestrated to advance the food security, biotechnology localization, and supply-chain resilience targets of Saudi Vision 2030, the public-private partnerships focus heavily on stabilizing livestock and agrifood systems. Key structural provisions within the agreements mandate the domestic manufacturing and localization of veterinary vaccines to enhance regional biosecurity, the development of specialized broiler poultry strains to accelerate meat self-sufficiency, and the security of long-term grain and feed input supply chains. Additionally, the investment framework opens new international distribution channels for Saudi aquaculture and niche agricultural exports, establishing trade protocols for Russian firms to market and distribute Saudi shrimp, fish, camel milk derivatives, and specialty coffee products globally.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is accelerating its net-zero emissions strategy for the agricultural sector by...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is accelerating its net-zero emissions strategy for the agricultural sector by scaling up the deployment of smart farming technologies and climate-resilient frameworks. The initiatives emphasize the adoption of artificial intelligence, internet-of-things (IoT) devices, automated irrigation networks, and precision fertilization methods designed to minimize water, energy, and chemical inputs. To offset emissions, the national program incorporates environmental restoration projects, including blue carbon ecosystem management, organic fertilizer manufacturing, and large-scale afforestation using high-capacity carbon-sequestering tree species. Furthermore, the modernization of livestock supply chains via the upcycling of local agricultural waste into sustainable animal feed aims to reduce operational overheads for farmers while driving down carbon footprints.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality has substantially expanded Qatar's urban green infrastructure, driving the nation’s total green area to 21.9...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality has substantially expanded Qatar's urban green infrastructure, driving the nation’s total green area to 21.9 million square metres and increasing the average citizen's allocation of green space to 6.8 square metres. Designed to fulfill the environmental sustainability and urban planning metrics of the Qatar National Vision 2030, the multi-sector initiative encompasses the planned scaling of public parks to 156 installations alongside the widespread rollout of 1,864 water-efficient irrigation networks across 715 domestic farms. To catalyze a localized circular economy, municipal authorities simultaneously modernized national waste management operations, processing over 755,000 tonnes of municipal waste, recovering approximately 4 million tonnes of recycled construction aggregates, treating 10,470 tonnes of end-of-life tires, and generating 276,000 megawatt-hours of electricity via dedicated waste-to-energy facilities while yielding 34,213 tonnes of organic compost for agricultural replenishment.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipality

records.description: The Civil Aviation Authority—acting in coordination with national environmental and water resource management bodies—has expanded the Sultanate of Oman's artificial rainfall enhancement network to 14 operational stations to strengthen national water security. Distributed across highly strategic topographic vectors including the Hajar Mountains, Musandam, and Dhofar, the infrastructure utilizes advanced chemical-free ionization technology to emit negative ions into the atmosphere, accelerating cloud condensation nuclei formation during suitable meteorological windows. This technological framework has successfully optimized seasonal precipitation yields, accelerated groundwater aquifer recharge rates, and mitigated dust pollution levels to bolster climate resilience across the country's arid zones. This report focuses on innovative water resource management, climate-adaptive technology deployment, and regional groundwater infrastructure; it is not related to the current Middle East conflict.

records.description: The World Bank Group has approved a new five-year Country Partnership Framework alongside four development operations totaling 285 million U.S. dollars to drive sustainable recovery, expand public service delivery, and stimulate job creation within a fragile, conflict-affected landscape. Strategically aligned with national stabilization priorities, the foundational investments target rapid rehabilitation across critical multi-sector networks including public health systems, nutrition programs, primary electrical grids, municipal water harvesting installations, and agricultural and fisheries management. By pivoting toward an agile, localized deployment model, the programmatic framework seeks to rebuild institutional capacities, enhance macroeconomic governance, and empower vulnerable populations by expanding the economic participation of women and scaling private sector infrastructure investments.
records.institution: The World Bank Group

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) of Oman has announced two new localized agricultural investment projec...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) of Oman has announced two new localized agricultural investment projects in the Al Ghuwayl area of the Ibri Wilayat, situated within the Al Dhahirah Governorate. Part of a broader state-backed strategy to expand modern agricultural production through private sector capital, the first venture establishes an advanced 10-acre tissue culture laboratory designed for the rapid and large-scale cultivation of disease-free, high-quality botanical seedlings and saplings to supply the domestic farming market. The second concurrent project allocates an additional 10 acres to the intensive cultivation of leafy vegetables utilizing a combination of protected greenhouse environments and traditional open fields. By introducing advanced agricultural technologies such as controlled-environment greenhouse systems and automated resource-efficiency workflows, the integrated initiatives are engineered to maximize year-round crop yields, conserve local groundwater resources, and accelerate import substitution to fortify national food security architecture in line with Oman Vision 2040.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) has finalized a memorandum of understanding with the Russian Ministry of...
records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) has finalized a memorandum of understanding with the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment to expand bilateral coordination on environmental preservation and ecological sustainability. Signed by administrative leadership from both nations, the cooperation framework outlines joint operational initiatives to expand vegetation cover, mitigate land degradation, enforce sustainable forestry practices, and modernize management models for natural and protected areas. Additionally, the partnership institutes data-sharing protocols and a joint working group to coordinate environmental monitoring, expand waste management infrastructure, protect migratory bird routes, and conduct scientific research to counter the illegal trade of endangered flora and fauna.
records.institution: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE) has officially launched the Abu Dhabi Water and Energy Resilience Framework during the third edi...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE) has officially launched the Abu Dhabi Water and Energy Resilience Framework during the third edition of the Water and Energy Majlis, held under the umbrella of Abu Dhabi Water & Power Week. Structured around three foundational pillars—infrastructure, human capital and governance, and technology and innovation—the newly introduced framework mandates 15 strategic measures designed to optimize supply security, capacity planning, emergency preparedness, and the diversification of vital resource networks. Developed to align with the UAE Water Security Strategy 2036 and the Net Zero 2050 charter, the initiative integrates advanced reverse osmosis desalination technologies, artificial intelligence for meteorological forecasting, and cloud-seeding methodologies advanced by the National Centre of Meteorology. Multi-lateral collaborations emphasized treating water, energy, and food security as a single interconnected system, anchored globally by strategic platforms like the Mohamed bin Zayed Water Initiative to mitigate regional resources vulnerabilities and enhance climate-smart distribution networks.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) continues to expand its utility-scale infrastructure portfolio to accelerate carbon emis...
records.description: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) continues to expand its utility-scale infrastructure portfolio to accelerate carbon emission reductions and support the overarching Dubai Clean Energy Strategy 2050 and the Dubai Net Zero Carbon Emissions Strategy 2050. Anchored by the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park—the largest single-site solar park in the world utilizing the independent power producer model—the authority has reached an operational capacity of 3,860 MW utilizing photovoltaic and concentrated solar power systems, on track to exceed 8,000 MW by 2030. This scaling capacity is projected to elevate clean energy to 36% of Dubai's total generation mix by 2030, mitigating over 8.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually. Concurrently, the authority operates the Middle East and North Africa region’s first industrial-scale solar-powered Green Hydrogen facility, generating 20 kilograms of hydrogen per hour with 240 kilograms of storage capacity to serve as a flexible testing platform for zero-emission grid re-electrification and secondary industrial applications.
records.institution: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA)

records.title: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), in direct partnership with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, hos...
records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), in direct partnership with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, hosted "Millets Harvest Day" to advance the National Agricultural Initiative for the Adoption of Climate-Smart Crops in the UAE. Geared toward translating agronomic research into scalable field applications, the initiative promotes the widespread cultivation of millet varieties specifically optimized to tolerate drought, extreme heat, and high soil salinity while requiring significantly less water than conventional grains. The multi-partner event engaged local farmers, researchers, and policymakers through field demonstrations and live harvesting, while introducing value-added food prototypes—such as millet milk and bio-fortified baked goods—to establish more resource-efficient, climate-resilient agrifood supply chains across the UAE's hyper-arid environments.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in coordination with the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority (DECCA)...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in coordination with the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority (DECCA) and the Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA) in Sharjah, launched a series of community-centric environmental preservation initiatives timed with World Environment Day. Structured to advance the UAE's strategic target of planting 100 million mangroves by 2030 and fulfilling its obligations under the international Mangrove Alliance for Climate (MAC), the multi-regional field operations encompassed a large-scale mangrove restoration drive at Khor Kalba, an endangered marine turtle release at the Jebel Ali Wildlife Sanctuary, and specialized public health workshops at the Thukher Club to embed food safety systems and sustainable consumption habits within family units. Backed by quantitative gains in national metrics—including elevating the domestic environmental awareness index to 89% and the environmental behavior index to 85% through volunteer-led tree distribution campaigns—these initiatives utilize nature-based carbon sequestration and public ecology programs to reinforce regional biodiversity protection and long-term climate change mitigation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality, through its 2025 Annual Report and the targeted work of the Animal Wealth Department, has accelerated the l...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality, through its 2025 Annual Report and the targeted work of the Animal Wealth Department, has accelerated the licensing of 45 livestock and animal production projects to enhance domestic production and reduce import reliance. In line with the sustainable agricultural objectives of the Qatar National Vision 2030, the portfolio comprises 30 operational initiatives and 15 facilities under active development, spanning 14 meat production farms, 11 general poultry and livestock ventures, 8 broiler chicken facilities, 6 table egg production sites, and 4 dairy operations, alongside specialized broiler parent stock and turkey breeding installations. Driven by these integrated public-private investments, the country has achieved a 99% domestic self-sufficiency rate in both local dairy production (reaching 171,283 tonnes) and poultry meat output (totaling 26,376 tonnes). This programmatic scaling is backed by rigorous annual livestock assessments tracking over one million animals—including sheep, goats, camels, and cattle—to stabilize national food supply chains through technological and structural modernization.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipality

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has broken ground on a $4.2 billion, 65-square-kilometer agricultural city nea...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has broken ground on a $4.2 billion, 65-square-kilometer agricultural city near Saham in the Batnah region. Supervised by the Singapore-based consultancy Surbana Jurong Group and built by a conglomerate of local companies, the mega-project is slated for completion in the third quarter of 2028. The initiative aims to enhance national food self-sufficiency and insulate the sultanate from global market volatility by distributing free land and offering subsidized advanced farming equipment to local producers. The smart city will leverage agritech innovations—such as hydroponics, aeroponics, and aquaculture—to feed 25,000 people annually, serving as a flagship blueprint among 140 development projects designed to curb the nation's rising reliance on foreign food imports.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in coordination with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has official...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in coordination with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has officially launched construction on a 65-square-kilometer, $4.2 billion sustainable agricultural city near Saham in the Al Batinah North region. Supervised by the infrastructure consultancy Surbana Jurong Group, the mega-project aims to aggressively mitigate import reliance—which currently drives 30% of national market purchases—by integrating high-efficiency agritech systems, including hydroponics, aeroponics, and advanced aquaculture networks designed to secure baseline nutrition for 25,000 residents annually. Operating as a structural anchor under the national food sufficiency strategy, which encompasses roughly 140 parallel development projects to buffer global supply chain volatility, the development model leverages subsidized hardware allocations and free land distributions to scale localized farming outputs and reinforce climate-resilient economic diversification.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The National Center for Palms and Dates has announced a 25% year-on-year increase in Saudi Arabian date exports to India.
records.description: The National Center for Palms and Dates has announced a 25% year-on-year increase in Saudi Arabian date exports to India. This growth is driven by shifting Indian consumer preferences toward healthier, high-quality alternatives to sugar-based confectionery, alongside an expanding trend of purchasing dates as year-round gifts rather than exclusively for seasonal religious periods. Indian trade operators, including commercial entities like Hindustan Foreign Traders and Vishal Enterprise, report robust demand spikes for premium varieties such as Safawi (locally termed Kalami) and Sukkari. Importers attribute the competitive edge of Saudi products over regional alternatives—such as Iranian varieties—to superior quality, enhanced shelf-life stability, and balanced pricing, which have collectively expanded market penetration across diverse consumer demographics in urban hubs like New Delhi.
records.institution: The National Center for Palms and Dates

records.description: A public company, in cooperation with government authorities and local farmers, is expanding support for ginger and turmeric production by purchasing harvests directly from farms to strengthen food security and promote sustainable agriculture. The initiative benefits 78 farms, with production reaching over 98,447 kg of turmeric and 468 kg of ginger, and aims to develop stable market channels, encourage cultivation of high-value crops, and enhance the competitiveness of local agricultural products through improved access to domestic markets.

records.title: Yemen has achieved self-sufficiency in potato seed production after halting imports 3 years ago, with domestic output now exceeding 8,000...
records.description: Yemen has achieved self-sufficiency in potato seed production after halting imports 3 years ago, with domestic output now exceeding 8,000 tons during the latest spring season. The General Company for Potato Seed Production in Dhamar supplies 9 locally developed seed varieties, supporting expanded cultivation and stabilizing prices in the local market. Government officials are promoting the use of locally produced seeds, encouraging farmers to rely on domestic varieties, and are now considering exporting surplus production, reflecting a broader strategy to strengthen agricultural self-sufficiency and reduce import dependence.
records.institution: the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and The General Company for Potato Seed Production in Dhamar Governorate

records.title: Yemen’s agricultural sector is undergoing a major transformation toward self-sufficiency, supported by government policies that expand pr...
records.description: Yemen’s agricultural sector is undergoing a major transformation toward self-sufficiency, supported by government policies that expand production, restrict imports, and strengthen food security. Crop production increased significantly, with cereals rising by 21% and legumes by 31% between 2015 and 2025, while wheat cultivation expanded to 18,000 hectares and maize reached 40,000 hectares with output of about 120,000 tonnes. New crops such as soybean now cover 1,350 hectares with expected production of 3,200 tonnes, involving over 300 farmers. The government has also banned imports of more than 52 agricultural products, contributing to savings of over $134 million, including $86.9 million in poultry imports. Livestock numbers exceed 10.7 million sheep, 10.3 million goats, and nearly 2 million cattle, while poultry production reached about 200,000 tonnes and 1.5 billion eggs in 2025, alongside investments such as 8.8 billion rials in dairy development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.description: Al-Maghrabah Cooperative launched the rice harvest in one district of Yemen, producing more than 7 tonnes of rice as part of efforts to improve farmers’ incomes and expand cultivation. The initiative reflects growing interest among farmers and plans to increase rice production in the coming period, with support from local associations to promote agriculture and help communities cope with economic challenges.
records.institution: Al-Maghrabah Cooperative

records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) obtained two international ISO certifications (ISO 26000 for social responsibility and ISO 21502 for project management) following successful assessments of its governance and operational practices. The achievement reflects ADAFSA’s commitment to global standards, sustainability, and institutional efficiency. The Authority has also strengthened community engagement through initiatives like the “Auwn” programme, which organised 292 events with 3,114 volunteers contributing 14,568 hours between 2019 and 2025. These efforts support improved project management, resource use, transparency, and the integration of social responsibility into agriculture, food security, and community development.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.description: Oman has launched a national project to recycle agricultural and animal waste into 25,000 tonnes of organic fertiliser annually, along with animal feed and palm frond-based construction materials, aiming to turn waste into economic value while improving soil fertility and reducing environmental harm. Using advanced recycling technologies, the initiative supports local farmers, cuts reliance on chemical fertilisers and imported wood, lowers emissions, and promotes a circular economy by converting farm residues into sustainable products.

records.title: Ecuador’s banana industry has reached record export volumes in early 2026, but production has dropped by about 30% due to low rainfall, i...
records.description: Ecuador’s banana industry has reached record export volumes in early 2026, but production has dropped by about 30% due to low rainfall, inadequate irrigation preparation, and rising input costs influenced by geopolitical tensions. Despite these challenges, the sector has shown resilience by opening new trade routes to Saudi Arabia and Turkey, creating alternative supply chains and opportunities for investors. However, risks remain significant, particularly from the deadly Fusarium disease and ongoing global instability, which continue to drive higher prices and uncertainty even as the industry adapts and grows.
records.institution: Ecuadorian banana exporters and producers, government and investors in Saudi arabia and turkey

records.description: Oman Food Investment Company (OFIC), in partnership with Al Saffa Poultry and private financial investors, is developing a $260 million poultry farm (Namma Poultry) as part of a national strategy to reduce reliance on imports and strengthen food security. The project responds to high regional import dependence—around 90% of food consumption and aims to increase domestic production of poultry, alongside parallel investments in dairy and livestock imports to expand local supply capacity.

records.title: The Ministry of Energy and Minerals has released an updated national roadmap for net-zero emissions alongside a new regulatory framework...
records.description: The Ministry of Energy and Minerals has released an updated national roadmap for net-zero emissions alongside a new regulatory framework for carbon markets, aiming for full carbon neutrality by 2050. Developed by the Oman Centre for Net-Zero, the strategy targets a 33% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2035 by converting mitigation efforts into tradable carbon credits to attract international investment. While maintaining a steady daily production of one million barrels of oil and expanding gas exploration, the institution is prioritizing a shift toward green industries, with targets for renewable energy to reach 10% of the mix by the end of this year and up to 100% by 2050. Key developments include $44 billion in green hydrogen investments, the establishment of a commercial hydrogen corridor with the Netherlands, and a 92% Omanization rate within the energy sector.

records.title: Dava Agricultural has announced the launch of the Taif mega-project, an expansion of controlled-environment farming covering 350 hectares...
records.description: Dava Agricultural has announced the launch of the Taif mega-project, an expansion of controlled-environment farming covering 350 hectares of glass greenhouses. The initiative aims to scale daily fresh produce output to 1,000 tons by 2030, building on the company's current 13.8% share of national greenhouse production. By utilizing high-tech hydroponic systems and water-saving technologies, the project seeks to replace various imported crops with premium local varieties, including tomatoes, grapes, and blueberries, while diversifying into open-field cultivation and sustainable energy through an on-site solar park. This development serves as a strategic move to strengthen national self-sufficiency and establish the region as a competitive exporter of fresh produce, particularly during the winter months.
records.institution: Dava Agricultural

records.title: Dhampur Bio Organics Limited has established a wholly owned subsidiary, DBOL International Food and Beverages Trading FZE, within the Jeb...
records.description: Dhampur Bio Organics Limited has established a wholly owned subsidiary, DBOL International Food and Beverages Trading FZE, within the Jebel Ali Free Zone Authority (JAFZA) in Dubai. This new entity is dedicated to the trading, distribution, and value-added packaging of sugar and other fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), leveraging the strategic logistics advantages of one of the world's largest free zones and its proximity to major shipping lanes. By moving packaging operations closer to end-markets, the institution aims to reduce logistics timelines for customers across the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia while benefiting from duty-free sourcing of materials and streamlined export documentation. This move represents a strategic international expansion intended to enhance supply chain efficiency and explore further opportunities in sugar-based products like confectionery and beverages.
records.institution: Dhampur Bio Organics Limited

records.title: DP World and Al Dahra Holding have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to develop comprehensive supply chain solutions for food and agri...
records.description: DP World and Al Dahra Holding have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to develop comprehensive supply chain solutions for food and agricultural commodities across the GCC and international markets. This strategic partnership aims to address regional reliance on food imports by combining global logistics infrastructure with large-scale agricultural sourcing and procurement. The collaboration will explore joint investments in port infrastructure, cold chain warehousing, and agri-food processing hubs, particularly in Abu Dhabi, while identifying new sourcing corridors across Africa, Europe, and the Americas. By integrating digital traceability systems and optimizing cross-border regulatory processes, the initiative seeks to enhance the resilience and efficiency of the regional food distribution network.
records.institution: DP World and Al Dahra Holding

records.title: Nama Water Services is implementing a comprehensive water sustainability strategy centered on the Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) proj...
records.description: Nama Water Services is implementing a comprehensive water sustainability strategy centered on the Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) project, a strategic initiative designed to bolster national water security and support Oman Vision 2040. By utilizing advanced water injection technology, the institution stores excess desalinated water in underground aquifers during low-demand periods for recovery during emergencies or peak consumption, targeting a storage capacity of up to 30 million cubic meters. This project, currently being piloted in the Sharqiyah Sands basin, aims to reduce operational pressure on desalination plants, lower energy consumption, and ensure a resilient supply for the North and South Al Sharqiyah and Al Dakhiliyah Governorates. Developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and academic partners like Sultan Qaboos University, the initiative represents a shift toward proactive, technology-driven water management and resource efficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in the A’Dhahirah Governorate, in coordination with the Ministry of Agricultur...
records.description: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in the A’Dhahirah Governorate, in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, has supported the expansion of the "Murtafaat Al Najeed" project, the first commercial chick-producing hatchery in the Wilayat of Ibri. The facility has reached an annual production capacity of approximately 700,000 chicks, utilizing modern incubation and hatching technologies to supply local farms across multiple governorates. By providing technical guidance, vaccination programs, and biosecurity oversight, the institution aims to increase national white meat self-sufficiency—which currently stands at 62%—and reduce reliance on imports. This initiative serves as a strategic model for localizing the poultry supply chain and enhancing national food security through integrated production cycles.
records.institution: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources

records.title: The National Center for Research and Development of Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) has successfully conducted a research trial in Al...
records.description: The National Center for Research and Development of Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) has successfully conducted a research trial in Al-Kharj Governorate to evaluate the adaptability of quinoa within arid environmental conditions. The study focused on assessing crop performance against high temperatures, soil salinity, and limited water availability to support crop diversification and national food security. Results identified high-yielding varieties suitable for local cultivation, with the "Golden Afternoon" and "Mint Vanilla" varieties producing approximately 4.3 and 4.0 tons per hectare, respectively. This initiative reflects the institution's commitment to developing modern agricultural technologies that improve production efficiency and ensure the sustainability of natural resources.
records.institution: The National Center for Research and Development of Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

records.title: The National Center for the Prevention and Control of Plant Pests and Animal Diseases (Weqaa) is spearheading a comprehensive transformat...
records.description: The National Center for the Prevention and Control of Plant Pests and Animal Diseases (Weqaa) is spearheading a comprehensive transformation of the agricultural sector through an integrated, surveillance-based biosecurity system. By implementing enhanced farm inspections, rigorous quarantine protocols, and advanced early-detection laboratories, the institution aims to mitigate the economic impact of transboundary pests and protect national food security. These efforts include the development of emergency response frameworks and a shift toward digital transformation in pest management. This proactive approach serves as a strategic investment in public health and economic stability, ensuring a resilient agricultural environment capable of addressing climate-related and biological risks.

records.description: The KEZAD Group, a division of AD Ports Group, has signed a long-term land lease agreement with the Abu Dhabi Refreshment Company to establish a 32,500-square-meter beverage production and distribution facility. With an investment of approximately AED 300 million, the state-of-the-art project is designed to expand the company's regional production capacity and optimize distribution through KEZAD's integrated industrial ecosystem and proximity to Khalifa Port. This initiative aligns with the Abu Dhabi Industrial Strategy, aiming to reinforce the emirate's status as a regional manufacturing hub for fast-moving consumer goods and strengthen downstream supply chains across the UAE. As a franchisee of PepsiCo, the Abu Dhabi Refreshment Company intends for this expansion to enhance its response to evolving consumer demand while supporting national goals for economic diversification and localized production.

records.description: The NRTC Holding Group and DAVA Agricultural have entered into a strategic Memorandum of Understanding to enhance regional agricultural collaboration and food security across the GCC. This partnership focuses on fresh produce sourcing, supply chain optimization, and sustainable trade, leveraging an integrated supply network that handles approximately one million tonnes of produce annually and advanced hydroponic greenhouse technology that achieves significant water savings. The collaboration aligns with regional sustainability goals and seeks to address a market opportunity exceeding billions in value by expanding high-tech agricultural investments and cross-border distribution networks.
records.institution: The NRTC Holding Group and DAVA Agricultural

records.title: The Qassim Region has solidified its role as a critical contributor to Saudi Arabia’s strategic food reserves, with wheat production serv...
records.description: The Qassim Region has solidified its role as a critical contributor to Saudi Arabia’s strategic food reserves, with wheat production serving as a primary pillar of the region's agricultural output. Aligned with Saudi Vision 2030, the local sector has integrated advanced farming and storage technologies—including high-yield, drought-resistant seed varieties and modern irrigation systems—to enhance self-sufficiency while addressing challenges like water scarcity and climate change. The annual harvest, which typically occurs between April and June, is a coordinated effort between government agencies and local farmers to supply the flour and bread industries, thereby supporting rural development and national food security. Through the expansion of advanced silos and proactive water management, the region continues to model a resilient and sustainable agricultural future for the Kingdom.
records.institution: The Qassim Region

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) marked the International Day of Plant Health 2026 by reaffirming its commitm...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) marked the International Day of Plant Health 2026 by reaffirming its commitment to "Plant Biosecurity for Food Security." Central to this mission is an integrated system aimed at combating agricultural pests, specifically focusing on the protection of date palms through the "One Health" approach and advanced early warning systems. Between 2019 and 2025, the authority deployed over 124,000 pheromone traps across 21,000 farms, capturing more than 11 million red palm weevils and treating 300,000 infected trees. Additionally, ADAFSA has integrated circular economy principles by recycling over 2,500 tonnes of palm waste into organic fertilizers while providing extensive technical training to farm owners on Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and sustainable agricultural practices. These efforts align with the UAE’s broader vision to strengthen food security and build a resilient agricultural sector capable of addressing evolving biological and climatic challenges.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The Dhofar Governorate, in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR), has launched four new in...
records.description: The Dhofar Governorate, in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR), has launched four new investment opportunities for water purification and bottling plants in the wilayats of Salalah, Taqah, Muqshin, and the Shalim and Hallaniyat Islands. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to expand the Sultanate’s water industry, which already produces 7.7 million liters of bottled water daily across 81 operational plants. To manage this growth, the MAFWR has introduced updated technical regulations and a streamlined application process via the Tatwir platform to ensure all new projects meet national health and safety standards. By encouraging private sector participation and ensuring a wide geographical distribution of facilities, the government aims to meet the rising demand for clean drinking water driven by population growth and regional development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.description: The Wali of Qurayat and local authorities in Oman are expanding the region's agricultural footprint during a highly successful mango season characterized by strong consumer demand and public participation. The project features 350 hectares of climate-controlled glass greenhouses, a 65-hectare solar energy park, and a large-scale plantation program of one million trees, alongside integrated fish production and eco-tourism facilities. Currently contributing nearly 14% of the Kingdom's greenhouse production, the company aims to scale its daily output to 1,000 tons by 2030 through advanced hydroponics and water-saving technologies. records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) has implemented a comprehensive agricultural project in the eastern Aleppo countryside to support the Syrian wheat production chain and enhance local food security. The initiative directly benefited 2,750 families by rehabilitating critical irrigation and drainage networks, installing solar-powered water pumping units, and supporting the propagation of high-quality Syrian wheat seeds through the provision of sifting and sterilization equipment. Additionally, the project rehabilitated a central seed warehouse and three agricultural extension centers, providing farmers with technical training in modern irrigation and crop management to improve long-term productivity and resilience.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief)

records.title: The Najran Region has established itself as a premier agricultural hub in Saudi Arabia, leveraging its fertile soil, moderate climate, an...
records.description: The Najran Region has established itself as a premier agricultural hub in Saudi Arabia, leveraging its fertile soil, moderate climate, and abundant water resources to bolster national food security. Local farmers have transitioned toward high-tech, sustainable practices—including vertical farming and greenhouses—to produce organic, pesticide-free crops such as citrus fruits, grapes, wheat, and the region's signature Al-Bayadh dates. By adopting these water-efficient and innovative methods, Najran’s agricultural sector continues to supply fresh produce to local markets while reducing environmental impact. These advancements are further reinforced by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, which provides specialized workshops and training to enhance the professional skills of farmers and stimulate regional economic growth.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Al Ain Farms Group and NRTC Group, both subsidiaries of Ghitha, have launched a joint venture called Al Ain Taaza to establish a domestic...
records.description: Al Ain Farms Group and NRTC Group, both subsidiaries of Ghitha, have launched a joint venture called Al Ain Taaza to establish a domestic ultra-fresh juice operation in the UAE. Targeting a 30% share of the country's AED 500 million fresh juice market within five years, the partnership leverages NRTC’s end-to-end cold-chain logistics and sourcing expertise alongside Al Ain Farms’ massive distribution network of 23,000 daily sales points. The venture aims to disrupt the market by delivering juice from harvest to shelf within 48 hours—significantly faster than the 4–6 week lead times of international brands—while reducing costs by an estimated 15–20% through vertical integration. Set to launch in Q3 2026 with 15 flavors, the initiative is designed to bolster national food security by reducing reliance on imported finished goods and insulating the local market from global supply chain volatility.
records.institution: Al Ain Farms Group and NRTC Group

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman, represented by its Minister during a session with the Shura Council,...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman, represented by its Minister during a session with the Shura Council, reviewed the robust performance of the food and water sectors under the Tenth Five-Year Development Plan and outlined strategies for the upcoming Eleventh Plan. Significant achievements include a growth in production to 5.6 million tonnes, a 7.9% increase in the sectors' contribution to GDP, and reaching a food self-sufficiency rate of 67.3%, with fish and dates exceeding 100%. The report highlighted extensive infrastructure development, including 85 groundwater recharge dams and a water monitoring network of over 3,400 stations, alongside OMR 1.87 billion in new investment contracts. With food industry exports reaching OMR 753 million and the creation of over 51,000 jobs for Omani workers, the Ministry is now prioritizing digital governance, technological transformation, and expanded private sector partnerships to further enhance national food security and sustainable resource management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef) has completed five development projects in the honey sector valued at...
records.description: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef) has completed five development projects in the honey sector valued at over SAR 38.2 million across Saudi Arabia. These initiatives, aligned with Saudi Vision 2030, aim to achieve honey self-sufficiency and bolster food security by supporting smallholder producers and modernizing value chains. The program focuses on empowering beekeepers through technical training, the introduction of modern breeding and pollination technologies, and the expansion of marketing opportunities. By reducing reliance on traditional methods and imports, these projects are designed to improve biodiversity, enhance crop pollination, and create sustainable local jobs within the apiculture industry.
records.institution: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef)

records.title: The Qassim Region has solidified its reputation as Saudi Arabia’s "food basket" following an exceptional harvest of seasonal peaches, wit...
records.description: The Qassim Region has solidified its reputation as Saudi Arabia’s "food basket" following an exceptional harvest of seasonal peaches, with individual trees yielding between 30 and 50 kilograms. This success follows a pilot phase where 12 varieties were tested, resulting in the identification of a highly successful, water-efficient cultivar well-suited to the region's deciduous growth patterns. The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has played a pivotal role in this expansion by providing technical support, promoting modern irrigation technologies, and conducting field visits to ensure agricultural sustainability. By focusing on water conservation and meticulous tree management—including specific pruning and fertilization—the initiative aims to bolster national food security while stimulating the local economy through seasonal employment in harvesting and marketing.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) and Borouge have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the supply of approximately 3,500 tonnes of Hig...
records.description: Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) and Borouge have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the supply of approximately 3,500 tonnes of High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) resin annually, representing a 600% increase in supply. Signed during the Make it in the Emirates forum, the agreement supports AAFG’s vertical integration strategy, particularly its in-house blow molding and cap production operations. This partnership aligns with the UAE’s Operation 300bn industrial strategy by prioritizing local manufacturing, enhancing supply chain resilience, and reducing reliance on imports to bolster national food security.
records.institution: Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) and Borouge

records.title: The Tatweer platform has launched 43 new investment opportunities in the North A’Sharqiyah Governorate, specifically affiliated with the...
records.description: The Tatweer platform has launched 43 new investment opportunities in the North A’Sharqiyah Governorate, specifically affiliated with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources. These opportunities are designed to provide a gateway for investors and entrepreneurs to develop high-quality agricultural and water-related projects with strong economic feasibility. By opening these channels, the platform aims to stimulate local economic growth and encourage private sector participation in the governorate's development.
records.institution: The Tatwee

records.title: The Al-Baha Region is leveraging its diverse terrain and fertile soil to strengthen its position as a vital agricultural hub within Saudi...
records.description: The Al-Baha Region is leveraging its diverse terrain and fertile soil to strengthen its position as a vital agricultural hub within Saudi Arabia. The region produces a wide variety of high-demand crops, including grapes, pomegranates, mangoes, and coffee, with its hundreds of thousands of pomegranate trees yielding thousands of tons annually. To support this production and enhance food security, the region has established 19 agricultural cities that focus on economic development, resource preservation, and the cultivation of promising seasonal fruits across both mountainous and coastal sectors.
records.institution: The Al-Baha Region

records.title: The International Affairs Office at the UAE Presidential Court, in partnership with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and supported by the...
records.description: The International Affairs Office at the UAE Presidential Court, in partnership with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and supported by the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific (JFPR), has launched a $1.5 million technical cooperation agreement to scale agricultural innovations across eight countries in Asia and the Pacific. Operationalized through the Agricultural Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale)—an initiative backed by the UAE and the Gates Foundation—the partnership focuses on integrating AI-powered weather forecasting, digital advisory services, and livestock productivity tools into national programs. This collaboration, which also involves the Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) and other global partners, aims to strengthen global food security by reaching farmers in Bangladesh, Indonesia, Nepal, the Philippines, Vietnam, Pakistan, Thailand, and the Maldives.
records.institution: The International Affairs Office at the UAE Presidential Court

records.title: The Joint Supreme Committee for Cooperation between Qatar and the United Arab Emirates concluded its seventh session in Abu Dhabi, markin...
records.description: The Joint Supreme Committee for Cooperation between Qatar and the United Arab Emirates concluded its seventh session in Abu Dhabi, marking a transition toward a more integrated phase of bilateral partnership. Co-chaired by the respective Ministers of Foreign Affairs, the session resulted in the signing of an Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement and several memoranda of understanding focused on agriculture, food security, and municipal cooperation. Key discussions centered on economic diversification through high-quality public-private partnerships, cooperation in future technologies like artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, and the enhancement of logistical connectivity between maritime and air transport hubs. The committee emphasized building resilient supply chains and food security systems to address global challenges, while also coordinating on health, education, and humanitarian efforts.
records.institution: The Joint Supreme Committee for Cooperation
