records.title: Date production in Madinah increased by 31% in 2024, exceeding 343,000 tons, according to the Madinah branch of the Ministry of Environme...
records.description: Date production in Madinah increased by 31% in 2024, exceeding 343,000 tons, according to the Madinah branch of the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. This growth has contributed to greater self-sufficiency and strengthened Saudi Arabia's food security strategies. Madinah hosted several date-related events in 2024, showcasing various date varieties from eight million date palms and highlighting local agricultural production and date-related industries.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The UAE remains the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over the past five years, according to Pakistan's...
records.description: The UAE remains the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over the past five years, according to Pakistan's Ministry of Commerce. Total Pakistani mango exports over this period reached $632.003 million. Other significant markets include the UK, Kazakhstan, Oman, Afghanistan, and Saudi Arabia. The report highlights the unique flavor and quality of Pakistani mangoes and their contribution to Pakistan's economy. Demand in the UAE is driven by its diverse population, and projections indicate increasing mango production in the UAE itself.
records.institution: The UAE Government

records.title: Blueberry trees have been successfully grown in Jabal Al Akhdar, Oman, by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources.
records.description: Blueberry trees have been successfully grown in Jabal Al Akhdar, Oman, by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources. This initiative aims to invest in economically valuable crops suited to cold mountainous regions. The trees are grown on 1,000 sq. meters, with each plant producing 3-5 kg of fruit. The project includes 500 Southern Highbush blueberry plants of four different species from Georgia, chosen for their requirement of 200-400 chill hours (temperatures below 7°C), which Jabal Al Akhdar's climate provides. The harvest season is from May to the end of June.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Almarai, a Middle East food producer, plans to increase its poultry output by 35% this year as part of its multi-billion-dollar expansion.
records.description: Almarai, a Middle East food producer, plans to increase its poultry output by 35% this year as part of its multi-billion-dollar expansion. The company reported increased fourth-quarter and annual profits. They plan to increase poultry capacity from 250 million to 300 million birds and boost output from 200 million to 270 million per year, targeting 450 million processed birds by 2027. Almarai holds a 35% market share in Saudi Arabia's poultry sector, with 66% of its revenue coming from the Kingdom. The company launched a $4.8 billion five-year investment strategy last year to improve growth and financial performance.
records.institution: Almarai

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Crown Farms, a UAE-based organic farm management company, has launched a new line of organic fertilizers to support sustainable agricultu...
records.description: Crown Farms, a UAE-based organic farm management company, has launched a new line of organic fertilizers to support sustainable agriculture and organic farming in the UAE. The fertilizers are designed to improve soil fertility, water retention, and nutrient absorption, promoting long-term sustainable crop growth. They contain essential nutrients and adhere to UAE organic standards, being free from harmful chemicals. This protects the environment and reduces reliance on synthetic fertilizers. The fertilizers are certified for use in organic farming and promote strong root growth.
records.institution: Crown Farms

records.title: The UAE is the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over five years, according to a Ministry of Commerce re...
records.description: The UAE is the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over five years, according to a Ministry of Commerce report. Other significant markets include the UK ($131.96 million), Kazakhstan ($93.86 million), Oman ($39.88 million), Afghanistan ($35.98 million), and Saudi Arabia ($29.61 million). Total Pakistani mango exports over the past five years reached $632.003 million. Pakistan's citrus exports for the current fiscal year have reached $30.9 million. The global demand for Pakistani mangoes, due to their unique flavor and quality, boosts the country's agricultural exports. The government continues to work on improving market access and expanding export opportunities to strengthen international trade and economic growth.
records.institution: The Ministry of Commerce

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI), in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI), in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD), has launched the Geospatial Data Platform for Agriculture and Water Resources. This platform aims to enhance agricultural sustainability and water resource management. By 2027, it aims to reduce groundwater use in agriculture by 2% and increase the use of unconventional water resources by 8-13%, while also improving water productivity and contributing to food security through improved local produce and innovative agricultural strategies. The platform provides farmers and government entities with accessible geospatial maps and comprehensive agricultural and water data for informed decision-making and improved water demand management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI)

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: A meeting at Ibb University, chaired by the university president, discussed ways to improve the educational process at the College of Agr...
records.description: A meeting at Ibb University, chaired by the university president, discussed ways to improve the educational process at the College of Agriculture and Food Sciences, both theoretically and practically. Attendees included university vice presidents and the college dean. The meeting reviewed the outcomes of a previous meeting with the Deputy Minister of Agriculture and the head of the Agricultural Research and Extension Authority to explore joint cooperation in developing the educational process. The focus is on aligning programs and courses with applied aspects to improve plant and animal production and food industries. The university president emphasized teamwork and utilizing available resources to enhance theoretical and practical performance according to quality standards.
records.institution: Ibb University

records.title: A recent desert locust survey and control campaign in Oman has found the situation to be stable and under observation.
records.description: A recent desert locust survey and control campaign in Oman has found the situation to be stable and under observation. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources monitored locust propagation, breeding locations, and environmental conditions. Monitoring in Al Wusta, North A’Sharqiyah, and South A’Sharqiyah governorates revealed "individual cases" and "transitional cases" of desert locusts, prompting a successful early intervention campaign. The Ministry emphasizes regular monitoring to detect and address any developments. Desert locusts pose a significant threat to food security and cause substantial economic damage, with a small swarm capable of consuming enough food for 35,000 people daily. Each adult locust can consume its own weight in food each day.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has begun work on a pilot marine fish farming project using Recirculating A...
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has begun work on a pilot marine fish farming project using Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) technology, a first for the country. The 8-tonne capacity project, focused on Sea Bream, is being built in Al Musannah with funding from the Ministry’s Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund. RAS technology reuses water through filtration and treatment, minimizing water and space requirements. The pilot aims to introduce new sustainable aquaculture technology, support diverse fish species cultivation, provide training for the fishing community and entrepreneurs, and encourage the growth of SME-sized fish farms, creating jobs for young Omanis.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia's date exports have significantly increased, reaching 1.5 billion tonnes in 2024, up from 579 million tonnes in 2016.
records.description: Saudi Arabia's date exports have significantly increased, reaching 1.5 billion tonnes in 2024, up from 579 million tonnes in 2016. The Kingdom has over 123,000 agricultural holdings producing around 300 date varieties from more than 37 million palm trees, yielding over three million tonnes of dates annually. Over 137 factories specialize in date products. The Al-Qassim region has the highest concentration of palm trees, followed by Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province. The Kingdom has achieved a 124% self-sufficiency rate for dates, with annual production exceeding 1.6 million tonnes.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The second Al Dhaid Agriculture Exhibition is set to begin at Expo Al Dhaid.
records.description: The second Al Dhaid Agriculture Exhibition is set to begin at Expo Al Dhaid. Organized by Expo Centre Sharjah with support from the Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry and in cooperation with the Department of Agriculture and Livestock, the event brings together key players in the agricultural and farming sectors. This year's edition has expanded to include over 40 specialized companies and stakeholders across the agricultural supply chain. The exhibition will cover various aspects of agriculture, including aquaculture, ornamental plants, farm equipment, financial services, pesticides, beekeeping, and food processing. It will showcase advanced agricultural technologies and solutions, with a focus on wheat and grain cultivation in the Gulf region, hydroponic and vertical farming, smart irrigation, modern horticulture, and eco-friendly organic pesticides and fertilizers.
records.institution: Expo Centre Sharjah, The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Sales at the first Al-Kharj Festival of Saudi Dates and Coffee have surpassed SR10 million ($2.6 million).
records.description: Sales at the first Al-Kharj Festival of Saudi Dates and Coffee have surpassed SR10 million ($2.6 million). The 10-day festival, featuring 30 date companies and shops offering over 26 varieties, and 20 coffee shops selling 2-5 tonnes of coffee daily, attracted visitors with special offers, the approaching Ramadan, and access to specialized markets. Supported by government entities, the festival highlighted the cultural importance of dates and coffee in Saudi Arabia, recognizing dates as a key agricultural export and coffee as a symbol of national identity. The event also provided a platform for SMEs and specialized companies to showcase their products and aimed to enhance Al-Kharj’s reputation.
records.institution: The Saudi Government

records.title: The UAE launched the largest phase of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3 to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, coinciding with a newly announce...
records.description: The UAE launched the largest phase of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3 to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, coinciding with a newly announced truce. A 20-truck convoy carrying over 200 tonnes of food, winter clothing, and essential items was dispatched. This phase represents the largest effort within the operation, which has already delivered approximately 29,784 tonnes of aid via 156 convoys. The operation utilizes airlifts, ships, and trucks to transport aid from Egypt to Gaza and includes a field hospital in Gaza, a floating hospital in Arish, transfer of critical cases to UAE hospitals, water projects like desalination plants in Rafah, and airdropped aid to inaccessible areas in northern Gaza.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: A "Ramadan Vegetables from Your Home" campaign, now in its fourth season and themed "Together towards self-sufficiency," has been launched.
records.description: A "Ramadan Vegetables from Your Home" campaign, now in its fourth season and themed "Together towards self-sufficiency," has been launched. Implemented by the Women's Development Department and the Women's Authority in cooperation with agricultural funding and support organizations, the campaign promotes home farming, supports food security, and aims to provide additional income for Yemeni families. Officials praised the campaign's efforts to promote self-reliance and local production as a way to address economic challenges and strengthen national sovereignty. Plans were also announced to establish a large shopping center for products from productive families and small projects to further support their development and reduce unemployment.
records.institution: The Women's Development Department and the Women's Authority

records.title: A rainwater harvesting project, funded at approximately 180 million riyals, has been inaugurated in the Sana'a basin.
records.description: A rainwater harvesting project, funded at approximately 180 million riyals, has been inaugurated in the Sana'a basin. The project, supervised by the Water Resources Authority, aims to replenish groundwater levels and support the agricultural sector by providing irrigation water. The first stage of the project involved creating a storage area with a capacity of over 135,000 cubic meters. The second stage will focus on creating entrances, exits, and sedimentation basins. This initiative aligns with directives to enhance water resource sustainability. Officials emphasized the importance of expanding such projects to preserve water resources and support agricultural development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fish Resources and Water Resources

records.title: In Tarim, Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in partnership with local authorities and with funding from KOICA, h...
records.description: In Tarim, Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in partnership with local authorities and with funding from KOICA, has inaugurated two infrastructure projects to address water-related issues. A surface bridge with a gabion weir in Dammon and protective gabion walls in Al-Sabir aim to mitigate flood risks, improve agriculture, and promote peace. The projects are part of the "Water for Peace" initiative launched in late 2023 to address water scarcity and environmental degradation exacerbated by climate change. The Dammon project slows floodwaters, protects farmland, recharges groundwater, and ensures safe passage during floods. The Al-Sabir project's gabion walls protect farms, distribute water more evenly, and reduce disputes among farmers.
records.institution: The International Organization for Migration (IOM)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture and the 17th Agriculture Ministers Conference in Berlin, focusing on "Farm...
records.description: Oman participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture and the 17th Agriculture Ministers Conference in Berlin, focusing on "Farming a Sustainable Bioeconomy." Oman highlighted its investment program for food security (2021-2024), involving 314 projects in agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and water, with a total investment of RO 1.266 billion. These projects aim to increase productivity, reduce imports, create added value, and provide jobs, aligning with Oman Vision 2040. Oman emphasized the importance of balancing food needs with environmental preservation and enhancing the bioeconomy through sustainable use of biological resources.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has made significant progress in its water sector projects, adhering to the...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has made significant progress in its water sector projects, adhering to the National Water Strategy. The Kingdom is the world's leading desalination producer, with a 4.19 million cubic meter annual capacity and operates an extensive 14,210 km water transmission network managing 19.42 million cubic meters daily. Through this strategy, the Kingdom has achieved multiple Guinness World Records for its water storage and production facilities, including the largest drinking water tank and evaporation desalination unit, and the world's largest mobile desalination plant. The Kingdom also boasts the lowest energy consumption in desalination plants. In 2024, the National Water Company (NWC) completed numerous water and sanitation projects, adding significant capacity and infrastructure.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Dubai Municipality launched the second Hatta Farming Festival as part of the ‘Dubai Farms’ program, under the Hatta Winter initiative.
records.description: Dubai Municipality launched the second Hatta Farming Festival as part of the ‘Dubai Farms’ program, under the Hatta Winter initiative. The festival showcases local agricultural products and services from 25 Emirati farmers and companies, aiming to support the UAE's agricultural market and promote Hatta as an agri-tourism destination. The event aligns with Dubai's vision for sustainable agriculture, the Hatta Comprehensive Development Plan, and the ‘Grow UAE’ program. The festival includes exhibitions, workshops, dialogue sessions with experts, livestock auctions, and awards for outstanding farmers. It also provides an agricultural extension platform with free guidance and services like testing and veterinary consultations.
records.institution: Dubai Municipality

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has announced preferred suppliers and contractors for a gigawatt-scale solar and battery st...
records.description: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has announced preferred suppliers and contractors for a gigawatt-scale solar and battery storage project in Abu Dhabi. Developed in collaboration with EWEC, the project will provide up to 1 GW of baseload power 24/7. Larsen & Toubro (India) and POWERCHINA (China) are the preferred EPC contractors. JA Solar, Jinko Solar (both China), and CATL (China) have been selected as preferred suppliers for PV modules and battery storage. The project will include a 5.2 GW (DC) solar PV plant and a 19 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS), making it the world's largest of its kind. Jinko Solar and JA Solar will each supply 2.6 GW of PV modules using TopCon technology, and CATL will supply its TENER technology for the BESS.
records.institution: Masdar

records.title: Saudi Arabian private sector leaders and Nigerian officials have agreed on a joint strategy to attract Saudi investment to Nigeria.
records.description: Saudi Arabian private sector leaders and Nigerian officials have agreed on a joint strategy to attract Saudi investment to Nigeria. The focus will be on mining, agriculture, food products, banking services, and financial technologies. During a meeting between representatives from both countries, the President of the Federation of Saudi Chambers emphasized the importance of the Saudi-Nigerian Business Council and Saudi Arabia's interest in collaborating on agriculture, livestock, and mining. Nigerian officials encouraged Saudi investment in their mining sector, highlighting untapped mineral wealth and investment incentives like tax exemptions and duty-free trade.
records.institution: The Saudi Government

records.title: Silal and Borouge have strengthened their partnership to promote sustainable agriculture and food security in the UAE.
records.description: Silal and Borouge have strengthened their partnership to promote sustainable agriculture and food security in the UAE. This collaboration combines Silal's expertise in sustainable farming practices, including digital farming solutions and farmer capacity building, with Borouge's innovative polyolefin solutions. The partnership will focus on research and development, implementing sustainable farming practices, and developing solutions for regional agricultural challenges. A key goal is enhancing UAE food security by increasing local food production and reducing reliance on imports.
records.institution: Silal and Borouge

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, launched the ‘100,000 See...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, launched the ‘100,000 Seedlings’ initiative, distributing seedlings to public schools nationwide. This initiative aims to educate students about the importance of agriculture and greening, aligning with the ‘Plant the Emirates’ National Programme and its ‘National Agriculture Centre.’ The initiative emphasizes sustainable agriculture, community participation, and national food security. The first phase involves distributing 15,000 seedlings, provided by the Khalifa Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology and Jenaan Investment Company, with the Environment Friends Society engaging volunteers in planting.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: A four-day training course for field school facilitators, funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and In...
records.description: A four-day training course for field school facilitators, funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing, concluded in Dhamar. The course equipped 36 agricultural guides with skills to facilitate field school activities across the province, focusing on expanding grain, legume, and livestock cultivation. The importance of community involvement in agricultural cooperatives was also emphasized. Participants gained practical skills in agricultural decision-making, guidance principles, and field school facilitation methods.
records.institution: The Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing in Dhamar

records.title: Bahrain and Oman have signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during a state visit.
records.description: Bahrain and Oman have signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during a state visit. One MoU focuses on municipal work, aiming to exchange information, expertise, and research in this field. The second MoU, concerning agriculture, livestock production, and food security, aims to support and develop these sectors through enhanced cooperation. This includes promoting sustainable farming practices, developing advanced agricultural techniques, improving agricultural infrastructure, and encouraging collaboration in agricultural product processing. The MoU also covers cooperation in tree planting (especially mangroves), joint exhibitions, and the use of artificial intelligence in marketing agricultural products and honey. In animal production, the MoU focuses on improving techniques, animal health, training, disease control, and information exchange.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: The UAE and Kenya have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to strengthen their economic ties.
records.description: The UAE and Kenya have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to strengthen their economic ties. The agreement aims to boost trade and investment, improve supply chains, and expand market access across key sectors such as agriculture, retail, healthcare, financial services, technology, and agriculture. This builds on existing trade growth between the two nations and seeks to further accelerate investment in areas like ICT, banking, infrastructure, and renewable energy, aligning with the UAE's broader economic growth objectives.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: The Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA), in partnership with Emirates Nature-WWF, the UAE Ministry of Climate Change...
records.description: The Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA), in partnership with Emirates Nature-WWF, the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, and Bee’ah, has completed a mangrove planting program in the AlQurm Protected Area, Khor Kalba. Over two weeks, 11,600 mangrove seedlings were planted. This initiative supports the UAE's goal of planting 100 million mangrove trees by 2030 and contributes to the Net Zero by 2050 Strategy. The program aims to enhance environmental sustainability, promote collaboration, and address climate change. It is part of a larger effort to expand mangrove coverage in Sharjah, with ongoing monitoring to ensure sustainability.
records.institution: The Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The World Future Energy Summit 2025 (WFES 2025), hosted by Masdar, has commenced in Abu Dhabi as part of Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (A...
records.description: The World Future Energy Summit 2025 (WFES 2025), hosted by Masdar, has commenced in Abu Dhabi as part of Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (ADSW). This three-day summit gathers global leaders, including heads of state, ministers, and industry experts, to discuss energy transition and circular economies, aiming to unlock a potential $10 trillion economic transformation. The event features numerous sessions and speakers focusing on topics like AI's role in creating a sustainable future, as well as the impact of renewable energy and climate technologies. Expected to draw over 30,000 attendees, the summit showcases innovations in renewable energy, AI, circular economy, green financing, and sustainable cities, with over 400 exhibitors presenting solutions in various sectors.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company – Masdar

records.title: Qatar eyes 55% self-sufficiency in vegetables by 2030
records.description: Qatar's National Food Security Strategy 2030 aims to achieve 55% self-sufficiency in vegetable production, a 50% increase in agricultural land productivity, 30% self-sufficiency in red meat, 80% in fish, and 100% in dairy and fresh chicken. Significant progress has been made in recent years, with over 950 productive farms operating and a doubling of organic farming land last year. In 2024, over 26 million kg of local vegetables were marketed, and livestock numbers reached 1.4 million. The new strategy, building on the previous 2018-2023 strategy, includes 17 initiatives focused on promoting healthy consumption, ensuring food safety and quality, promoting sustainability and climate change adaptation, and building strong partnerships. It aligns with Qatar National Vision 2030 to develop a resilient and adaptable food system.
records.institution: Ministry of Municipality and Environment

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Saudi Arabia is bolstering its food security strategy with a new trout farming project developed by KACST and King Abdulaziz University,...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is bolstering its food security strategy with a new trout farming project developed by KACST and King Abdulaziz University, supported by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. This initiative introduces a nutrient-rich fish species suitable for diverse environments, aiming to meet growing domestic seafood demand and reduce supply chain vulnerabilities. Aligned with Vision 2030's goal of 600,000 tonnes of annual fish production, the project uses a water-efficient recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) to enhance fish health and quality. Trout have been successfully farmed to commercial size, prompting private sector adoption of RAS technology in several regions. The focus on trout and other cold-water fish addresses the demand for protein-rich, omega-3-rich food sources.
records.institution: King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST) and King Abdulaziz University

records.title: the Saudi Reef program has provided SAR 2.4 billion in financial support to rural communities in Saudi Arabia.
records.description: the Saudi Reef program has provided SAR 2.4 billion in financial support to rural communities in Saudi Arabia. This program supports small farmers and rural producers, improving livelihoods and promoting sustainable rural development in line with Saudi Vision 2030. Over 77,400 beneficiaries have received support, with a focus on empowering rural women, who make up over 57,400 of the recipients. Saudi Reef is a key national initiative aimed at transforming rural communities and enhancing their economic and environmental sustainability.
records.institution: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef)

records.title: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), in collaboration with 14 government agencies, has enhanced the "Saudi Authorized Econ...
records.description: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), in collaboration with 14 government agencies, has enhanced the "Saudi Authorized Economic Operator Program." This program offers administrative, procedural, and financial benefits to importers, exporters, and logistics service providers (including customs brokers and shipping agents). The program aims to empower the logistics sector, facilitate trade, streamline procedures, boost competitiveness, enhance supply chain efficiency, and improve access to global markets. Participating entities include various ministries and authorities related to key economic & Agriculture sectors. Since its launch, over 550 businesses have joined the program, which is globally recognized and approved in 80 countries, aligning with World Customs Organization standards. Interested parties can find more information on ZATCA's website.
records.institution: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA)

records.title: An organic honey products factory and laboratory has been approved for the central region of Sharjah, aiming to contribute significantly...
records.description: An organic honey products factory and laboratory has been approved for the central region of Sharjah, aiming to contribute significantly to the production and innovation of honey-based products. The facility will specialize in producing high-quality honey alongside pharmaceutical and cosmetic materials derived from honey, supporting both local and international markets. In its initial phase, the factory plans to achieve a production capacity of 120 tonnes of honey annually, emphasizing the use of organic methods to ensure sustainability and product quality. This project is expected to enhance the region's reputation as a hub for organic and health-focused products, aligning with broader agricultural and economic development goals.
records.institution: The Department of Agriculture and Livestock

records.title: Farm and land owners in Sharjah have been warned against illegally renting out their plots, a practice common during the winter season.
records.description: Farm and land owners in Sharjah have been warned against illegally renting out their plots, a practice common during the winter season. Sharjah Municipality emphasizes that these lands are allocated for authorized activities like agriculture and livestock rearing to support citizens economically, contribute to self-sufficiency, and strengthen food security. Using the land for other purposes is harmful to neighboring farms and tenants, potentially violating tenant rights. The Farm Violations Removal Committee urged owners to comply with permitted land use regulations.
records.institution: Sharjah Municipality

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) held its first Agricultural and Veterinary Quarantine Forum to discuss prev...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) held its first Agricultural and Veterinary Quarantine Forum to discuss preventing transboundary animal diseases and agricultural pests from entering the country. The forum aimed to increase cooperation between government entities and the private sector, aligning with the National Food Security Strategy 2051. Discussions focused on leveraging global best practices, updating legislation, incorporating advanced technology, and enhancing the capabilities of UAE nationals in quarantine procedures. Presentations were given by experts from Australia, UAE University, and the University of Al Dhaid, covering topics such as biosecurity best practices, transboundary animal diseases, and challenges facing agricultural quarantine in the GCC.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: A four-day training course for field school facilitators has begun in Dhamar province.
records.description: A four-day training course for field school facilitators has begun in Dhamar province. Organized by the agriculture sector and funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing, the course aims to train 36 agricultural guides to facilitate field schools within the "Implementing Field Schools in the Directorates" program. The training focuses on equipping participants with the skills to conduct effective guidance sessions and train field school members in grain, legume, and livestock cultivation. The course emphasizes analyzing agricultural problems and developing effective solutions.
records.institution: Dhamar Governorate

records.title: The first phase of a shrimp factory rehabilitation project has been inaugurated in Hodeida city.
records.description: The first phase of a shrimp factory rehabilitation project has been inaugurated in Hodeida city. Funded by the Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing Unit, the project included rehabilitating the factory hangar, providing new equipment, and creating a modern production environment. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the project's importance for developing the fisheries sector, increasing fish exports, and improving fishermen's livelihoods. The Hodeida governor highlighted its contribution to food security and local self-sufficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The millet harvest has begun in Al-Munirah District, Hodeidah Governorate, as part of a project to cultivate hard lands and sand dunes.
records.description: The millet harvest has begun in Al-Munirah District, Hodeidah Governorate, as part of a project to cultivate hard lands and sand dunes. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the importance of expanding cultivation in these areas, noting that over 100,000 acres were planted with millet. He stressed that this season's harvest will significantly contribute to self-sufficiency and reduce imports, urging consumers to prioritize local millet. The Minister framed the harvest as a sign of Yemen's progress towards self-sufficiency. The Governor of Hodeidah highlighted the region's success in producing large quantities of grain, particularly millet.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Fish production has significantly increased along the Aseer region's coast, generating substantial revenue.
records.description: Fish production has significantly increased along the Aseer region's coast, generating substantial revenue. This growth is attributed to government initiatives aimed at supporting the fishing industry. Further production increases are planned within the next few years. Support is provided to both commercial and independent fishermen, including the distribution of new boats and a mentorship program connecting experienced fishermen with younger generations. The region recently hosted a fish and marine heritage festival showcasing local seafood, businesses, and cultural activities. Aseer's coastline is a diverse marine environment.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: KSrelief, the humanitarian arm of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has provided substantial aid to earthquake-affected individuals in norther...
records.description: KSrelief, the humanitarian arm of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has provided substantial aid to earthquake-affected individuals in northern Syria. In the town of Jindires, located in the Aleppo Governorate, the center distributed 1,476 food baskets and an equal number of health kits. This distribution directly benefited 8,856 individuals and constitutes the second phase of a larger project focused on delivering essential food and health resources to those impacted by the earthquake.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: A technical team in Ibb province has begun a survey and evaluation of water resources and agricultural lands in the Maitam Basin area.
records.description: A technical team in Ibb province has begun a survey and evaluation of water resources and agricultural lands in the Maitam Basin area. The survey, involving the General Authority for Water Resources, the Local Corporation for Water and Sanitation, Agricultural Sector Offices, and the Geological Survey Authority, aims to assess agricultural land and water needs, study the current water situation, and address challenges like the use of unsuitable irrigation water, particularly sewage water. Officials stressed the importance of preventing sewage water use due to its harmful effects and affirmed that measures will be taken to stop this practice.
records.institution: The General Authority for Water Resources

records.title: Hafr Al Batin, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, has announced a SAR9 billion ($2.4 billion) plan to develop the Middle East's largest...
records.description: Hafr Al Batin, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, has announced a SAR9 billion ($2.4 billion) plan to develop the Middle East's largest "livestock city." This project aims to supply 30% of Saudi Arabia's red meat demand and will include livestock facilities, feed factories, a veterinary hospital, and meat processing plants. Powered by renewable energy (solar panels producing 15 billion kilowatt-hours annually), the city is projected to produce 140,000 liters of milk daily, require 100 tonnes of feed per hour, and generate 1.5 million square meters of leather annually.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is preparing to launch "Tabseet," an e-services platform and portal, along wit...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is preparing to launch "Tabseet," an e-services platform and portal, along with a new official website. The project aims to simplify and expedite services for farmers, fishermen, exporters, and other beneficiaries. The first phase of "Tabseet" will offer 50 services, with plans to expand to 250 services across various ministry sectors. The project emphasizes automation and service facilitation through governorate offices. Several ministries and institutions are collaborating on the project, and the launch will coincide with the launch of the ministry's unified website and a service guide.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Commercial Bank International (CBI), a UAE bank, has invested in Boomitra, a carbon project developer and Earthshot Prize winner, to prom...
records.description: Commercial Bank International (CBI), a UAE bank, has invested in Boomitra, a carbon project developer and Earthshot Prize winner, to promote regenerative agriculture in the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. Boomitra uses AI and satellite data to measure soil carbon sequestration, improving soil health and crop yields while generating carbon credits for farmers. CBI's investment reflects its commitment to sustainability and aligns with the UAE's vision for sustainable agriculture. This partnership aims to address issues like land degradation, prevalent in the Middle East and North Africa, by using technology to restore soil health and promote sustainable farming practices.
records.institution: Commercial Bank International (CBI)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) has launched a tender for a 1.5-GW greenfield solar power project in Abu Dhabi's Al Zarraf...
records.description: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) has launched a tender for a 1.5-GW greenfield solar power project in Abu Dhabi's Al Zarraf area. Following a pre-qualification stage, 16 companies are now invited to submit proposals by the second quarter of 2025. The winning bidder will own up to 40% of the project, with the Abu Dhabi government holding the remaining equity. The selected developer will be responsible for all aspects of the project, including development, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance, and will sign a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with EWEC.
records.institution: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC)

records.title: The "Buthoor Al Bahrain" (Seeds of Bahrain) campaign, a three-month initiative promoting green spaces and supporting Bahrain's national a...
records.description: The "Buthoor Al Bahrain" (Seeds of Bahrain) campaign, a three-month initiative promoting green spaces and supporting Bahrain's national afforestation plan, has concluded. Conducted in partnership with UN-Habitat, the FAO, and NIAD, the campaign distributed over 13,000 saplings across 57 sites in Bahrain. The initiative aimed to increase Bahrain's tree count to 3.6 million by 2035 and fostered public engagement, environmental responsibility, and partnerships between various stakeholders.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture

records.title: In Oman, the Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the water treatment company Nada Al Rabeei, is offering technical support to fa...
records.description: In Oman, the Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the water treatment company Nada Al Rabeei, is offering technical support to farms for the installation of desalination units. This initiative addresses the increasing problem of water salinity impacting agricultural productivity. The support includes on-site assessments of water quality and crop needs, recommendations for appropriate desalination unit specifications, and provision of maintenance and operation manuals to ensure sustainable use of the technology.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, The Water Treatment Company Nada Al Rabeei

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Oman's agriculture and fisheries sectors are experiencing significant growth and attracting investment under Oman Vision 2040.
records.description: Oman's agriculture and fisheries sectors are experiencing significant growth and attracting investment under Oman Vision 2040. Agricultural output reached 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, with consistent growth in livestock and fisheries production as well. Exports, particularly in fisheries, have generated substantial revenue. The Oman Food Investment Holding Company plans significant investments in food-related ventures, focusing on modern technologies like hydroponics and aquaculture. Key projects include Al Najd and Saham Agricultural Cities and the Barr Al Hikman Shrimp Aquaculture Farm. Investment opportunities exist across various areas, including livestock farming, greenhouses, aquaculture, and food processing.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: In Saudi Arabia's Northern Borders region, women are skilled in producing wild ghee, a cultural staple linked to the region's large lives...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia's Northern Borders region, women are skilled in producing wild ghee, a cultural staple linked to the region's large livestock population (over 7 million cattle and camels). Production is highest in winter due to demand for dishes like porridge. The process involves multiple stages, from milking to creating "Khathir" (a fermented milk product), churning it in a "Samil" (a goatskin or sheepskin container), and then melting the resulting butter into ghee, which is stored in leather containers ("Al-Nahw" or "Al-Dharf"). Local women display their ghee and other handicrafts at events, with the Arar market and Lavender Hall providing key venues and training opportunities.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company's subsidiary, Agricultural Development Company (ADC), signed a 165 million Saudi riyal ($43.95 million) contract wit...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company's subsidiary, Agricultural Development Company (ADC), signed a 165 million Saudi riyal ($43.95 million) contract with China's Chengdu Design & Research Institute to build 100 poultry broiler houses in Saudi Arabia. These modern farms will utilize automation and Industry 4.0 technologies and are expected to be operational by January 2027. The project aligns with Tanmiah's overall expansion strategy in primary poultry processing.
records.institution: Tanmiah Food Company

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The "Reef Saudi" program launched the "Our Winter is Rural" initiative at the "Rural Village Agricultural Fair – Ghee and Honey" event in...
records.description: The "Reef Saudi" program launched the "Our Winter is Rural" initiative at the "Rural Village Agricultural Fair – Ghee and Honey" event in Riyadh. This initiative aims to promote Saudi Arabia's rural regions as unique tourist destinations, showcasing their natural beauty, cultural diversity, and local products like ghee and honey. It seeks to empower rural communities and contribute to sustainable development in line with Saudi Vision 2030. The fair allows visitors to experience rural life and discover local products. The Reef Saudi program, recognized by the FAO as the largest global development program of its kind, has supported over 77,000 agricultural projects and contributed to job creation in rural areas.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Dubai International Chamber facilitated the expansion of Dubai-based agri-food technology provider Farm To Plate into Eswatini.
records.description: Dubai International Chamber facilitated the expansion of Dubai-based agri-food technology provider Farm To Plate into Eswatini. The Chamber connected Farm To Plate with key stakeholders, leading to a partnership with the Royal Science and Technology Park. This collaboration aims to modernize Eswatini's agri-food supply chain, empower local farmers, enhance sustainability, and optimize agricultural practices using Farm To Plate's technology. The partnership will introduce end-to-end supply chain tools to boost farmer incomes, improve food quality assurance, promote local products, enhance export readiness, and strengthen local food production.
records.institution: Dubai International Chamber, Farm To Plate

records.title: The UAE provided 700 tons of food aid to Somalia to assist families impacted by severe drought.
records.description: The UAE provided 700 tons of food aid to Somalia to assist families impacted by severe drought. The aid was delivered to Somalia's Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) and will be distributed to drought-stricken regions, including Kismayo, Garowe, areas near Mogadishu, and regions between Mogadishu and Jowhar. SoDMA expressed gratitude to the UAE for its ongoing humanitarian support. Somalia has been struggling with recurring droughts and famine, which have devastated agriculture and livestock.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: The Northern Borders Region of Saudi Arabia is rich in diverse wild plants, including the arta plant (calligonum comosum), which has retu...
records.description: The Northern Borders Region of Saudi Arabia is rich in diverse wild plants, including the arta plant (calligonum comosum), which has returned to Wadi Arar after being nearly extinct due to overgrazing and illegal logging. Environmental laws and natural reserves have aided in the revival of various plant species. The arta is described as a thornless shrub with white branches, green tips, and fragrant white and red flowers, producing hairy, spherical fruits that range from red to yellowish-green.
records.institution: The Saudi Government

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival has solidified its position as a key tourism and economic event for Saudi Arabia and the Al-Jouf...
records.description: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival has solidified its position as a key tourism and economic event for Saudi Arabia and the Al-Jouf region. Showcasing Al-Jouf's status as the "land of olives," the festival features local and international participants, highlighting olive and oil production, processing, and related industries. It supports local businesses and families, providing platforms for their products. The event also includes product quality testing and cultural displays showcasing Saudi heritage.
records.institution: The Saudi Government

records.title: The Tihama area in Al-Baha region is a significant agricultural area in Saudi Arabia, covering over 900 hectares and producing a diverse...
records.description: The Tihama area in Al-Baha region is a significant agricultural area in Saudi Arabia, covering over 900 hectares and producing a diverse range of crops including mangoes, coffee, bananas, citrus fruits, and grains. This agricultural diversity supports the local economy and creates job opportunities. Local farms have also become tourist destinations, offering guided tours and hands-on experiences to promote sustainable agriculture and further support the local economy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: A workshop introducing a water map and strategies for revitalizing community initiatives was held in Jawf Governorate, Yemen.
records.description: A workshop introducing a water map and strategies for revitalizing community initiatives was held in Jawf Governorate, Yemen. Organized by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, the workshop aimed to educate over 40 participants on utilizing water resources for agricultural advancement and sustainable development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia pre-qualifies bidders in 2-GW battery storage tender
records.description: Saudi Arabia has pre-qualified 33 companies to bid on four battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, each with a capacity of 500 MW/2,000 MWh, totaling 2,000 MW/8,000 MWh. These projects will be developed under the build-own-operate (BOO) model. The winning developers will own the projects and sign a 15-year energy storage service agreement with the Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC). The BESS projects will support Saudi Arabia's goal of achieving 50% renewable energy in its electricity mix by 2030.
records.institution: The Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Arctech Solar will supply its SkyLine II single-axis solar tracking system for the 1.5-GW Al Ajban solar PV plant in Abu Dhabi.
records.description: Arctech Solar will supply its SkyLine II single-axis solar tracking system for the 1.5-GW Al Ajban solar PV plant in Abu Dhabi. The project, owned by EDF Renewables, Korea Western Power (KOWEPO), and Masdar, is expected to begin commercial operations in Q3 2026. Arctech has been active in the Middle East since 2017 and is currently building a manufacturing facility in Jeddah, expected to be operational in 2025.
records.institution: Masdar

records.title: the first Al Ain Dates Festival has commenced.
records.description: the first Al Ain Dates Festival has commenced. Organized by the Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority, the festival celebrates the historical significance of the palm tree in Emirati heritage and promotes Al Ain's cultural, economic, and agricultural importance. The festival features seven date competitions showcasing different varieties, a date auction, date shops, and a traditional market.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority

records.title: Oman to set up ‘Net Zero Centre’ to meet 2050 targets
records.description: Oman will establish a "Net Zero Centre" to help achieve its goal of net-zero emissions by 2050. The center will be responsible for developing strategies, monitoring net-zero projects (including energy efficiency initiatives), and providing technical support to public and private entities. It will also focus on adopting international best practices and technologies, supporting research and innovation, and developing national expertise. Furthermore, the center will manage carbon, hydrogen, and low-carbon product certifications and oversee carbon certificate trading in line with international standards.
records.institution: Net Zero Centre

records.title: A 10-day training course for leaders of development associations in Sa'afan district, Sana'a province, has concluded.
records.description: A 10-day training course for leaders of development associations in Sa'afan district, Sana'a province, has concluded. The course, funded by the Agricultural and Fisheries Projects and Initiatives Financing Unit, trained 18 participants in management, planning, evaluation, and financial systems relevant to development work. Local officials emphasized the importance of applying this knowledge to strengthen communities and support sustainable development, particularly in agriculture and community services, despite ongoing challenges. Participants received completion certificates at a closing ceremony.
records.institution: The Social Affairs and Labor Office,The Western Sector Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Association

records.title: The Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) is launching the Citrus Season to support local farmers and promote agritourism.
records.description: The Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) is launching the Citrus Season to support local farmers and promote agritourism. This event aims to support local farmers, promote AlUla as an agritourism destination, and stimulate economic growth. The season will showcase the region's diverse citrus production, which includes 29 varieties grown on over 5,000 farms, yielding 14,000 tons of fruit annually. The Citrus Season will feature exhibitions for local farmers and families, various events, and a training course on using citrus fruits in cooking. Along with the AlUla Dates Season, it serves as a key economic driver, promoting local products in regional markets and contributing to sustainable development.
records.institution: The Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU)

records.title: A’Saffa Foods SAOG has announced an expansion plan to increase its broiler chicken production from 48 million to 60 million birds per year.
records.description: A’Saffa Foods SAOG has announced an expansion plan to increase its broiler chicken production from 48 million to 60 million birds per year. This expansion is part of a five-year growth strategy to meet rising demand for poultry products, address food security challenges, and solidify the company's leading position in the sector. The investment also aims to strengthen the supply chain, improve operational efficiency, and create more jobs in Oman, contributing to the nation's economic development under Oman Vision 2040.
records.institution: A’Saffa Foods SAOG

records.description: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival will take place at the Prince Abdulilah Urban Center in Sakaka. records.description: The Asian Arab Business Forum 2024 in Muscat highlighted Oman's strategic role as a global trade hub connecting Asia, the Arab world, and beyond. The forum emphasized collaboration in sectors like renewable energy, technology, logistics, tourism, and agriculture. Attendees discussed Oman's investment-friendly policies and its potential as a key link in the global economy. The event also focused on building connections with Europe, particularly Greece, to bridge the gap between East and West. Organizers emphasized their commitment to ongoing engagement and future initiatives to solidify Oman's position in global trade.
records.institution: The College of Banking and Financial Studies (CBFS)

The event attracted significant interest from farmers and livestock breeders, with 451 submissions across four main categories and 13 subcategories. With total cash prizes of AED5.3 million, the award aims to stimulate excellence in plant and animal agriculture, promote sustainable practices, and strengthen the food security system. It honors distinguished farmers, livestock breeders, and productive families, encouraging the adoption of modern agricultural systems and fostering positive competition to ensure the sector's sustainability.

This distribution underscores Saudi Arabia's continued dedication to humanitarian support through KSrelief.

records.title: Oman has achieved 100% self-sufficiency in cucumber production, with over 103,000 tonnes produced in 2023, primarily in North al Batinah.
records.description: Oman has achieved 100% self-sufficiency in cucumber production, with over 103,000 tonnes produced in 2023, primarily in North al Batinah. The country also boasts high self-sufficiency rates for peppers (95%) and tomatoes (83%), with significant production also concentrated in North al Batinah. While some re-exporting and importing of these crops occurs, Oman is largely meeting its domestic needs.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.description: The Hatta Honey Festival, a UAE event supporting Emirati beekeepers and honey production. Organized by Dubai Municipality, the festival features 51 Emirati beekeepers and aims to promote the honey sector, support local businesses, and enhance Hatta's appeal as a tourist destination. The festival includes a honey auction, a best Emirati honey competition, educational workshops, entertainment, and children's activities. Dubai Municipality is also providing on-site laboratory testing to ensure honey quality and food safety. The event aims to generate economic opportunities for Hatta residents and contribute to the emirate's overall development.
records.institution: Dubai Municipality

records.title: A 40-day training course on agricultural and livestock value chains concluded, qualifying 38 agriculture graduates from Sana'a, Dhamar, a...
records.description: A 40-day training course on agricultural and livestock value chains concluded, qualifying 38 agriculture graduates from Sana'a, Dhamar, and Ibb universities. The country also saw a 53.4% increase in average annual precipitation and a substantial rise in floodwater collected by dams. With bilateral trade valued at A$9.9 billion in 2023 and two-way investments totaling A$20.6 billion, the deal strengthens ties across agriculture, mining, and critical minerals. Key Australian exports like meat, dairy, seafood, coal, and pulses will benefit, with the Australian Meat Industry Council welcoming increased market access for beef, lamb, and goat meat. The agreement is expected to take effect by the end of 2024.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade

The initiative seeks to enhance Dubai's R&D capacity, foster collaboration between sectors, and position the city as a global hub for scientific research and innovation. The selection process will prioritize projects that align with these goals.

Supported by H.H. Dr. Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, the initiative promotes local wheat cultivation to enhance food security and reduce dependence on imports. Under the patronage of the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the event will focus on agricultural sustainability and food security, aligned with the UAE's 2030 National Vision. This year's edition will feature sectors such as aquaculture, vertical farming, livestock health, and veterinary supplies. AgraME will also introduce the Regenerative Agriculture Middle East Conference, promoting collaboration and innovation in agriculture across the region.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has closed Panaderia Bakery in Abu Dhabi due to multiple violations of food...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has closed Panaderia Bakery in Abu Dhabi due to multiple violations of food safety regulations, which posed a risk to public health. The violations were detailed in a Food Control Report, which noted the bakery's non-compliance with health and safety standards and poor maintenance of the facility. The closure followed several infractions recorded in previous inspections during the past year. The bakery will be permitted to reopen only after it implements corrective actions that align with UAE food safety laws and addresses the specific reasons for the closure. These include issues such as improper display of ready-to-serve foods and the presence of personal items in storage areas. ADAFSA's ongoing efforts to uphold food safety standards include regular inspections and public campaigns to encourage reporting of food safety concerns.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

This "continuity coalition" could be launched at Cop29 in Baku, building on health-related discussions from Cop28 in the UAE. The coalition aims to integrate health considerations into climate policy, addressing issues like pollution and disease. A second health day will take place at Cop29, focusing on resilience, development, and urban health challenges.

The forum, which involved over 200 experts, highlighted initiatives from the G20 Riyadh Summit aimed at biodiversity conservation, land degradation prevention, and coral reef research advancements. Additionally, the Saudi Green Initiative and the Middle East Green Initiative were discussed as crucial efforts to protect 30 percent of Saudi's terrestrial and marine areas by 2030. The forum also set the stage for the upcoming COP16, focusing on enhancing international efforts against land degradation and drought.

Organized by the National Center for Wildlife (NCW), the event focuses on nature-based solutions, protected areas, and sustainable land restoration. A highlight is Saudi Arabia's Protected Areas Plan, aiming to protect 30% of the country's land and marine environments by 2030, aligning with the Saudi Green Initiative. The forum promotes collaboration and knowledge sharing across the region.

records.description: Bahrain’s agricultural sector is expected to grow by 1.9% annually from 2024 to 2029, according to a report. Despite its dependence on imported food, Bahrain remains a top global producer of dates. The government is enhancing local agriculture through financial assistance and partnerships with tech firms to reduce reliance on imports. The National Initiative for Agricultural Development focuses on modern farming techniques, water efficiency, and expanding green spaces. Key crops include dates, figs, and potatoes, with local dairy and poultry mainly serving the domestic market.

records.description: Oman Krishikkottam, a group promoting pesticide-free agriculture, held its 14th seed distribution event in Ruwi, providing 17 varieties of vegetable seeds to over 200 people. This initiative encourages sustainable, home-grown food practices, particularly within Oman's Indian diaspora. The event featured educational sessions on organic farming techniques, aimed at empowering families to grow vegetables at home. With a community of over 4,500 families, the group continues to advocate for organic farming and a healthier environment.

records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources (MAFWR) has launched the National Animal Wealth Vaccination Project in South Batinah. The project aims to vaccinate livestock against major epidemic and infectious diseases over an eight-month period. This initiative is part of the national strategy to improve animal health, lower treatment costs, and ensure the production of safe, high-quality animal products. Last season, over 288,964 animals were vaccinated. The program also focuses on educating livestock breeders on modern practices.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s KSrelief continues its humanitarian efforts, delivering aid across multiple regions.
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s KSrelief continues its humanitarian efforts, delivering aid across multiple regions. In Libya, it distributed 2,916 food baskets in Derna to assist 14,580 people affected by Storm Daniel. In Sudan, the agency provided 600 shelter bags in Northern State, aiding 3,479 people impacted by flash floods. KSrelief also carried out medical missions in Turkiye’s Gaziantep and Hatay, focusing on orthopedic surgeries for victims of recent earthquakes. In Lebanon, through the Al-Amal Charitable Bakery project, 150,000 bread bags were distributed to Syrian, Palestinian, and local families, benefiting 62,500 individuals.

records.description: Oman's first commercial saffron farm, Saffron Oman, has begun operations in Al Jabal Al Akhdar. The farm spans over 25,000 square meters and aims to harvest its first saffron crop by the end of 2024. The project, led by Ahmed Ali al Hanshi, is focused on cultivating saffron due to its high value and ideal growing conditions in the region. The farm plans to become self-sufficient by producing saffron bulbs and avoiding future imports, positioning Oman as a regional and global player in saffron production.
records.institution: Saffron Oman

records.description: Saudi Arabia views Italy as a key partner in its efforts to deliver green energy and fuels, such as renewable-powered hydrogen, to Europe. As part of its energy strategy to diversify from oil and gas, Saudi Arabia is expanding its production capacity for low-carbon products like blue and green hydrogen. The country is seeking allies to facilitate the export of these products, with Italy being identified as a "partner of choice" for bringing them to the European market. Saudi Arabia is also exploring partnerships with other European nations, including Germany, to invest in infrastructure like ports and pipelines to transport green energy.

records.description: Oman has launched Phase 1 of a ginger cultivation project in Dhofar, involving 30 farmers across three acres in the wilayats of Rakhyut and Dhalkut. Supported by the Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund, the project expects to yield 20 to 30 tonnes by February 2025. It offers technical support, promotes modern irrigation systems, and aims to expand into the private sector. A total of 60 farmers are expected to benefit over the next two years, reducing reliance on imports and creating local economic opportunities.

records.title: The UAE and Jordan have signed a $2.3 billion investment agreement aimed at boosting Jordan's railway sector.
records.description: The UAE and Jordan have signed a $2.3 billion investment agreement aimed at boosting Jordan's railway sector. The memorandum of understanding focuses on developing a 360-kilometer railway network in Jordan to connect phosphate and potash mines to the Port of Aqaba. UAE's Etihad Rail also signed agreements with Jordan’s transport ministry, Jordan Phosphate Mines Company, and Arab Potash Company to transport 16 million tons of minerals annually. This project, set to begin construction bids in 2026, will enhance logistical efficiency, create job opportunities, and strengthen Jordan’s export capabilities. It follows a $2 billion agreement between the two countries signed in 2023.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Investment

records.title: The khareef season in Dhofar, known for its lush landscapes and tourist appeal, also offers significant potential for agricultural research.
records.description: The khareef season in Dhofar, known for its lush landscapes and tourist appeal, also offers significant potential for agricultural research. With around 800 of Oman’s 1,200 plant species found in Dhofar, the monsoon season provides ideal conditions for scientists to study plant growth, ecological interactions, and water management. Continuous rainfall reduces evaporation, enhances crop growth, and lowers soil salinity, benefiting agriculture year-round. Researchers are also exploring fog harvesting as a sustainable water source for farming in arid climates.
records.institution: Director of the Department of Agricultural and Livestock Research in Dhofar

records.title: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture has sought assistance from the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority's (ADAFSA) Collabora...
records.description: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture has sought assistance from the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority's (ADAFSA) Collaborating Centre for Camel Disease to investigate a mysterious disease causing camel deaths in Ethiopia and East Africa. A team of experts, recommended by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, began working in July to identify the cause and develop treatment methods.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture, following recommendations from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, has so...
records.description: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture, following recommendations from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, has sought assistance from ADAFSA's Collaborating Centre for Camel Disease to address unexplained camel deaths threatening livestock across Ethiopia, Sudan, Somalia, and Kenya. A team of experts from the centre began work in Ethiopia in July to investigate the cause and develop preventive and treatment methods.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Oman Flour Mills Company reported a 25% increase in export volumes, reaching 40,449 metric tonnes of flour products this year.
records.description: Oman Flour Mills Company reported a 25% increase in export volumes, reaching 40,449 metric tonnes of flour products this year. This growth is attributed to the company's efforts in expanding its infrastructure, improving packaging standards, and enhancing transportation to meet demand in local and international markets. The company is also exploring new opportunities in the food industry, including acquisitions in the animal feed sector and plans to diversify into sweets and confectionery. OFM’s expansion has also created over 500 new jobs in Oman.

records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources is undertaking a project to restore 100 aflaj irrigation systems in Dhahirah at a cost of over RO848,000. So far, 20 aflaj have been rehabilitated, with work ongoing on the remaining 80.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has provided recycling containers to 80% of households in Doha, allowing residents to separate recyclabl...
records.description: Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has provided recycling containers to 80% of households in Doha, allowing residents to separate recyclable materials like plastic, glass, paper, and metal from organic waste. The recyclable waste is transported to a recycling hub in Mesaieed, which currently has 11 operational factories, with seven more nearing completion and an additional 12 under construction. The initiative will expand to other municipalities, including Umm Salal, Al Daayen, Al Khor, and Al Shamal, by 2026, and further to Al Rayan, Al Wakra, and Al Sheehaniya by 2027.
records.institution: Qatari Ministry of Municipality

records.title: Ma Hawa, an Emirati brand, has launched its innovative Water-from-Air bottles in the UAE, using atmospheric moisture to produce pure drin...
records.description: Ma Hawa, an Emirati brand, has launched its innovative Water-from-Air bottles in the UAE, using atmospheric moisture to produce pure drinking water. The bottles are now available at select Union Coop stores and ADNOC outlets, with plans to expand further across the country. This technology offers a sustainable solution to the UAE’s water scarcity issues, providing an eco-friendly water source in one of the most water-stressed regions globally.
records.institution: Ma Hawa

records.title: Silal, a leading UAE food and technology company, has announced its acquisition of a majority stake in Al Bakrawe Holding, a key regional...
records.description: Silal, a leading UAE food and technology company, has announced its acquisition of a majority stake in Al Bakrawe Holding, a key regional importer and distributor of fresh fruits and vegetables. This acquisition aims to enhance Silal's position as a major supplier of fresh produce in the UAE, leveraging Al Bakrawe’s extensive global sourcing network. The collaboration will improve supply chain capabilities and expand market reach, contributing to a more sustainable food ecosystem in the region. This is Silal's third strategic acquisition.
records.institution: Silal

records.title: UAE-based Future Food Foundry (3F) has invested over $20 million in NextGen Farms (NGF) and Sustenir Group to create the largest plant su...
records.description: UAE-based Future Food Foundry (3F) has invested over $20 million in NextGen Farms (NGF) and Sustenir Group to create the largest plant superfood ecosystem in Singapore. The partnership aims to enhance food security in the region by leveraging controlled environment farming techniques to produce nutrient-rich superfoods. This move strengthens 3F’s agri-tech presence in MENA and Asia-Pacific, with plans for sustainable agriculture and food innovation expansion. Both NGF and Sustenir specialize in advanced farming technologies and superfood production.
records.institution: Future Food Foundry (3F)

records.title: Yemeni fishermen are increasingly turning to artificial reefs (ARs) made from scrap materials to boost fish stocks as they face the combi...
records.description: Yemeni fishermen are increasingly turning to artificial reefs (ARs) made from scrap materials to boost fish stocks as they face the combined challenges of civil war, environmental decline, and dwindling catches. These DIY reefs, created from firewood, tyres, and metal, are meant to replace dying coral reefs, providing habitat for marine life and helping fishermen maintain their livelihoods. However, the use of manmade materials has raised environmental concerns, with critics warning of potential water pollution and harm to marine ecosystems. Despite these risks, the practice persists, driven by the steep decline in fish stocks, economic hardship, and dangerous conditions for fishermen.
records.institution: Yemeni Fishermen

records.description: QatarEnergy is set to build a new urea production complex in Mesaieed Industrial City, doubling the country's output from 6 million to 12.4 million tonnes per annum. This expansion will make Qatar the world’s largest producer of urea, a key agricultural fertilizer, as global demand rises due to population growth. The project will include three ammonia production lines supplying feedstock to four new urea production trains, with the first train expected to be operational by the end of the decade.
records.institution: QatarEnergy

records.title: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company, a leading flour milling firm in Saudi Arabia, has announced the price range for its Initial Publ...
records.description: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company, a leading flour milling firm in Saudi Arabia, has announced the price range for its Initial Public Offering (IPO) at SAR62 to SAR66 per share. The offering is expected to raise between SAR954 million and SAR1,016 million ($255 million to $271 million), with a market capitalization ranging from SAR3.182 billion to SAR3.387 billion ($848 million to $903 million). The institutional book-building period began on September 1 and will close on September 5. The IPO consists of 15,394,502 shares, representing 30% of the company’s issued share capital, being sold by existing shareholders. Proceeds from the sale will be distributed to the selling shareholders, with the shares to be listed on the Saudi Exchange following the IPO. HSBC Saudi Arabia is serving as the financial advisor and lead manager for the offering.
records.institution: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company
