records.title: Saudi Arabia has launched a tender for a fish farming project in the Jubail governorate on the northeastern coast as part of its Vision 2...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched a tender for a fish farming project in the Jubail governorate on the northeastern coast as part of its Vision 2030 development plan. The initiative, covering a four-hectare area, aims to promote healthier eating habits and enhance food security through aquaponics. This method synergizes fish farming with plant cultivation in tanks, where fish waste serves as natural fertilizer for the plants while the plants clean the water, eliminating the need for chemicals. The tender deadline is set for November 27, and this project follows the issuance of 18 aquaculture licenses in the Mecca region, which represents about one-third of the country's Red Sea coastline.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Saudi Arabia has lifted a 21-year ban on South African meat imports, allowing South African producers to export beef, lamb, and mutton to...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has lifted a 21-year ban on South African meat imports, allowing South African producers to export beef, lamb, and mutton to the Kingdom. Twelve South African companies have been approved for beef exports, while seven have been approved for lamb and mutton. This development was discussed during a virtual trade session attended by officials and industry stakeholders from both countries, focusing on the potential to increase trade and export market share.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Saudi authorities have sentenced four board members of Raydan Food Co, including the vice chairman, to 90 days in prison for market viola...
records.description: Saudi authorities have sentenced four board members of Raydan Food Co, including the vice chairman, to 90 days in prison for market violations such as insider trading and providing misleading financial information. In total, 14 individuals connected with the Tadawul-listed company were penalized, with some ordered to pay SAR 77 million ($20 million) in compensation for illegal trading activities. The group also faces fines totaling SAR 50.6 million, and 11 members have been banned from working with entities supervised by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) for up to three years. The violations involved false representation of the company’s financial statements from 2018 to 2020 and insider trading prior to a public announcement in March 2022. Affected parties are invited to file compensation claims through the CMA's website.

Trufud supplies major supermarkets and wholesale markets in Oman and aims to expand its agricultural output. records.description: Fish prices in Bahrain have surged due to a shortage of local fish and increased reliance on imports. The hot weather has made it difficult to catch larger local fish, leading to the sale of smaller fish at higher prices, with some imported varieties also contributing to the price hike. Currently, about 70% of fish in Bahrain’s Central Market are imported from countries like India, Pakistan, and Oman. The situation has caused strain on consumers, with prices rising significantly for both local and imported fish.

records.title: Qatar is on track to double its economy by 2031, driven by strategic initiatives that have restored government revenues to levels seen be...
records.description: Qatar is on track to double its economy by 2031, driven by strategic initiatives that have restored government revenues to levels seen before the 2014 oil price shock. The country's significant position in the global energy market, particularly as the world's sixth-largest gas producer with the third-largest gas reserves, has been pivotal. With planned increases in LNG output by 85% at the North Field by 2025, Qatar's natural gas production is expected to nearly double by 2030. Beyond hydrocarbons, Qatar's economic diversification efforts have reduced its reliance on oil and gas, with two-thirds of its GDP now coming from non-oil sectors like real estate, construction, financial services, trade, manufacturing, logistics, and tourism. Additionally, foreign investment reforms and infrastructural developments linked to the World Cup and National Vision 2030 have further fueled economic growth across various sectors.

Crude oil exports saw a 7.6% increase, while refined oil and liquefied natural gas exports declined. Non-oil exports increased by 11.2%, with minerals, base metals, and chemical products leading this growth. Additionally, re-exports grew by 8.1%. The UAE was the largest market for Oman’s non-oil exports and re-exports, with significant increases in both categories.

records.description: Oman recorded an 11.6% increase in the value of fruit and vegetable imports, totaling over OMR 110 million from May 2023 to May 2024. records.title: UAE Amends Labour Law, Introduces Stricter Fines for Violations
records.description: The UAE government has significantly amended its Labour Law, introducing a range of stricter regulations and higher fines for violations in employment relationships. According to the new federal decree-law, penalties for employment violations can now reach between Dhs100,000 and Dhs1 million. These amendments include severe fines for employers who engage in illegal practices such as hiring without proper permits, failing to provide jobs after recruitment, misusing work permits, and shutting down operations without settling workers' rights. Additional penalties are set for the illegal employment of minors and fictitious recruitment practices, including fraudulent Emiratisation. The decree also shifts the jurisdiction for labor disputes from the Court of Appeal to the Court of First Instance unless already adjudicated. Additionally, MOHRE is empowered to initiate criminal proceedings for fictitious employment, with provisions for employers to settle cases before court sentencing by paying a substantial portion of the fines and returning any unduly received incentives.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.description: The UAE and Chile have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to significantly enhance their bilateral relations, particularly in non-oil trade, which stood at $306 million in 2023. Both nations aim to triple this figure by 2030. This agreement, signed during Chilean President Gabriel Boric Font's historic first visit to the UAE, seeks to eliminate or reduce customs duties, streamline customs procedures, and remove trade barriers, thus fostering increased investment flows and private sector partnerships.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: Saudi Arabia has introduced the Seasonal Markets System, a significant upgrade to the trading infrastructure for dates.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced the Seasonal Markets System, a significant upgrade to the trading infrastructure for dates. Initiated by the National Center for Palms and Dates in cooperation with the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, this mandatory electronic platform is designed to regulate and enhance date trading in seasonal markets across the kingdom. By requiring registration for sellers, buyers, and marketers, the system aims to streamline sales, ensure financial security, and provide access to market data and marketing services. It's a strategic move to boost the sustainability and global competitiveness of Saudi Arabia's prominent date sector, which is a key economic contributor with over 36 million palm trees producing more than 1.6 million tons of dates annually.
records.institution: The National Center for Palms and Dates

records.title: The farms of Qatif Oasis play a crucial role in supplying a wide variety of seasonal produce throughout Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province.
records.description: The farms of Qatif Oasis play a crucial role in supplying a wide variety of seasonal produce throughout Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. Stretching across 800 square kilometers from Safwa to Dammam, this region is home to over 3,700 farms, of which 2,454 are active and produce crops including vegetables, fruits, and fresh dates. Notably, these farms contribute significantly to the local economy, annually providing 29.5 tonnes of dates from over 540,000 fruit-bearing palm trees.
records.institution: Qatif Oasis

records.title: The UAE's renewable energy firm, Masdar, has broadened its footprint in the European green energy landscape with a substantial $887 milli...
records.description: The UAE's renewable energy firm, Masdar, has broadened its footprint in the European green energy landscape with a substantial $887 million investment in Spain. This investment secures a 49.99 percent stake in 48 solar plants, managed by Endesa, an Enel subsidiary. This move not only underscores Masdar's commitment to fostering the energy transition in Spain and Europe but also marks a strategic expansion into renewable energy markets across the continent. This agreement paves the way for future collaborations, including a memorandum of understanding with Endesa to explore the development of an additional 3 gigawatts of solar capacity. As European utilities navigate the high-interest rate environment by divesting minority stakes in renewable assets.
records.institution: Masdar

records.title: The “Al Dhaid Date Festival” in its eighth iteration, organized by the Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry, is currently underway at...
records.description: The “Al Dhaid Date Festival” in its eighth iteration, organized by the Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry, is currently underway at Expo Al Dhaid. This festival has become a critical platform for farmers to access the latest in agricultural technologies, sustainable practices, and organic products aimed at enhancing palm cultivation and date production. Participants include companies specializing in organic farming and agricultural machinery, presenting alternatives to chemical inputs and showcasing cutting-edge equipment designed to boost farm productivity while preserving environmental health.
records.institution: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI)

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Aquaponics, an innovative farming method that merges aquaculture with hydroponics, is making strides in sustainable agriculture in Oman.
records.description: Aquaponics, an innovative farming method that merges aquaculture with hydroponics, is making strides in sustainable agriculture in Oman. This method cultivates fish and plants together in a closed-loop system that recycles water. Fish waste provides a nutrient-rich source for the plants, while the plants clean the water, which is then recirculated back to the fish tanks. Highly efficient and conserving up to 90% more water than traditional farming, aquaponics supports year-round food production without the need for soil or chemical fertilizers.
records.institution: Omani Farmers

records.title: At a global summit in Rome, Saudi Arabia showcased its environmental initiatives, particularly in combating land degradation.
records.description: At a global summit in Rome, Saudi Arabia showcased its environmental initiatives, particularly in combating land degradation. The presentation was led by the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification. The delegation highlighted Saudi Arabia's readiness to host the upcoming 16th Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification and Land Degradation in Riyadh. The efforts discussed included the restoration of ecosystems and the launch of forest and dryland initiatives.
records.institution: Saudi National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification

records.title: In North Sharqiyah, Oman, a significant agricultural expansion has contributed to the region's food security and economic growth, with th...
records.description: In North Sharqiyah, Oman, a significant agricultural expansion has contributed to the region's food security and economic growth, with the area now producing 250,000 tonnes of various crops annually. This development was highlighted by Dr. Abdul Aziz bin Ali al Mashaikhi, Director General of Agriculture and Water Resources in North Sharqiyah. The region has seen a notable increase in fruit crop areas by 2.3%, totaling nearly 285 hectares, and a 1.3% increase in date palm cultivation, covering over 3,000 hectares and producing 54,188 tonnes of dates. North Sharqiyah, ranking fourth in date production nationally, offers substantial investment opportunities aimed at employing modern agricultural technologies, including greenhouses.
records.institution: Agriculture and Water Resources in North Sharqiyah

records.title: During a visit to Brazil, a senior Saudi minister engaged with major Brazilian companies to advance food production localization and avia...
records.description: During a visit to Brazil, a senior Saudi minister engaged with major Brazilian companies to advance food production localization and aviation cooperation. Discussions with executives from Minerva Foods and JBS focused on bringing food production expertise and technology to Saudi Arabia, aiming to enhance the Kingdom's production capabilities. Additionally, meetings with Embraer explored possibilities for advancing the aviation industry within Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, Minerva Foods, & JBS

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has launched a new agriculture and food security data platform to support de...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has launched a new agriculture and food security data platform to support decision-making and enhance food security management in Abu Dhabi. This comprehensive platform provides detailed insights across all aspects of the agriculture and food sectors, from production to consumption. It facilitates informed policymaking by analyzing current data to improve the efficiency of food security strategies and develop a sustainable and resilient food system for the emirate. The platform integrates data from 16 strategic partners and covers over 335 indicators, enabling proactive management of food emergencies, diseases, and pests, thereby minimizing supply chain disruptions. Additionally, it includes a sophisticated warning system to handle various risks and threats.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The United Arab Emirates and Morocco have completed negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), poised to enh...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates and Morocco have completed negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), poised to enhance trade and investment relationships between the two countries. This agreement aims to streamline the flow of goods and services by lowering or abolishing tariffs, simplifying trade barriers, and ensuring more accessible market access. It encompasses cooperation across various sectors, including renewable energy, tourism, and infrastructure, reflecting a shared vision for economic growth and expanded private sector engagement.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

records.title: First Milling Company ("First Mills"), a leading Saudi milling enterprise, has reported robust financial results for the first half (H1)...
records.description: First Milling Company ("First Mills"), a leading Saudi milling enterprise, has reported robust financial results for the first half (H1) and second quarter (Q2) of 2024. The company saw a 10.5% year-on-year increase in H1 revenue, reaching SAR 518.8 million, fueled by a 31.1% increase in Feed sales due to favorable market conditions and product diversification. Despite a decrease in Bran sales, Flour sales rose by 7.3% driven by popular retail products. The company also enjoyed a 13.4% increase in net profit for H1, totaling SAR 123.2 million, with a notable net margin of 23.8%. This financial success was supported by capacity upgrades at its Jeddah plant and effective cost management, leading to broad-based growth across all product categories in Q2, culminating in a 13.3% increase in revenue for the quarter.
records.institution: Saudi First Milling Company (First Mills)

records.title: In Dhofar, Oman, efforts to combat invasive plant species, particularly the Parthenium weed, have intensified with the distribution of ov...
records.description: In Dhofar, Oman, efforts to combat invasive plant species, particularly the Parthenium weed, have intensified with the distribution of over 40 billion local grass seeds by the Dhofar Municipality. Parthenium has significantly impacted the region's plains and agricultural fields by releasing chemicals that inhibit the growth of other plants and cause allergies in humans and livestock. The initiative, which includes the distribution of 68 varieties of wild plant seeds, aims to restore the local ecosystem, enhance biodiversity, and strengthen agricultural productivity.
records.institution: Dhofar Municipality

records.title: In Baha, Saudi Arabia, a farmer has transformed earthworms, traditionally considered a garden nuisance, into a valuable resource for orga...
records.description: In Baha, Saudi Arabia, a farmer has transformed earthworms, traditionally considered a garden nuisance, into a valuable resource for organic farming. The farmer has set up a vermicomposting operation, using worms to convert organic waste into high-quality fertilizer. This initiative began with a modest setup and has expanded significantly due to its success. The organic fertilizer produced through this method has proven to enhance plant growth, fruit production, and soil health, demonstrating a sustainable alternative to chemical fertilizers.
records.institution: Saudi Farmers

records.description: Saudi Arabia has reached a notable milestone in agricultural development by achieving a 68% self-sufficiency rate in mango production, with an annual output exceeding 89,500 tons grown across about 6,966 hectares. The country is now cultivating over 20 different varieties of mangoes, which are celebrated for their health benefits including enhancing digestion, supporting heart health, boosting immunity, and contributing to skin and eye health.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is set to enhance its bilateral relations with Brazil and Chile, focusing on attracting investments in the mineral and indus...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is set to enhance its bilateral relations with Brazil and Chile, focusing on attracting investments in the mineral and industrial sectors. The delegation, led by the Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources, will visit major cities in both countries from July 22-30, engaging in high-level discussions with senior officials and leading global companies involved in mining, aviation, food processing, and other industries. The visit includes meetings with significant entities in Brazil such as the Brazilian Mining Association and Vale, and in Chile with the Minister of Mining and major industry leaders. These meetings are geared toward leveraging Brazil's diverse economy and Chile's status as a major lithium producer to foster cooperation in sectors crucial for the future, such as electric vehicle production and renewable energy. The visit is expected to conclude with the signing of important agreements that will further mutual growth in mining and industrial capacities.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources

records.title: The UAE and Mauritius have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), marking the UAE's first such agreement with an A...
records.description: The UAE and Mauritius have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), marking the UAE's first such agreement with an African nation. This agreement aims to bolster economic growth by removing most tariffs, enhancing trade and investment, and creating new job opportunities. From January to April 2024, non-oil trade between the two countries rose significantly, reflecting growing economic ties. This CEPA is expected to increase the UAE's GDP by 0.96% and Mauritius's economy by over 1% by 2030.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: The Zubair Enterprises Development Centre (Zubair EDC) in Oman is spearheading a feasibility study on the use of Azolla as fish feed, in...
records.description: The Zubair Enterprises Development Centre (Zubair EDC) in Oman is spearheading a feasibility study on the use of Azolla as fish feed, in collaboration with Tuhlub and the Leaders Consultancies and Development Centre. This study aims to enhance the aqua feed industry and boost food security in Oman. Azolla, known for its rapid growth rate and nutritional properties, could offer a sustainable alternative to conventional feed.
records.institution: Zubair Enterprises Development Centre (Zubair EDC)

records.title: Abu Dhabi's clean-energy company, Masdar, has successfully raised $1 billion through its second green bond issuance, which was highly ove...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's clean-energy company, Masdar, has successfully raised $1 billion through its second green bond issuance, which was highly oversubscribed with an orderbook that peaked at $4.6 billion. This issuance, split into two tranches with tenors of five and ten years, will support Masdar's investments in new greenfield projects, particularly in developing economies, aiming to expand its portfolio capacity to 100GW by 2030. The funds are part of a broader Green Finance Framework under which Masdar plans to raise up to $3 billion. This follows their inaugural green bond sale of $750 million in 2023. The proceeds are allocated primarily to international investors, with a significant portion also going to MENA region investors.
records.institution: Masdar

records.description: Qatar and Iraq have reinforced their economic and renewable energy cooperation during the seventh session of the Qatari-Iraqi Joint Committee for Economic and Trade Cooperation held in Baghdad. This meeting, chaired by the respective Ministers of Commerce and Industry from both countries, highlighted their mutual commitment to deepen bilateral relations. records.title: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH, a consultancy known for its focus on alternative fuels, has launc...
records.description: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH, a consultancy known for its focus on alternative fuels, has launched a significant plastic waste management project in Saudi Arabia. This venture is in partnership with Empower, which specializes in traceability solutions, and involves a joint venture with the Saudi Investment Recycling Company (SIRC), the government's key entity for waste management initiatives. The project aims to process around 3 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually across six governorates, converting it into refuse-derived fuels (RDF) and potentially reducing CO2 emissions by about 1,791,300 tonnes per year. A notable feature of this project is the use of blockchain technology by Empower to ensure a transparent and traceable waste management process from collection to RDF conversion. This will enable real-time monitoring and provide critical data to stakeholders. Additionally, the project will incorporate Plastic Credits, which are financial incentives for verified plastic waste recycling activities, helping to close the financial gaps in waste processing and make the initiative financially viable and attractive to investors.
records.institution: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH

records.title: Saudi Aramco's Wa’ed, established to support Saudi entrepreneurs and SMEs, aims to double its support to startups by 2023.
records.description: Saudi Aramco's Wa’ed, established to support Saudi entrepreneurs and SMEs, aims to double its support to startups by 2023. Since its inception in 2011, Wa’ed has backed around 90 companies with loans and investments, and it plans to increase this number through additional deals in 2021. Wa’ed is focused on high-impact business ideas and has a success rate of 83% among its supported companies.
records.institution: Saudi Aramco Entrepreneurship Center (Wa’ed)

records.title: The Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) has entered into an $8 million contract with the Saudi-based waste management company Reviva to establ...
records.description: The Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) has entered into an $8 million contract with the Saudi-based waste management company Reviva to establish a recycling waste complex in Jeddah. The project, which covers an area of 10,000 square meters, aims to enhance waste utilization by transforming it into valuable resources, thus promoting a circular economy within the kingdom. This initiative is part of Saudi Arabia's broader environmental sustainability efforts, aligning with the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and the Green Ports Initiative. It seeks to position Saudi Arabia as a global logistics hub and elevate Jeddah Islamic Port among the top ten ports worldwide. The collaboration between Mawani and Reviva is expected to advance the kingdom's waste management capabilities significantly, in line with Saudi Vision 2030 and boosting the private sector's role in economic growth.
records.institution: Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani)

records.title: During a high-level meeting in Abu Dhabi, leaders from the UAE and Indonesia reviewed their strategic relationship under the Comprehensiv...
records.description: During a high-level meeting in Abu Dhabi, leaders from the UAE and Indonesia reviewed their strategic relationship under the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), focusing on key areas like economy, investment, renewable energy, food security, infrastructure, education, health, climate action, and the environment. They discussed the growth in non-oil trade between the two nations, from $2.7 billion in 2014 to $4.4 billion in 2023, and the completion of projects worth over $21 billion in Indonesia last year. Several Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and agreements were announced, covering various sectors including solar energy, public budget management, smart systems, peaceful nuclear energy use, and real estate development.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: Plenty, a U.S.
records.description: Plenty, a U.S. vertical farming startup, has teamed up with Mawarid, a subsidiary of Alpha Dhabi Holding, to launch a $680 million joint venture aimed at developing indoor farms across the Middle East. The venture plans to establish five farms over the next five years, starting with a facility in Abu Dhabi scheduled to begin construction next year. This farm is expected to produce over 4.5 million pounds of premium strawberries annually for local and Gulf Cooperation Council markets, beginning in 2026. The venture is financed through a combination of equity and debt, the latter provided by a regional bank.
records.institution: Plenty & Mawarid

records.title: Tadweer Group, a leader in waste management in the UAE, has introduced four new subsidiaries to innovate and enhance its recycling and wa...
records.description: Tadweer Group, a leader in waste management in the UAE, has introduced four new subsidiaries to innovate and enhance its recycling and waste management services. These subsidiaries—Tadweer Environmental Services and Solutions, Tajmee’e, UpCycle, and Tahweel—reflect the group's commitment to transforming waste into valuable resources, supporting decarbonization, and fostering a circular economy through advanced technologies. Tadweer Environmental Services and Solutions will handle public waste collection and management using digital tools, while Tajmee’e will focus on optimizing pre-collection and collection processes. UpCycle is set to advance technology integration at waste treatment and recycling centers, including a new Material Recovery Facility. Tahweel aims to expedite the development of waste conversion technologies, crucial for waste-to-energy and waste-to-value projects. These initiatives are part of Tadweer's strategic aim to divert 80% of waste from landfills by 2030 and leverage its expertise to boost sustainability efforts across Abu Dhabi and beyond. This strategic expansion follows Tadweer’s acquisition of e-waste leader Enviroserve and its recent progress on Abu Dhabi’s dedicated facility for material recovery from waste, marking significant advancements in regional waste management solutions.
records.institution: Tadweer Group

records.title: The UAE has committed to investing Dh550 million over the next decade to construct up to 10 hospitals worldwide as part of its Global Hos...
records.description: The UAE has committed to investing Dh550 million over the next decade to construct up to 10 hospitals worldwide as part of its Global Hospitals Programme, starting with a medical center in Indonesia. This initiative, part of the Zayed Humanitarian Legacy Initiative, aims to promote global health equity and provide specialized medical care in underserved areas. Additional efforts include supporting health services in conflict zones and establishing facilities like a cardiovascular center in Cairo and field hospitals in Chad and Gaza.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: During a state visit to the UAE, Indonesian President Joko Widodo and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed engaged in significant talks...
records.description: During a state visit to the UAE, Indonesian President Joko Widodo and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed engaged in significant talks, resulting in the signing of several agreements aimed at enhancing cooperation in areas such as the environment, tourism, and renewable energy. The meeting, a culmination of sustained efforts to deepen ties between the two nations, addressed expanding economic partnerships and joint initiatives in combating climate change and improving global education. The visit, marking the end of President Widodo's final term, also saw him receiving the Order of Zayed, the highest civilian honor in the UAE, recognizing his contributions to strengthening bilateral relations. Additional agreements included collaborations in solar energy, nuclear energy, public budget management, and smart banking systems, alongside plans for a new research center and real estate and tourism projects.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.description: G.D. Foods Manufacturing (India) served as the official condiment partner at the 4th edition of the India-GCC Buyers-Sellers Meet (BSM) on Food & Beverage in Dubai, offering a key platform for Indian exporters in the sector. This event, held over two days, gathered a delegation of 35 to 40 Indian food and beverage exporters and connected them with about 150 top distributors, importers, buyers, and retail outlets from GCC countries including Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE. G.D. Foods showcased an extensive range of products from its TOPS brand, which includes items such as ketchup, culinary sauces, pickles, and more. The participation aimed to enhance the visibility of Indian culinary tastes globally and establish significant business relationships within the FMCG sector.
records.institution: G.D. Foods Manufacturing (India)

records.title: The UAE and Indonesia have strengthened their cooperation by signing eight agreements during a state visit by the Indonesian President to...
records.description: The UAE and Indonesia have strengthened their cooperation by signing eight agreements during a state visit by the Indonesian President to the UAE. These agreements span various sectors, including the installation of solar energy systems, public budget management, smart banking systems, peaceful nuclear energy use, and environmental research with the establishment of a mangrove research center. Additionally, there are agreements related to financial cooperation, real estate development, tourism investment, and maritime security. This collaboration is part of the broader Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), enhancing bilateral relations in priority areas such as economy, renewable energy, food security, infrastructure, health, and climate action. This partnership has already seen a significant increase in non-oil trade between the two countries, rising from $2.7 billion in 2014 to $4.4 billion in 2023, with further investments valued at over $21 billion in 2023 alone.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: The Saudi General Food Security Authority has distributed US$78.7 million to local wheat farmers for the 2024 season, rewarding 792 farme...
records.description: The Saudi General Food Security Authority has distributed US$78.7 million to local wheat farmers for the 2024 season, rewarding 792 farmers for their combined delivery of 175,703 tonnes of wheat. This payout marks the first installment processed through the Mahsoly electronic platform. The initiative is part of a broader strategy authorized by the Cabinet, allowing the purchase of up to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat annually from local farmers over five years, aimed at bolstering domestic wheat production. This move is in line with Saudi Arabia's efforts to improve agricultural self-sufficiency and meet the food demands of its growing population and expanding economy. With a forecasted 25% increase in wheat production for the 2024-25 season, reaching 1.5 million tonnes, the country adapts its agricultural practices based on environmental factors and global market conditions. This strategy includes competitive pricing to encourage wheat cultivation over alfalfa hay, anticipating a continuation of last year's price of US$467 per tonne. As domestic consumption is expected to rise by 5% to 4.75 million tonnes, driven by a booming tourism sector, Saudi Arabia is preparing to meet increasing food demands with higher imports of essential grains.
records.institution: Saudi General Food Security Authority

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has expanded its partnership with Spinneys and Circa Biotech to reduce food...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has expanded its partnership with Spinneys and Circa Biotech to reduce food waste by transforming it into agricultural feed using black soldier fly larvae. During a trial in Abu Dhabi, Spinneys successfully reduced landfill-bound food waste by 54 percent, redirecting it instead to Circa Biotech where it was converted into nutritious animal feed, organic fertilizers, and sustainable biofuel.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: In Rakhyut, Dhofar Governorate, a series of training programs aimed at increasing camel milk production and its derivatives has been laun...
records.description: In Rakhyut, Dhofar Governorate, a series of training programs aimed at increasing camel milk production and its derivatives has been launched through a collaboration between the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). The initiatives are designed to empower productive families in the Niyabat of Asa’ib, with a focus on financial management and enhancing the skills of women camel breeders. Dhofar Governorate, where 60% of Oman's camels are located, is set to benefit significantly from these programs. Targeting 20% of rural women in the Wilayat of Rakhyut.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources & Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: A partnership between NEOM and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) focuses on combating the threat posed by insect...
records.description: A partnership between NEOM and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) focuses on combating the threat posed by insects to Saudi Arabia's extensive palm tree population, which numbers around 36 million. This collaboration utilizes advanced optical fiber sensing technology developed by AK-Sens, a startup from KAUST, aiming for early detection of harmful pests like the red palm weevil. Initial trials show promising results, achieving high accuracy in detecting infestations quickly across large numbers of trees.
records.institution: Topian

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Thailand are stepping up their collaborative efforts in the realms of environment and food security, as evidenced by a r...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Thailand are stepping up their collaborative efforts in the realms of environment and food security, as evidenced by a recent high-level meeting in Riyadh. Saudi Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Eng. Abdulrahman Alfadley, and Thai Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maris Sangiampongsa, discussed ways to enhance bilateral relations, focusing specifically on food security, livestock sector development, environmental cooperation, and increasing vegetation cover. The meeting, which included key officials like the Governor of the General Food Security Authority and the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Development, aimed to deepen cooperation and share expertise in critical sectors to mutually benefit both nations in sustainable development and food production.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has committed $46 million to construct a state-of-the-art veterinary laboratory in Riyadh, designed to advance the developme...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has committed $46 million to construct a state-of-the-art veterinary laboratory in Riyadh, designed to advance the development and production of vaccines targeting local disease strains in animals. This initiative, part of a broader strategy to boost local veterinary capabilities, will focus on disease diagnosis, vaccine development, and the localization of these vaccines to address region-specific animal health challenges. The facility aims to enhance the control and prevention of animal diseases through sophisticated diagnostic tools, including DNA sequencing, and will also support the creation of vaccines derived from local microbial strains.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has introduced a financial reward program designed to support and retain professional fishermen, offering up to SR54,000 (ap...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced a financial reward program designed to support and retain professional fishermen, offering up to SR54,000 (approximately $15,000) to those who meet specific criteria. Managed by the Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Programme (Reef), the initiative targets Saudis with a valid fishing license who are actively engaged in fishing and are not employed in any other public or private sector jobs. Eligible participants must be at least 18 years old and reside in Saudi Arabia during the support period. Each fishing expedition must last a minimum of six hours. The program also provides financial aid during times when fishermen are unable to sail due to adverse weather, security measures, or maritime accidents, as well as compensation for injuries that temporarily prevent fishing.
records.institution: Saudi Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Programme (Reef)

These projects, announced through the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture's FURAS portal, aim to bolster domestic production and reduce reliance on imported food, aligning with the Kingdom's Vision 2030 goals. The initiatives include the development of orchards, coffee cultivation, and the production of flowers and wild plants, emphasizing the strategic importance of these ventures in boosting agricultural productivity. Key projects include a coffee city with the capacity to cultivate over 150,000 trees and an Al-Ennab Village project focused on palm and fruit trees, among others.

This program, part of the Reef Saudi initiative, aims to develop the fisheries industry and enhance the livelihoods of small fishermen and rural families by increasing productivity and ensuring food security. Aligned with Vision 2030, the program will bolster the local economy and support the sustainable development of the fisheries sector. This includes modernizing infrastructure, such as ports on the Red Sea and Arabian Gulf, and providing concessional loans for equipment purchases. Eligible fishermen must hold a valid fishing license, not be employed in other sectors, be at least 18 years old, and reside in the Kingdom.

records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture recently conducted a comprehensive review of renewable water resources and their economic utilization during a workshop at its headquarters in Riyadh. This initiative aimed to refine strategies for water supply and demand management across all regions. The event, part of the UN high-level political forum, attracted leading global experts who deliberated on strategies to reduce carbon footprints in urban environments, a crucial step toward achieving global sustainable development goals. Discussions emphasized the need for integrating sustainable practices into urban planning and development to foster environmentally friendly cities that align with the 'Urgent Green Actions for Global Agenda 2030.' Highlights included insights from distinguished speakers who shared innovative approaches to sustainable urban development, including the use of renewable energy and education on climate resilience.

records.title: Dubai to Develop ‘World’s Largest’ Fresh Food Hub
records.description: Dubai has announced its plan to develop what is described as "the world's largest" logistics center for fresh food, significantly expanding its current fruit and vegetable market in collaboration with DP World. This initiative, part of the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33), aims to double the emirate's economy to $8.7 trillion by 2033 and reinforce its status as a global hub for trade. The project, which will connect to international markets, is designed to enhance Dubai’s capacity in the global food trade sector, particularly in the handling and distribution of fruits and vegetables. This expansion is expected to create substantial commercial and investment opportunities, leveraging Dubai's strategic location and advanced infrastructure to attract global companies and integrate them into its economic projects.
records.institution: Dubai Municipality & DP World

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has introduced a resolution to regulate food and fodder sampling for control...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has introduced a resolution to regulate food and fodder sampling for control and inspection purposes, ensuring the safety and quality of food products within Abu Dhabi. This resolution, issued by the Director General of ADAFSA, Saeed Al Bahri Salem Al Ameri, classifies samples into two categories: objective samples for routine checks and selective samples for identifying violations or detailed lab analysis. It stipulates precise requirements for the sampling process, including methods of collection, packaging, transportation, and storage to preserve sample integrity for chemical or bacteriological analysis. Furthermore, the resolution outlines procedures for re-analysis if initial results are unsatisfactory, allowing establishments to request additional tests at their expense in neutral, accredited laboratories.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Saudi Arabia has initiated several substantial environmental and water infrastructure projects to enhance sustainability across the region.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has initiated several substantial environmental and water infrastructure projects to enhance sustainability across the region. Key among these is the Rayyis and Rabigh Independent Water Transmission Pipeline Project, with a capacity of 500,000 cubic meters per day and an estimated cost of 2.4 billion riyals. This project is notable for its private sector involvement and innovative design, which facilitates bi-directional water transmission, ensuring a steady water supply to the Makkah and Madinah regions. Additionally, the Yanbu Independent Water Production Project, costing 3.3 billion riyals, will provide 450,000 cubic meters of drinking water daily using advanced reverse osmosis technology powered by solar energy. These initiatives, spearheaded by the Saudi Water Partnership Company, highlight the nation's commitment to developing sustainable infrastructure and utilizing renewable energy in water production, with completion targeted for early 2026.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia recently concluded its two-year presidency of the 36th session of the Committee on Fisheries (COFI36) of the UN Food and Agr...
records.description: Saudi Arabia recently concluded its two-year presidency of the 36th session of the Committee on Fisheries (COFI36) of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), showcasing its contributions to the fisheries sector. This session, held in Rome, Italy, was chaired by Saudi Arabia's Permanent Representative at the FAO, with participation from over 19 ministers and more than 300 delegates from FAO member states. The FAO Director-General commended Saudi Arabia for its significant efforts in promoting sustainable practices within the fisheries sector. The presidency focused on implementing prior recommendations and enhancing member state performance in fisheries management and aquaculture development. Saudi Arabia facilitated discussions on adhering to responsible fishing practices and expanding aquaculture, underlining the sector's importance in sustainable economic growth and environmental conservation.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has initiated the "Harvest Season" campaign to enhance public awareness about the benefits of consuming locally produced fruits and to improve the marketing effectiveness for the support of local farmers. Announced on a Wednesday, this campaign is part of broader efforts to promote healthier lifestyles through the consumption of local produce and to educate the public on the nutritional benefits of various fruits available throughout the year. The campaign also aims to support the production and quality of local goods, increase awareness of agricultural products, and assist in the marketing of these products, thereby boosting farmer incomes.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.description: The UAE and Japan recently held discussions to enhance cooperation in food security and climate-smart agriculture as part of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Initiative (CSPI). The meeting, between UAE's Minister of Climate Change and Environment and Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, focused on expanding collaboration in agriculture, fisheries, and sustainable practices. They discussed technology transfer, innovative agricultural techniques, and shared priorities for COP29.

records.title: The Agricultural Research Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has achieved significant advancements in agricultural technology...
records.description: The Agricultural Research Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has achieved significant advancements in agricultural technology, notably using gamma rays to develop new vegetable varieties that are well-suited to Qatar's environmental conditions. According to the director of the department, this innovative technique has led to promising research and production outcomes, including the imminent introduction of a new tomato variety. Additionally, the department has enhanced meat and dairy production by developing and utilizing advanced fodders adapted to local conditions. These fodders have significantly increased production levels over traditional options. The department's efforts extend to the cultivation of Al Labid fodder, which is both water-efficient and climate-resilient, marking a crucial step towards sustainable livestock management and water resource conservation in Qatar. Moreover, the department's research stations have incorporated cutting-edge technology like climate-controlled greenhouses and automated fertilization systems, furthering efficiency in water and fertilizer use through sophisticated hydroponics systems.
records.institution: Omani Agricultural Research Department at the Ministry of Municipality

records.title: Agthia Group, a UAE-based food and beverages company, has expanded its operations into Saudi Arabia with the opening of a Dhs 90 million...
records.description: Agthia Group, a UAE-based food and beverages company, has expanded its operations into Saudi Arabia with the opening of a Dhs 90 million protein manufacturing facility in Jeddah’s Industrial City 1. This new facility, spanning over 9,000 square meters with an annual production capacity of over 9,000 tonnes, is designed to meet growing demand for Agthia’s protein brands in the GCC's largest market. Equipped with advanced production lines, in-house labs for microbiology and sensory evaluation, and a supply chain supporting over 69 raw materials, the facility is poised to capitalize on the processed meat market in Saudi Arabia, which is expected to reach $7.11 billion by the end of the decade. This strategic expansion aims to enhance Agthia’s market presence, solidify its position in the region, and contribute to the diversification of its product portfolio. The company has also reported a significant increase in quarterly revenue and profit, despite economic challenges, underscoring its successful growth strategy.
records.institution: Agthia

records.title: In Saudi Arabia, a new cooperative insurance scheme was introduced by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture to mitigate eco...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia, a new cooperative insurance scheme was introduced by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture to mitigate economic losses caused by plant pests and animal diseases. This initiative, launched under the National Transformation Program and operated by the Weqaa Center, aims to bolster the sustainability of the agricultural sector. The insurance model focuses on a cooperative and solidarity-based approach that considers the humanitarian and social needs of the agricultural community, including farmers and livestock breeders. It seeks to shield agricultural producers from financial setbacks and promote investment in the sector by reducing the risks associated with agricultural production.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: FarmERP, a leader in sustainable technology solutions for agriculture, has announced a partnership with Saudi Arabian tech company Seiyaj...
records.description: FarmERP, a leader in sustainable technology solutions for agriculture, has announced a partnership with Saudi Arabian tech company Seiyaj Tech to enhance its presence and impact in Saudi Arabia's agricultural sector. This strategic collaboration, formalized by a Memorandum of Understanding in Riyadh, leverages Seiyaj Tech’s extensive network and expertise in localizing green energy technologies. The alliance aims to address the unique agricultural challenges of Saudi Arabia, such as extreme weather and water scarcity, by providing advanced technological solutions to boost productivity, profitability, and sustainability.
records.institution: FarmERP

records.title: Saudi Arabia has opened bidding for the construction of a "coffee city" in the Qalwah Governorate of the Al-Baha Region, as part of its e...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has opened bidding for the construction of a "coffee city" in the Qalwah Governorate of the Al-Baha Region, as part of its efforts to boost local coffee production under the Saudi Vision 2030 initiative. Spanning over 5.5 million square meters, this ambitious project aims to augment the existing coffee sector by adding 300,000 trees. The initiative reflects the kingdom's broader strategy to localize production and expand its agricultural footprint. Currently, Saudi Arabia is among the top ten nations globally in coffee consumption and has significant coffee farming activities primarily in Jizan, Aseer, and Al Baha. The deadline for bid submissions is set for 9 September 2024, with reviews to follow immediately. This development is backed by substantial investment, including a significant allocation from the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund to elevate coffee production to new heights by 2030.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s largest dairy company, Almarai, reported a 6% decline in Q2 revenue for 2024, dropping to SAR 5.2 billion from SAR 5.46 bi...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s largest dairy company, Almarai, reported a 6% decline in Q2 revenue for 2024, dropping to SAR 5.2 billion from SAR 5.46 billion the previous year, largely due to seasonal consumption shifts. This also resulted in a 10% decrease in Q2 net profit, amounting to SAR 620 million. However, the company's performance for the first half of 2024 remains positive, with an 8% increase in revenue to SAR 10.6 billion and a 10% rise in net profit to SAR 1.31 billion, driven by solid volume growth in dairy and poultry and effective cost controls. Despite the challenging quarter, Almarai anticipates continued growth throughout 2024, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions. Additionally, Almarai has launched the "Almarai Chefs Program" in collaboration with the Social Development Bank to support small cooking projects in Riyadh, aiming to enhance the contributions of emerging entrepreneurs to the Saudi food sector and promote sustainable business growth.
records.institution: Almarai

records.description: In Jazan, a region in southwest Saudi Arabia renowned as the Kingdom’s fruit basket, a concerted effort is underway to bolster sustainable coffee production. Over 2,000 coffee farms operate in Jazan, collectively producing over 1,000 tons of coffee annually. The National Center for the Prevention and Control of Plant Pests and Animal Diseases, known as "Weqa," alongside relevant authorities, recently held a workshop aimed at expanding the number of coffee trees and enhancing sustainable cultivation practices in the area. The workshop brought together government and private sector stakeholders to align efforts and introduce innovative agricultural practices.

records.title: In Saudi Arabia, a strategic shift toward renewable energy is underway as the nation aims to source half of its electricity from renewabl...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia, a strategic shift toward renewable energy is underway as the nation aims to source half of its electricity from renewables by 2030. This transition is part of the broader Vision 2030 initiative, which seeks to diversify the economy and reduce carbon emissions. Significant investments have been made in both wind and solar energy, with major projects across the country. The wind energy sector has seen the development of the Middle East's largest wind farm, while the solar sector is expanding with several large-scale projects aiming to capitalize on the country’s abundant sunlight. Additionally, the country is exploring other renewable sources like bioenergy, geothermal, and small-scale hydroelectric power to further its sustainability goals.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Energy

records.title: SABIC Agri-Nutrients has announced a significant development in Saudi Arabia with the launch of a new blue ammonia project in Jubail Indu...
records.description: SABIC Agri-Nutrients has announced a significant development in Saudi Arabia with the launch of a new blue ammonia project in Jubail Industrial City. This initiative, supported by an allocation of feedstock from the Ministry of Energy, aims to produce 1.2 million metric tons per annum (MMTA) of low-carbon ammonia, along with 1.1 MMTA of urea and specialized agricultural nutrients. The project aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, focusing on clean energy production and export. SABIC Agri-Nutrients will conduct engineering studies to identify and implement the most efficient technologies for energy and feedstock utilization, marking a crucial step towards enhancing the kingdom’s position in the global clean energy sector.
records.institution: SABIC Agri-Nutrients

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Romania have signed a memorandum of understanding to bolster agricultural cooperation, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Romania have signed a memorandum of understanding to bolster agricultural cooperation, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's national goals. This agreement, established between the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture and the Romanian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, focuses on enhancing economic support in agriculture and rural development. The collaboration will leverage modern technologies to boost agricultural production and improve the management of animal and plant resources. Key areas of this partnership include advancing livestock breeding, promoting animal health, achieving food security, and ensuring sustainable economic growth. Additionally, the agreement aims to increase the trade of agricultural products and collaborate on agricultural research, with particular emphasis on field crops, plant varieties, and modern beekeeping technology.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: In response to increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices, Saudi Arabia has established the Saudi Alliance for Agricultural...
records.description: In response to increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices, Saudi Arabia has established the Saudi Alliance for Agricultural and Food Technologies. This new coalition, consisting of forty public and private entities, aims to enhance the nation's food supply chain. Launched in Riyadh by the deputy minister at the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the alliance includes notable founding partners such as the Research, Development and Innovation Authority, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, and Topian—a food subsidiary of NEOM. This initiative seeks to foster collaboration across the agricultural and food technology sectors, aiming to preserve natural resources and ensure sustainable water and food security.

records.description: Saudi Arabia has established a new agency dedicated to advancing agricultural and food technologies. This initiative aims to enhance the nation's agricultural sector through the adoption of cutting-edge technologies, improving both efficiency and productivity. The new body will focus on fostering innovation in food production methods, ensuring sustainability, and enhancing food security, aligning with the broader goals of Saudi Vision 2030. This move is part of Saudi Arabia's ongoing efforts to diversify its economy and reduce its dependence on oil by investing in and modernizing its agricultural sector.

records.description: Abu Dhabi-based Ghitha Holding, through its subsidiary Al Ain Farms, has completed the acquisition of Arabian Farms Investments LLC for $65.3 million, securing all of the company's assets in both the UAE and Saudi Arabia. This acquisition, which is part of a strategic expansion, is subject to regulatory approvals and conditions outlined in the share purchase agreement. Arabian Farms, renowned for its Saha brand of poultry products, adds to Ghitha Holding's diverse portfolio, which spans food, agriculture, and more, across various regions. The deal reflects Ghitha's aggressive growth strategy, which has already seen substantial revenue increases and expansion into new markets and product categories.
records.institution: Ghitha Holding

records.title: Alila Jabal Akhdar, a luxury hotel situated at 2000 meters in the Hajar mountains of Oman, has inaugurated the country's first hydroponic...
records.description: Alila Jabal Akhdar, a luxury hotel situated at 2000 meters in the Hajar mountains of Oman, has inaugurated the country's first hydroponic farm within a hotel setting, marking a significant advancement in sustainable hospitality. This hydroponic initiative, which began earlier this year, involves a soil-free cultivation method that uses nutrient-rich water, allowing for the year-round, rapid growth of fruits and vegetables like lettuces, strawberries, and cucumbers. The farm not only enhances the guest experience by offering fresh, tailor-made dining directly from garden to table but also emphasizes the hotel's commitment to sustainability. This project, which is set to expand in its second phase, also aims to support the local community by providing jobs and educational tours to inspire sustainable practices. With this venture, Alila Jabal Akhdar reinforces its dedication to eco-conscious luxury, integrating various sustainability initiatives across its operations.
records.institution: Alila Jabal Akhdar

records.title: Oman is advancing a draft law on Personal Income Tax (PIT), aimed at high earners, to the State Council as part of its efforts to diversi...
records.description: Oman is advancing a draft law on Personal Income Tax (PIT), aimed at high earners, to the State Council as part of its efforts to diversify its economic policies and reduce reliance on oil revenues. This proposed tax, introduced first in 2022, would levy rates between 5% and 9% on high income levels, distinguishing between foreign nationals and Omani citizens based on income thresholds. Currently, Oman's tax system focuses primarily on corporate income and withholding taxes for non-residents. The move to introduce PIT aligns with the country's Medium-Term Fiscal Plan (2020-2024) and marks a significant shift in fiscal policy, potentially impacting high-earning expatriates and wealthy Omani citizens. This legislative progression is part of broader discussions that include enhancing vocational education and adjusting VAT policies for new homeowners.
records.institution: Omani Shura Council

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi Arabian halal food brand, has attained the esteemed AA+ rating from the BRCGS International Certi...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi Arabian halal food brand, has attained the esteemed AA+ rating from the BRCGS International Certification for its poultry facility, marking a significant milestone in the food industry. This recognition underscores Tanmiah’s commitment to upholding superior food safety and quality standards, distinguishing it as a leader in the sector. The BRCGS Global Standard for Food Safety, recognized worldwide, mandates rigorous safety and quality protocols. Tanmiah's achievement as the first fresh chicken producer in Saudi Arabia to receive an AA+ rating during an unannounced audit reflects its consistent adherence to these stringent standards. The unannounced audits assess the facility's daily operations and adherence to critical areas including food safety management, site standards, product control, and personnel hygiene, emphasizing Tanmiah's dedication to excellence.
records.institution: Tanmiah Food Company

records.title: Iyris, previously known as RedSea, has announced an exclusive distribution agreement with Sherwood Middle East, a prominent agricultural...
records.description: Iyris, previously known as RedSea, has announced an exclusive distribution agreement with Sherwood Middle East, a prominent agricultural supplies distributor and subsidiary of Silal, to promote its SecondSky greenhouse covers in the UAE. This agreement marks a significant expansion for Sherwood, now the exclusive distributor of SecondSky in the region. SecondSky covers are designed to block near-infrared heat radiation, which significantly reduces energy consumption by over 40%, cuts water use by 30%, and boosts profitability by 28%. These covers are set to transform farming operations in the UAE by enhancing yield, quality, and profit margins, particularly suited for the region's hot climate.

records.title: Oman has experienced a remarkable 300% increase in wheat production over the past five years, culminating in a harvest of 7,119 tonnes du...
records.description: Oman has experienced a remarkable 300% increase in wheat production over the past five years, culminating in a harvest of 7,119 tonnes during the 2022/2023 agricultural season. This growth reflects the nation's commitment to agricultural productivity and food security, driven by strategic government initiatives and partnerships with academic institutions. The introduction of high-yielding, stress-resistant wheat genotypes and the expansion of cultivated areas have played critical roles in this success. The government's backing has been crucial in addressing challenges like water scarcity and labor shortages. Innovations such as super-absorbent biopolymers for soil moisture retention and advanced seed priming techniques have further enhanced wheat resilience against drought and climate variations.
records.institution: Agricultural and Marine Sciences Department at Sultan Qaboos University

records.title: Dubai Approves $6.8 Billion FDI Program to Attract $176.96 Billion in Investments by 2033
records.description: Dubai has launched a significant $6.8 billion Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Development Program, aimed at attracting approximately $176.96 billion in investments by 2033 to establish itself as one of the world’s top three urban economies. This initiative is part of a broader economic strategy that includes the introduction of new economic models and incentive programs to attract international businesses and support the expansion of existing ones. Alongside economic development, Dubai is also focusing on urban planning enhancements around Metro stations to improve public transport efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. Additionally, the Executive Council has approved social and cultural programs like the 'Manbar' and 'Ghras Al Khair' to promote national identity and societal values. These combined efforts are designed to fortify Dubai’s position as a global commercial hub and an attractive destination for living and working.
records.institution: The Executive Council of Dubai

records.title: Turkmenistan and the UAE have seen a notable 15.8 percent increase in their trade turnover, reaching $1.29 billion last year, according t...
records.description: Turkmenistan and the UAE have seen a notable 15.8 percent increase in their trade turnover, reaching $1.29 billion last year, according to Deputy Minister Kerimberdi Kurbanov of Turkmenistan's Ministry of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations. This growth reflects a 13.3 percent rise in Turkmenistan's exports to the UAE and a 16.2 percent increase in imports from the UAE. The trade is predominantly driven by Turkmenistan's chemical products, fuel and energy sectors, and agricultural goods exported to the UAE, while imports consist largely of metallurgical products, vehicles, and machinery. This development underscores both nations' commitment to expanding economic cooperation through mutual investments, trade diversification, and joint projects in energy, infrastructure, and digital sectors, aimed at fostering sustainable economic growth and enhancing international partnerships.
records.institution: Turkmenistani Ministry of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations

records.title: Saudi Arabia has shown keen interest in importing 200,000 tonnes of red meat and one million tonnes of soybeans annually from Nigeria, ac...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has shown keen interest in importing 200,000 tonnes of red meat and one million tonnes of soybeans annually from Nigeria, according to Agriculture Minister Mohammad Abubakar. This move comes as Nigeria aims to diversify its exports away from its dominant oil and gas sectors, seeking to bolster foreign exchange earnings amidst dollar shortages that have impacted its economy. The discussions followed a visit by Saudi Arabia's agriculture minister to Nigeria, where meetings with local agribusiness leaders paved the way for Saudi Arabia's expression of interest. Abubakar highlighted that Nigeria has outlined a roadmap to meet Saudi Arabia's demand, signaling a significant step in bilateral trade relations between the two countries.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Tetra Pak has announced a significant partnership with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) through...
records.description: Tetra Pak has announced a significant partnership with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) through its commercial arm, Ektifa, to equip the Meliha Dairy Factory with advanced processing and filling solutions. Located in the UAE, Meliha Dairy Factory is the country’s first farm integrating authentic organic production methods. Tetra Pak’s collaboration will introduce state-of-the-art processing equipment and sustainable filling lines, including the innovative Tetra Top Filling Line, which offers recyclable packaging solutions for chilled products, yogurt, and still drinks. This initiative underscores Sharjah’s commitment to environmental sustainability and local organic dairy production, enhancing production efficiency and product quality while minimizing environmental impact.
records.institution: Tetra Pak

records.title: Tetra Pak has partnered with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock and its commercial arm, Ektifa, to enhan...
records.description: Tetra Pak has partnered with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock and its commercial arm, Ektifa, to enhance the Meliha Dairy Factory in the UAE with cutting-edge processing and sustainable packaging solutions. The partnership underscores Sharjah's commitment to sustainable agriculture and aligns with Tetra Pak’s expertise in providing comprehensive, environmentally friendly production capabilities. This initiative not only promises to boost production efficiency and reduce environmental impact but also supports the production of organic, locally sourced dairy products, advancing the region's focus on authentic organic production methods.

records.description: ACWA Power, the Water and Electricity Holding Company (Badeel), and Saudi Aramco Power Company (SAPCO) have inked power purchase agreements (PPAs) with the Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC) for three substantial solar photovoltaic (PV) projects in Saudi Arabia. records.title: Saudi Arabia has launched the Supervisory Council for the Ibex protected area, marking a significant stride in wildlife conservation and...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched the Supervisory Council for the Ibex protected area, marking a significant stride in wildlife conservation and community involvement. Spearheaded by the Saudi National Center for Wildlife (NCW) in collaboration with the Riyadh Region Emirate, this initiative aims to enhance management practices and preserve biodiversity within the 1841 square kilometers Ibex protected area in southern Saudi Arabia. The council's formation emphasizes local community engagement, aligning with global standards of conservation that promote sustainable use of natural resources and foster environmental awareness among residents. The area, renowned for its diverse wildlife and unique geological features, offers ecotourism opportunities such as camping, hiking, and beekeeping, contributing to local economic growth while safeguarding the region's natural and cultural heritage. Saudi Arabia's commitment to conservation through initiatives like the Ibex Supervisory Council reflects its adherence to Vision 2030 goals and sets a precedent for future conservation efforts nationwide.
records.institution: Saudi National Center for Wildlife (NCW)

records.title: BEAM Launches Initiatives for Graduates of Creative Science Schools

records.title: Osool Poultry Company has entered into a strategic collaboration with Aviagen, a renowned U.S.-based poultry industry expert, to launch a...
records.description: Osool Poultry Company has entered into a strategic collaboration with Aviagen, a renowned U.S.-based poultry industry expert, to launch a groundbreaking OMR10 million (US$26 million) poultry project in Oman named ‘Jaddat’ (mother hens). This project aims to establish local production of fertilized eggs and high-quality chicks, significantly enhancing Oman’s poultry industry’s self-sufficiency and reducing dependence on imported one-day-old chicks, which currently support Osool’s annual production capacity of 150 million eggs. The initiative will leverage Aviagen’s extensive technical expertise and support, focusing on advanced production technologies to improve product quality and operational efficiency.
records.institution: Osool Poultry Company & Aviagen

records.title: The Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA) has approved Arabian Mills Company for Food Products to list 15.4 million shares, representing 3...
records.description: The Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA) has approved Arabian Mills Company for Food Products to list 15.4 million shares, representing 30% of its total shares, on the Tawadul stock exchange. This move aligns with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, aimed at economic diversification away from oil revenues. Arabian Mills, formerly the Second Mills Company, operates three mills in Riyadh, Jazan, and Hail, with a daily flour production capacity of around 4,920 tons. The IPO approval underscores Saudi Arabia’s commitment to privatization and market reforms, following the successful IPO of the Modern Mills Company earlier in the year, which raised US$314.6 million.
records.institution: Saudi Arabian Mills

records.title: Vietnam has successfully exported dragon fruit with red and yellow flesh to Saudi Arabia for the first time, marking a significant milest...
records.description: Vietnam has successfully exported dragon fruit with red and yellow flesh to Saudi Arabia for the first time, marking a significant milestone in bilateral trade. The fruit debuted at Spinneys, a prestigious UAE-based supermarket chain, during its recent opening. Vietnamese Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dang Xuan Dung, highlighted the growing presence of Vietnamese agricultural products in the kingdom and expressed optimism for expanding the range of Vietnamese goods at Spinneys. He pledged the embassy's support in facilitating connections between the supermarket and Vietnamese exporters, aiming to foster increased trade between Vietnam and Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Spinneys

records.title: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi-based renewables company, is set to expand significantly in the United States, aiming to grow 'more than tenfold' w...
records.description: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi-based renewables company, is set to expand significantly in the United States, aiming to grow 'more than tenfold' within the next three to seven years. Philip Haddad, president and CEO of Masdar Americas LLC, outlined ambitious plans to invest in development and operational platforms, emphasizing the US as pivotal to Masdar's goal of achieving a global renewable energy portfolio of at least 100 gigawatts by 2030. The company recently announced the acquisition of a 50% stake in Terra-Gen, a major US-based independent renewable energy producer, and continues to strengthen its presence with strategic investments like the acquisition of California-based solar and battery storage project, Big Beau. Masdar's expansion underscores its role as a key player in advancing sustainable energy solutions internationally, supported by its ownership under Abu Dhabi-listed ADNOC, TAQA, and sovereign investor Mubadala.
records.institution: Masdar

records.title: The UAE’s Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the Republic of Georgia has officially come into effect, marking a sig...
records.description: The UAE’s Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the Republic of Georgia has officially come into effect, marking a significant milestone in bilateral economic relations. This agreement aims to enhance trade cooperation by eliminating or reducing customs duties on 95 percent of tariff lines, covering more than 90 percent of non-oil bilateral trade. It is expected to more than triple the total value of non-oil trade between the UAE and Georgia to $1.5 billion within five years, contributing $3.9 billion to the UAE’s GDP and $291 million to Georgia’s GDP by 2031. The CEPA also anticipates boosting UAE exports to Georgia to $1.3 billion by 2031, benefiting sectors such as refined sugar, electrical appliances, vehicles, polymers, and machinery. This move solidifies the UAE’s position as Georgia’s leading trading partner in the Arab world and aims to accelerate bilateral investment across various key sectors, fostering economic growth and strengthening ties between the two nations.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: UAE: New Guidelines for Public-Private Partnerships, Sandbox Conditions Regulation
records.description: The UAE has introduced two significant regulatory frameworks aimed at enhancing its business ecosystem: the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Manual and the Sandbox Conditions regulation. Approved by the UAE Cabinet, the PPP Manual establishes guidelines for federal government entities to collaborate effectively with the private sector on developmental projects. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and the efficient utilization of private sector capabilities to achieve societal and economic benefits. Concurrently, the Sandbox Conditions regulation, introduced by the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), aims to attract global fintech companies and startups by providing a structured environment to test innovative financial products and services. Both initiatives underscore the UAE's commitment to fostering innovation, driving economic growth, and optimizing public-private collaborations across key sectors such as infrastructure, energy, healthcare, and finance.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Finance

records.title: Osool Poultry Company has signed an agreement with Aviagen (Ross) to establish a major poultry project named “Jaddat” (mother hens), with...
records.description: Osool Poultry Company has signed an agreement with Aviagen (Ross) to establish a major poultry project named “Jaddat” (mother hens), with an investment of OMR10 million. Aviagen will provide full technical support for the project, which aims to enhance food security and achieve self-sufficiency in Oman by meeting the country's chicken needs and reducing imports. The project will produce fertilized eggs, quality chicks, and other poultry products, reducing the risks associated with poultry imports. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources supports the poultry industry by transferring global knowledge, training Omani cadres, and promoting food security.
records.institution: Osool Poultry Company
