records.title: Abu Dhabi-based food company Agthia Group has witnessed a notable surge in its net profits, reaching US$71.06 million for 2023, marking a...
records.description: Abu Dhabi-based food company Agthia Group has witnessed a notable surge in its net profits, reaching US$71.06 million for 2023, marking a 16% increase from the previous year. This growth is attributed to the strong performance of the company's snacking and agri-business sections. Agthia Group, listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, operates through its consumer business and agribusiness segments, which include Grand Mills flour and Agrivita animal feed products. The company's revenue in the snacking vertical experienced a significant 38% year-on-year growth, fueled by robust value growth across retail channels in the UAE and internationally. Despite challenges such as currency headwinds in Egypt affecting the protein and frozen business, the overall group net revenue increased by 12.1% year-on-year to AED4.56 billion. This positive performance has led Agthia's board of directors to recommend a full-year cash dividend payment and bonus shares, reflecting the company's strong financial position and growth trajectory.
records.institution: Agthia Group

records.description: The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) unveiled plans to launch a $1 billion Fund of Fund (FoF) on February 24, aimed at investing in international venture capital firms across the Gulf region. This initiative targets sectors such as financial technology, education technology, and healthcare, with the goal of attracting global venture capital funds and startups to Qatar and neighboring Gulf countries. By providing dedicated capital for startups transitioning from seed rounds to Series A to C rounds, QIA seeks to bolster the startup ecosystem in Qatar, bridging the gap with neighboring economic powerhouses like Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Mansoor Ebrahim Al-Mahmoud, Chief of Qatar Investment Authority, emphasized the FoF's role in facilitating access to venture capital for innovative companies, enabling them to expand locally and internationally, thus contributing to Qatar's economic development and global competitiveness. With QIA's vast experience and substantial assets, including its extensive portfolio covering various sectors globally and its strategic partnerships with Chinese companies, the FoF represents a strategic move to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the region while strengthening ties with international markets.

Experts suggest that promising areas for business partnership encompass trade, transportation, communication, as well as industries like chemicals, textiles, agriculture, and the oil and gas sector. records.title: India's Commerce Ministry has approved the export of 64,400 tonnes of onions, with 50,000 tonnes allocated to Bangladesh and 14,400 tonne...
records.description: India's Commerce Ministry has approved the export of 64,400 tonnes of onions, with 50,000 tonnes allocated to Bangladesh and 14,400 tonnes to the UAE through the National Cooperative Exports Ltd (NCEL). The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) specified that the UAE would receive quarterly shipments of 3,600 metric tonnes. Despite a general ban on onion exports to stabilize domestic markets, exceptions were made for these nations upon their requests. The modalities for exports to Bangladesh will be determined by the NCEL in coordination with the department of consumer affairs. This decision follows an export ban implemented on December 8 of the previous year, aimed at improving local availability and controlling prices, set to expire on March 31.

records.description: Dubai Municipality's latest agricultural beautification endeavor at the intersection of Al Meydan and Al Khail Streets aims to enhance the city's aesthetics, sustainability, and green spaces across an extensive 302,266 square meter area. This ambitious project incorporates cutting-edge automated irrigation systems, eliminating the need for human intervention while ensuring efficient water usage. Under the leadership of H.E. Dawoud Al Hajri, Director General of Dubai Municipality, the initiative aligns with the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to position Dubai as a global leader in environmental sustainability. Drawing inspiration from horse hoof prints, the project's design integrates natural elements with carefully selected ornamental plants, creating a visually striking landscape. Notably, the introduction of Chorisia trees marks a significant addition to Dubai's biodiversity, underscoring the Municipality's commitment to implementing innovative and sustainable beautification projects that adhere to international standards and promote environmental stewardship.

records.title: Kenya and Saudi Arabia have forged a voluntary agreement on carbon credit deals to address land degradation issues, with Saudi Arabia's D...
records.description: Kenya and Saudi Arabia have forged a voluntary agreement on carbon credit deals to address land degradation issues, with Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister for Environment, Osama Faqeeha, emphasizing Kenya's strategic importance as a partner. However, carbon offsetting has sparked controversy in Kenya, with President William Ruto denying the signing of carbon credit deals with a Dubai-based company last year, although discussions were ongoing. The agreement aims to support Kenya's readiness for Article 6 of the Paris Agreement by generating carbon credits aligned with national climate targets. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia, aiming to have 50% of its energy mix from renewable and chemical sources by 2030, sees potential collaboration in carbon credits within a circular carbon economy framework. Despite Saudi Arabia's status as a polymer producer and opposition to global efforts to eliminate plastic pollution, Dr. Faqeeha stresses the importance of addressing land degradation, which threatens global stability and prosperity. He warns of the alarming rate of land degradation and its implications for Africa's GDP, highlighting the need for concerted efforts to mitigate this environmental challenge.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Emirates Flight Catering, a global leader in aviation hospitality, has completed the full acquisition of Bustanica, formerly known as Emi...
records.description: Emirates Flight Catering, a global leader in aviation hospitality, has completed the full acquisition of Bustanica, formerly known as Emirates Crop One, the world’s largest indoor vertical farm. Located adjacent to Al Maktoum International Airport at Dubai World Central, the 330,000sqft facility has an annual capacity of over 1 million kilograms of high-quality leafy greens, achieved with a remarkable 95% reduction in water usage compared to conventional agriculture. Bustanica's produce is available in major UAE retailers and served on Emirates flights, offering pristine greens cultivated without pesticides. The acquisition aims to bolster the UAE’s commitment to food and water security while showcasing local sustainability and innovation. With advanced technologies and a dedicated team, Bustanica exemplifies Emirates Flight Catering's dedication to excellence, innovation, and sustainability, contributing to a more resilient and self-sufficient food supply chain in the UAE.

records.description: Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia are set to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in environmental protection, wildlife preservation, and climate change mitigation. The decision emerged from a bilateral meeting between Bangladesh's Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Saber Hossain Chowdhury and Saudi Arabia's State Minister for Environment Dr. Osama Ibrahim Faqeeha during the UN Environment Assembly in Nairobi, Kenya. The MoU aims to enhance cooperation in various critical areas, including environmental protection, wildlife conservation, climate change mitigation, and pollution control. State Minister Faqeeha extended an invitation to Minister Chowdhury to attend the United Nations Convention on Desertification in December 2024, highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries in addressing global environmental challenges. Discussions during the meeting covered knowledge exchange programs, agricultural sustainability, mangrove conservation, waste management, smart city development, and strategies to combat land degradation, emphasizing the joint commitment of Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia to finding innovative solutions to environmental issues. Minister Chowdhury also highlighted Bangladesh's dedication to promoting environmental sustainability both domestically and internationally, showcasing initiatives like the Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan and the National Adaptation Plan aimed at addressing climate change.

records.description: South Africa and Saudi Arabia are forging a partnership aimed at significant agricultural exports, with South African Agriculture Minister Thoko Didiza highlighting Saudi Arabia's role as a pivotal market, annually importing around R380 billion (US$20 billion) worth of agricultural products. South Africa, aiming to expand domestic production on over two million hectares of underutilized land, sees Saudi Arabia as a crucial partner in deepening trade relations across various value chains. The recent negotiations on red meat exports have paved the way for expanded bilateral agricultural relations, with South African livestock industries now able to export to Saudi Arabia. Both nations envision a fruitful partnership with strengthened trade and investment relations, showcasing South Africa's high-quality agricultural products and presenting attractive investment opportunities. While Saudi Arabia's agricultural imports primarily come from other countries, South Africa's recent market access for beef exports to Saudi Arabia signifies a promising development, aligning with South Africa's ambition to expand its export markets while maintaining strong ties with existing partners.

The head of the Environment Authority, announced that Oman has initiated a series of renewable energy projects aimed at achieving 39% of its total energy production from clean sources by 2040. He highlighted the Oman Blue Carbon Project, which plans to plant 100 million mangrove trees to absorb 14 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalents, garnering significant global and scientific acclaim for its first update to the second nationally determined contribution report.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) announced on Feb.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) announced on Feb. 25 that it convened the first Korea-Qatar Smart Farm Cooperation Committee in Doha, Qatar, aiming to facilitate exchanges and cooperation in smart agriculture between the two nations following an MOU signed in October 2023. The Qatar-Korea Smart Farm Cooperation Committee, chaired by Lee Sang-man, an official from MAFRA, discussed smart agriculture policies, research collaboration, and joint technology demonstrations in smart farming. A proposal was made to establish an innovation valley in Qatar based on the Korean smart farm innovation valley model. MAFRA has been actively promoting domestic smart agriculture policies and is now focusing on expanding Korean smart farms overseas, particularly in countries like Qatar. Qatar, in line with its national food security strategy, is keen on adopting smart agriculture practices and plans to visit Korea to explore cooperation opportunities, including potential business forums between Qatar's Hassad Food and Korean companies. Hassad Food, an investment arm of the Qatar Investment Authority, aims to meet a significant portion of Qatar's food demand and is interested in collaborating with Korean entities. Lee emphasized the importance of international cooperation in smart agriculture and expressed MAFRA's commitment to supporting Korean smart farming technology's entry into promising export markets like the Middle East.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA)

records.title: In February 2024, Saudi Arabia achieved a significant milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, leveraging high...
records.description: In February 2024, Saudi Arabia achieved a significant milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, leveraging high-tech greenhouses and vertical farming techniques pioneered by Dava Agricultural Co. Founded in 2019 with a mission to ensure year-round agricultural production for food security, Dava's innovative approach enabled them to overcome the challenges posed by the nation's harsh climate and reliance on imports. With meticulous planning and support from governmental entities and CEO Mr. Faisal Al Batal's leadership, Dava successfully shipped 5 tonnes of premium tomatoes to Europe, marking the beginning of a promising export venture. Looking ahead, the company aims to expand its exports, diversify its product range, and establish a sister company dedicated to vegetable and fruit distribution, signaling Saudi Arabia's growing presence in the global agricultural market.
records.institution: Dava Agricultural Co.

records.title: Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abu Dhabi to enhance agricultural innovation an...
records.description: Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abu Dhabi to enhance agricultural innovation and research, specifically focusing on the development and promotion of various aspects of Date Palm cultivation and related industries. The signing ceremony was witnessed by the UAE's Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, H.E. Sheikh Nahyan Mubarak Al Nahyan. The MoU aims to foster joint cooperation and expertise-sharing between the two countries, offering Pakistani farmers opportunities to expand date palm cultivation through innovative approaches. With the UAE providing technological support, Pakistan aims to capitalize on its rich topography, which holds significant potential for date palm cultivation. Additionally, the agreement paves the way for organizing the First Pakistan International Date Palm Festival 2024. Pakistan and the UAE maintain a fraternal relationship and collaborate on various mutually beneficial projects spanning political, economic, agricultural, cultural, energy, and defense sectors.

records.title: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has initiated discussions with business delegations from Estonia and the Russian Fede...
records.description: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has initiated discussions with business delegations from Estonia and the Russian Federation to bolster investment cooperation in the agricultural sector. During a meeting between Abdullah Sultan Al Owais, Chairman of the SCCI, and Madis Kallas, Minister of Regional Affairs of Estonia, held at the SCCI's headquarters, various avenues for joint work and enhanced communication among the business communities of Sharjah and Estonia were explored. The focus was on leveraging mutual expertise and experience to ensure the success of agricultural projects and stimulate investment in this crucial sector. High-profile officials, including HE Mohammad Ahmed Amin Al Awadi, Director-General of the SCCI, and Abdul Aziz Al Shamsi, Assistant Director-General for Communication and Business Sector, attended the meeting. Al Owais reiterated the Chamber's commitment to supporting investment development in the agricultural sector, driven by Sharjah's strategic approach towards sustainable agricultural development and food security. The discussions with the Estonian delegation reaffirmed the Chamber's eagerness to tap into global agricultural expertise and broaden the base of companies in this sector, making Sharjah an attractive destination for agricultural investment. Additionally, Al Owais met with a delegation from Russia, led by Vitaly Stepanov, CEO of the Moscow Export Centre, to discuss cooperation and trade exchange in agriculture and food production, emphasizing the importance of achieving food security and participating in exhibitions dedicated to modern agricultural techniques. Meanwhile, the SCCI explored avenues for bolstering investment and fostering partnerships with an Indian delegation during the "Sharjah-India Business Forum," highlighting Sharjah's attractive investment climate and the opportunities it presents across various sectors. The forum shed light on the comprehensive economic partnership agreement between the UAE and India, aiming to expand cooperation, increase investments, and boost trade exchange volumes between the two nations. Al Owais emphasized the strong and growing economic and trade relations between India and the UAE, particularly with Sharjah, aiming to enhance bilateral trade volume and mutual investments for common interests.
records.institution: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI)

Dr. Masoud Jarallah Al Marri, Director of the Food Security Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality, highlighted the significance of this meeting in activating a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the two countries. The MoU aims to bolster the smart agriculture industry, foster agricultural research collaboration, and facilitate mutual cooperation guided by principles of equality and shared interests. Dr. Al Marri underscored ongoing collaboration within the Knowledge Program project, in partnership with the Korea Trade and Investment Promotion Agency, focusing on addressing climate change impacts on Qatar's food production. The project emphasizes enhancing production efficiency, resource utilization, and developing resilient crop varieties. He emphasized the importance of sharing successful Korean smart agriculture experiences, advocating for further projects, research, and knowledge exchange to fortify bilateral relations and advance agricultural practices.

Pascual, the Secretary for Trade and Industry of the Philippines, anticipates fruitful negotiations on fisheries subsidies, agriculture, and climate issues at the upcoming World Trade Organisation’s (WTO) 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) in Abu Dhabi. records.description: Bilateral discussions between Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica of Fiji and Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade of the UAE, primarily focused on economic growth, fisheries, agriculture, and e-commerce negotiations. These talks, held in preparation for the 13th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization (WTO) in Abu Dhabi, aimed to achieve substantive outcomes fostering inclusive and sustainable development. records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has reaffirmed its dedication to fostering a fair and sustainable global trading system by pledging a $10...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has reaffirmed its dedication to fostering a fair and sustainable global trading system by pledging a $10 million grant to support vital World Trade Organisation (WTO) initiatives. This announcement comes ahead of the WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13), which the UAE will host from February 26 to 29 in Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE Minister of Foreign Affairs, lauded the UAE's role as the host of MC13, welcoming leaders and representatives from 166 member states. Stressing the importance of collaborative negotiations to modernize global trade rules and promote sustainable economic growth, Sheikh Abdullah emphasized the significance of the grant in advancing key WTO programmes. The $10 million grant will be allocated to three critical initiatives: the Fisheries Funding Mechanism to promote sustainable fishing practices, the Enhanced Integrated Framework to support Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in utilizing trade for growth and poverty reduction, and the Women Exporters in the Digital Economy (WEIDE) Fund to empower women-led businesses in LDCs to access global markets through digitalization. These initiatives align with the UAE's strategic objectives of promoting sustainable development and fostering international partnerships. Sheikh Abdullah reiterated the UAE's commitment to expanding economic cooperation globally through its comprehensive economic partnership agreements programme. The MC13 conference is expected to serve as a crucial platform for addressing key trade issues and shaping the future of the global trading system.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs

records.title: Saudi Arabia has achieved a groundbreaking milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, overcoming its arid climat...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has achieved a groundbreaking milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, overcoming its arid climate and traditional reliance on imports. Spearheaded by Dava Agricultural Co., which employs advanced greenhouses and vertical farming techniques, the initiative aims to ensure year-round food security. With support from government entities like the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, as well as Saudi Export and Saudi Cargo, Dava successfully shipped 5 tonnes of tomatoes to Europe in collaboration with Dutch company Lehmann & Troost. This inaugural export, followed by a planned 10-tonne shipment and projections of 12 tonnes per day by 2025, marks a significant achievement for Saudi agriculture. Dava’s commitment to freshness and innovation, including refrigerated trucks and advanced packaging, underlines its dedication to revolutionizing the country’s agricultural landscape. With plans for further expansion into various crops and the establishment of distribution centers, Dava aims to bolster Saudi Arabia’s export capabilities and enhance global trade while contributing to the growth of the domestic agricultural sector.
records.institution: Dava Agricultural Co.

Ambassador Essa Al-Duhailan highlighted the potential for Bangladeshi farmers and experts to contribute to initiatives such as the Saudi Green Initiative and Middle East Green Initiative, which aim to plant over 50 billion trees in the region. These initiatives, spearheaded by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman, prioritize combating climate change and preserving the environment through afforestation and emissions reduction efforts. Additionally, discussions encompassed plans to streamline the employment process for Bangladeshis and preparations for the upcoming Hajj season, including the implementation of the Makkah Route initiative for the fourth consecutive year, facilitating pilgrims' journey to Saudi Arabia.

He also highlighted the strengthening bilateral relations, citing frequent high-level visits and increased flight connectivity between the two countries, with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni visiting the UAE multiple times in recent years. records.title: At the second Sharjah Talks, health and organic farming experts emphasized the significant positive impact of nurturing mini farms at hom...
records.description: At the second Sharjah Talks, health and organic farming experts emphasized the significant positive impact of nurturing mini farms at home on psychological well-being and family unity. The event, themed ‘Sustainable Harvest: Organic Agriculture and Nutrition Wellness,’ highlighted the importance of achieving balance and harmony within the human entity. Saeed Al Rumaithi, UNICEF Climate Change Ambassador and Co-founder of ‘The Organic Farm,’ advocated for transforming unused spaces at home into mini-farms to promote organic farming, emphasizing the importance of preserving soil and using local seeds. Eman Al Marri, an organic home farming expert, highlighted the benefits of home gardens in improving family life quality and increasing immunity. In another panel discussion, speakers emphasized holistic wellness encompassing physical, emotional, spiritual, and mental aspects, with an emphasis on organic farming as a return to natural farming practices. The event also featured Musleh Al Aryani, an eight-year-old farm owner, who shared innovative farming experiments aimed at contributing to the nation’s food security.
records.institution: UAE Department of Statistics and Community Development (DSCD) & the Sharjah Government Employees Club (SGEC)

records.title: Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have inked a significant real estate investment agreement, with Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding...
records.description: Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have inked a significant real estate investment agreement, with Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company (ADQ) spearheading a $35 billion initiative to develop Ras Al Hekma City. This transformative project, located approximately 350 kilometers northwest of Cairo, aims to establish Ras Al Hekma as a premier Mediterranean vacation destination, financial hub, and free zone, bolstering Egypt's economic and tourism potential. Under the deal, ADQ will oversee the $24 billion development of Ras Al Hekma, with an additional $11 billion earmarked for key projects across Egypt to foster economic growth and prosperity. Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly revealed that the investment, expected within two months, comprises $24 billion in cash liquidity and $11 billion from UAE deposits at the Central Bank of Egypt, translating into Egyptian pounds for development purposes. The project is anticipated to attract up to $150 billion in investments, generating millions of jobs and injecting liquidity into the Egyptian economy. Managing Director and CEO of ADQ, Mohamed Hassan Al Suwaidi, emphasized the commitment to transforming Ras Al Hekma into a prominent coastal destination through strategic partnerships and infrastructure projects. This influx of investment is poised to alleviate Egypt's economic challenges, including geopolitical tensions and foreign currency shortages, with positive market reactions already observed. The agreement is expected to pave the way for a new deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), offering ample liquidity to cover Egypt's financing gap and bolstering the Egyptian pound while providing an opportunity to replenish foreign exchange reserves.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company (ADQ)

records.title: The Atlantic Council's empowerME Initiative recently hosted a workshop titled "Women in finance: Building a more sustainable and inclusiv...
records.description: The Atlantic Council's empowerME Initiative recently hosted a workshop titled "Women in finance: Building a more sustainable and inclusive finance system," focusing on the significant contributions of women in developing sustainable finance in the UAE. Moderated by Abeer Abu Omar from Bloomberg, the panel featured prominent figures such as Shaikha Nasser Al Nowais from Rotana Hotel Management Corporation, Patricia Gomes from HSBC, Linda Fitz-Alan from Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts, and Thereshini Peter from Visa Inc. They discussed various challenges hindering women's advancement in finance and proposed solutions, emphasizing the importance of policy changes to promote inclusion and empowerment in the workplace. U.S. Ambassador to the UAE, Martina Strong, highlighted the economic impact of empowered women and commended the growing visibility of women in leadership roles in regional startups. The panelists stressed the need for diversity and inclusion in driving innovation and resilience, with specific strategies outlined to address obstacles and promote gender parity. Despite the UAE's high gender equality ranking, there remains a gap in female representation in board positions, signaling the need for concerted efforts to attract, retain, and support women in the workforce. The discussion concluded with a call for stronger measures by businesses to promote gender parity, including better recruitment practices, support for work/life balance, and increased opportunities for coaching and mentorship, ultimately aiming to break through the glass ceiling and create a more inclusive financial sector in the UAE.
records.institution: The Atlantic Council

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture of Uzbekistan and Abu Dhabi Food Hub have forged a collaboration in the agricultural domain, marking a signif...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture of Uzbekistan and Abu Dhabi Food Hub have forged a collaboration in the agricultural domain, marking a significant development in bilateral ties. This agreement emerged during the participation of Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Minister of Agriculture Ibrahim Abdurakhmanov, in the renowned Gulfood international food exhibition held in Dubai, UAE. Amidst fruitful discussions, beneficial agreements and memorandums of cooperation were inked, signifying a pivotal step forward. A pivotal meeting between Minister Abdurakhmanov and Suresh Vaidhyanathan, the director of Abu Dhabi Food Hub, catalyzed the establishment of this mutually advantageous cooperation in agricultural development. The signed memorandum of cooperation outlines plans for establishing a specialized food center, underscoring the commitment of both parties to foster collaborative initiatives. Notably, Abu Dhabi Food Hub - KEZAD, serving as a comprehensive and integrated ecosystem, is poised to facilitate wholesale trade and logistics across diverse food categories, further enhancing the prospects for fruitful cooperation in agriculture between Uzbekistan and Abu Dhabi.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority

records.title: The UAE and Kenya have solidified negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), heralding a new era of trade col...
records.description: The UAE and Kenya have solidified negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), heralding a new era of trade collaboration between the two nations aimed at safeguarding crucial East and West supply chains, stimulating investment in priority sectors, and enhancing market access for businesses operating in both territories. Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade, lauded the CEPA as a pivotal achievement in strengthening economic ties with Africa and creating fresh avenues for businesses and investors in both nations. The agreement is poised to not only bolster trade and investment but also foster innovation and sustainable growth, particularly in key sectors such as agriculture, technology, and tourism. With Kenya's economy showing promising growth projections, including a notable surge in real GDP, the CEPA holds immense potential for UAE businesses seeking to tap into Kenya's dynamic markets, particularly in its services and agriculture sectors. This partnership underscores the UAE's commitment to robust foreign trade, exemplified by the nation's record-high non-oil trade in goods in 2023, which reached $710 billion, marking a significant uptick from previous years.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs

records.title: UAE: New Biosecurity Programme to Promote Integration of Human, Animal, Plant, Environmental Health
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has unveiled its 'One Health' biosecurity program, aligning with the directives of the wise leadership and international standards outlined in the Joint International Action Plan on the One Health Approach for 2022-2026. This initiative, introduced during a workshop attended by esteemed international organizations affiliated with the United Nations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH), and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), underscores Abu Dhabi's commitment to cross-sectoral integration for community and environmental health and safety. The program encompasses eight key initiatives aimed at establishing a robust surveillance system, analyzing data to identify risks, and implementing preventive measures to curb disease spread. Additionally, it emphasizes awareness, education, and training to safeguard natural resources against pollution and overexploitation, while fostering integration across sectors like health, agriculture, and education. Mouza Suhail Al Muhairi, Deputy Director-General for Regulatory and Administrative Affairs at ADAFSA, highlighted the significance of international cooperation in promoting biosecurity and shared best practices. The program's launch signifies a crucial step towards bolstering public health, food security, and environmental sustainability in alignment with Abu Dhabi's vision for the future. International organizations pledged their support for Abu Dhabi's pioneering endeavors in biosecurity, aiming to disseminate these practices regionally and globally, while federal and local authorities reaffirmed their commitment to establishing Abu Dhabi as a model for biosecurity and One Health initiatives.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority

records.title: The Indian government has made an exception to the export ban on onions and allowed the overseas sale of a fixed quantity of 54,760 tonne...
records.description: The Indian government has made an exception to the export ban on onions and allowed the overseas sale of a fixed quantity of 54,760 tonnes of onions to Bangladesh, Mauritius, Bahrain, and Bhutan. Consumer Affairs Secretary Rohit Kumar Singh announced that 50,000 tonnes of onions will be exported to Bangladesh, 1,200 tonnes to Mauritius, 3,000 tonnes to Bahrain, and 560 tonnes to Bhutan with immediate effect. These shipments will be carried out by private traders until March 31, and the modalities are currently being worked out. Singh mentioned that the decision was made following a recommendation from the Ministry of External Affairs. Various countries have requested onion supplies from India, and the quantity is being evaluated on a case-by-case basis by the Ministry of External Affairs, with a final decision made by a group of ministers. The ban on onion exports is currently in place until March 31, imposed on December 8, 2023, to bolster domestic supply and curb price inflation. It is unlikely that the ban will be lifted even after March 31, given the expected lower production of rabi (winter) onions due to reduced cultivation, particularly in Maharashtra. In the 2023 rabi season, onion production was estimated at 22.7 million tonnes. Normally, rabi onions are stored for consumption during the lean season, and the government often purchases rabi onions to maintain a buffer. Agriculture ministry officials will assess the coverage of rabi onions in key growing states like Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat in the coming days.
records.institution: Indian Government

records.title: Mishref Cooperative Society and Gulf Bank have joined forces to launch the "A Step Towards Change" sustainability campaign in Kuwait, pro...
records.description: Mishref Cooperative Society and Gulf Bank have joined forces to launch the "A Step Towards Change" sustainability campaign in Kuwait, promoting eco-friendly practices through the distribution of reusable bags. Approximately 20,000 reusable bags will be handed out at Mishref co-op over a week, accompanied by awareness-raising events. Fahad Al-Sharah from Gulf Bank highlighted the initiative's goal of reducing plastic consumption and fostering behavioral change, aligning with Kuwait's environmental strategy and Gulf Bank's 2025 objectives. Abdullah Adel Al-Qallaf of Mishref Co-op introduced a "Fast Track" service for shareholders using reusable bags to incentivize their continued use. Meanwhile, the Scientific Center in Kuwait reaffirmed its commitment to waste management and recycling, emphasizing sorting waste and providing designated containers for different materials. General Manager Msaed Al-Yaseen detailed initiatives like "The Last Catch," a sculpture collecting plastic bottles for recycling, highlighting the urgent need to address plastic pollution and raise environmental awareness for sustainable development locally and globally.
records.institution: Mishref Co-op & Gulf Bank

records.title: Oman’s Ministry Amends Regulations of Law on Fishing and Protection of Marine Living Resources
records.description: The Ministry of Agricultural, Fisheries and Water Resources in Oman has introduced an amendment to the executive regulations of the Law on Fishing and Protection of Marine Living Resources through Ministerial Decision No. 39/2024. This decision, in line with the Law of Live Aquatic Wealth and the Executive Regulations of the Law of Sea Fishing and Protection of Aquatic Living Resources, prohibits shark fishing from December 1st until September 30th of the following year. Any actions conflicting with this decision will be nullified. The decision will be published in the Official Gazette and will come into effect the day after its publication.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agricultural, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Qatar has demonstrated its commitment to supporting Tanzania's flood victims by dispatching a second aid flight carrying 45 tonnes of ass...
records.description: Qatar has demonstrated its commitment to supporting Tanzania's flood victims by dispatching a second aid flight carrying 45 tonnes of assistance, including food and medical supplies, following a previous delivery of 49 tonnes just days prior. This assistance comes amidst a humanitarian crisis triggered by intense rainfall in late 2023, resulting in floods and mudslides across Tanzania. The floods have devastated communities, claiming lives, injuring many, and disrupting vital infrastructure. President Samia Suluhu Hassan, while highlighting the profound impact of climate change on poorer nations during her participation in the United Nations climate summit, emphasized the urgent need for international solidarity and support. As Tanzania grapples with the ongoing challenges posed by the floods, local forecasts predict continued rainfall until March, underscoring the necessity for sustained humanitarian aid efforts. Qatar's swift response reflects its solidarity with Tanzania and its unwavering commitment to assisting those affected by natural disasters.
records.institution: Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs

records.title: The Saudi-Pakistani Business Forum kicked off in Riyadh with the aim of enhancing trade relations between the two nations, setting a targ...
records.description: The Saudi-Pakistani Business Forum kicked off in Riyadh with the aim of enhancing trade relations between the two nations, setting a target of $20 billion in trade. Hosted by the Federation of Saudi Chambers and inaugurated by Minister of Commerce Dr. Majid Al-Qasabi, the event saw the participation of key Saudi and Pakistani delegates. Fawaz bin Rafaah, acting Deputy Governor of the General Authority of Foreign Trade for Private Sector Affairs and Global Presence, highlighted the essential role of the private sector in advancing trade ties, representing Dr. Al-Qasabi. Pakistani Federal Minister for Commerce, Industries & Investment, Dr. Gohar Ejaz, emphasized the potential of the Free Trade Agreement to stimulate investment and expressed Pakistan's eagerness to engage in Vision 2030 projects. Dr. Ejaz outlined Pakistan's ambition to elevate trade with Saudi Arabia to $20 billion and emphasized the need for a conducive business environment. Hassan Al-Huwaizi, Chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers, underlined the forum's objective to promote investment and trade partnerships, noting the significant progress in trade exchanges, which currently stand at $5.7 billion. Eng. Fahad Al-Bash, Chairman of the Saudi-Pakistani Business Council, discussed ongoing collaborative initiatives between investors from both countries, including ventures in various sectors such as technology, agriculture, and petrochemicals. The forum also featured presentations on investment opportunities in both countries by relevant government bodies, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties and achieve the ambitious trade target.
records.institution: Saudi-Pakistani Business Forum

records.title: DP World, in collaboration with Adroit Overseas Canada and Al Amir Foods, is investing AED550 million (US$150 million) to construct the A...
records.description: DP World, in collaboration with Adroit Overseas Canada and Al Amir Foods, is investing AED550 million (US$150 million) to construct the Agri Terminals complex at Jebel Ali Port in Dubai, the largest port in the city. With Jebel Ali Port already managing over 73 percent of the UAE’s food and beverage trade, the Agri Terminals are poised to play a crucial role in advancing the country’s food security objectives. Covering nearly 100,000 square meters, the Agri Terminals will be the city’s largest integrated agricultural processing and silo storage facility, specializing in storing and processing various agricultural products. The facility will have a total storage capacity of 200,000 metric tonnes developed over two phases and will feature advanced infrastructure such as pneumatic ship unloaders and state-of-the-art conveying equipment. Scheduled for completion in early 2025, this project aligns with DP World’s commitment to strengthening the UAE’s food supply chain and bolstering Dubai’s role in global food trade, supporting the National Food Security Strategy 2051. The initiative is expected to stimulate over AED 1.2 billion (US$327M) in new international trade and enhance Dubai’s bulk handling capacity, solidifying its position as a key player in regional and global trade. The groundbreaking event was attended by prominent officials from DP World, Dubai Municipality, Adroit Overseas Canada, Al Amir Foods, and other entities involved in the project.
records.institution: DP World

records.title: The Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA) in Sharjah unveiled a pioneering project during the UAE Innovation Month, showcasing...
records.description: The Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA) in Sharjah unveiled a pioneering project during the UAE Innovation Month, showcasing the integration of robotic technologies into coral reef farming. Spearheaded by Dr. Osama Malika Wahba, a scientific researcher at EPAA, the initiative aims to preserve and restore coral reefs, crucial components of the UAE's marine ecosystems. This innovative project leverages locally developed robotic technology equipped with artificial intelligence to efficiently farm coral reefs over expansive areas. Noteworthy for its precision and efficiency, the technology enables precise measurement of farming areas, identification of coral reef types, and monitoring of ambient temperatures, thereby optimizing the farming process. Moreover, the device's utilization of solar energy ensures sustainability and environmental friendliness, while its incorporation of artificial intelligence significantly reduces the time required for coral reef farming, bolstering efforts to preserve the marine environment and promote environmental sustainability in the UAE.
records.institution: Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA)

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Estonia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at enhancing cooperation in food managem...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Estonia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at enhancing cooperation in food management. The signing ceremony, which took place recently, involved officials from both countries. The agreement signifies a mutual commitment to collaborating on various aspects of food management, including food safety, security, and sustainability. Through this partnership, the UAE and Estonia seek to exchange knowledge, best practices, and technological innovations to address common challenges and promote efficient food management systems. This MoU reflects the UAE's ongoing efforts to strengthen international partnerships and leverage expertise from diverse sources to enhance its food management capabilities.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and the Environment

records.title: Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have embarked on a collaborative effort to address environmental challenges in the Karakalp...
records.description: Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have embarked on a collaborative effort to address environmental challenges in the Karakalpakstan region, focusing on combating land degradation and promoting sustainable agricultural practices. The Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection, and Climate Change of Uzbekistan disclosed that Aziz Abdukhakimov, the Minister of Ecology, met with Tarifa Al Zaabi, the Director General of the UAE International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), to discuss joint initiatives. Minister Abdukhakimov emphasized the urgency of tackling land degradation, particularly in Karakalpakstan, exacerbated by climate change and the Aral Sea crisis. Plans include establishing a climate center under the Ministry and collaborating with ICBA on projects like "Development of Sustainable Agricultural Production Systems in the Degraded Areas of Karakalpakstan." This project, with a budget exceeding $1.09mn, aims to bolster the resilience of farmers in the region through various initiatives, such as establishing a Genetic Resources Bank, conducting scientific research on drought- and waterproof crop varieties, and providing training and modern equipment for soil research laboratories. By introducing climate-resistant farming systems and promoting integrated production models, the project seeks to enhance agricultural productivity and empower local farmers. Additionally, the collaboration underscores the shared commitment of both nations to address climate change at the international level, with plans for ICBA's participation in the inaugural Samarkand Climate Forum in April. This initiative is vital in mitigating the adverse effects of the Aral Sea crisis, including salinization, soil degradation, desertification, and respiratory health risks posed by dust particles, while fostering sustainable agricultural practices and economic growth in the region.
records.institution: UAE International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: Musandam’s Breakwater Project Nears Completion, Boosting Fisheries Sector in Oman
records.description: The Musandam Governorate in Oman is on the brink of completing a significant breakwater project aimed at fortifying maritime safety and boosting the fisheries sector. Spearheaded by Khalifa bin Ali Al Shehhi, Director of the Fish Wealth Department at the Directorate General of Agriculture, Fish, and Water Resources, the project has reached an impressive 80 percent completion rate, with a total investment of RO 2.5 million. Al Shehhi highlighted the project's pivotal role in combating sand accumulation and turbulent waves, crucial for safeguarding the livelihoods of local fishermen and enhancing fish landing operations. The initiative encompasses various infrastructural elements such as main and secondary peninsulas, sheds, warehouses, boat slips, and service facilities, designed to bolster the fisheries sector's infrastructure comprehensively. With major components spanning Ghumma and Al Jari, including primary and secondary breakwaters and port basin areas, the project is poised to revitalize fish landing areas and create conducive environments for Omani fishermen's aspirations, with an anticipated completion in the first half of the year.
records.institution: Directorate General of Agriculture, Fish, and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) in Oman is leading the charge in transforming the industrial landsc...
records.description: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) in Oman is leading the charge in transforming the industrial landscape through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and factory automation technologies. With a focus on improving productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability, this initiative represents a significant milestone in Oman's quest for economic diversification and technological advancement. Spearheaded by the 'Factory Automation and Artificial Intelligence' program, the MoCIIP aims to equip private sector entities with state-of-the-art technologies to drive efficiency and innovation in manufacturing processes. Mazin Al Siyabi, Director of Technical Assistance at the ministry, highlights the crucial role of AI and automation in enhancing Oman's industrial growth, emphasizing their potential to boost efficiency and competitiveness. Al Siyabi stresses the importance of collaboration with academia and the private sector to empower the workforce with automation skills, positioning Oman as a leading investment destination aligned with Oman Vision 2040 objectives. This initiative targets both new factories and existing facilities, promoting operational excellence through advanced technology integration. Stakeholders in the industrial sector, including academia and industry leaders, acknowledge the positive impact of these efforts in driving sectoral growth and fostering a competitive industrial landscape. As Oman celebrates its Industrial Day, the nation's commitment to sustainable industrial growth through technological innovation and strategic partnerships is evident, positioning Oman as a regional hub of innovation and industrial excellence.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP)

records.title: Saudi Arabia is moving forward with plans to establish a marketplace dedicated to goods from Iraq, as announced by the Iraqi Federation o...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is moving forward with plans to establish a marketplace dedicated to goods from Iraq, as announced by the Iraqi Federation of Industries (IFI). According to reports, the commercial attaché in Riyadh expressed interest in creating a trading hub to showcase Iraqi products in Saudi Arabia, with the aim of bolstering economic and trade relations between the two countries. The IFI has called on Iraqi entrepreneurs interested in exporting to submit a list of their agricultural and industrial products for display and promotion in Saudi Arabia. While the date for the establishment of this marketplace was not specified, the move underscores the growing economic ties between Saudi Arabia and Iraq. The statement follows previous announcements highlighting the increasing trade exchange between the two countries, which reached $1.5 billion, according to Saudi Minister of Commerce Majid Al-Qasabi. The recent session of the Saudi-Iraqi Coordination Council in Jeddah witnessed several agreements aimed at mutual political and economic benefits, with both sides expressing eagerness to continue collaboration across various sectors, including energy, education, banking, and electrical interconnection.
records.institution: Iraqi Federation of Industries (IFI)

records.title: H2O Hospitality (H2O), a South Korean digital innovation company in the accommodation and leisure industry, has established its regional...
records.description: H2O Hospitality (H2O), a South Korean digital innovation company in the accommodation and leisure industry, has established its regional headquarters in Abu Dhabi in collaboration with the Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO), marking a milestone in economic cooperation between South Korea and Abu Dhabi. With South Korea's renowned innovation prowess and Abu Dhabi's recognition as the smartest city in the MENA region, the partnership emphasizes synergies in innovation and technology. ADIO provided H2O with growth-enabling support, including financial incentives and connections to Abu Dhabi's ecosystem and international trade opportunities. The move reflects H2O's strategy to leverage its success in Asia and tap into the MENA hospitality market, which is poised for growth, with Abu Dhabi's tourism sector benefiting from H2O's solutions to enhance guest experience and operational efficiency. John Lee, Founder & CEO of H2O, highlighted the company's commitment to supporting Abu Dhabi's tourism sector through digital transformation. ADGM Authority CEO Salem Mohammed Al Darei emphasized the strategic collaboration between ADGM and ADIO in establishing a platform that fosters investment and innovation, aligning with Abu Dhabi's vision for growth and economic diversification. H2O joins other key players in establishing operations in Abu Dhabi with support from ADIO, further enhancing the emirate's appeal as a destination for global entities in innovative sectors.
records.institution: H2O Hospitality (H2O)

records.title: Driven by a passion for promoting a plant-based lifestyle, Qatari entrepreneur Ghanim Al Sulaiti embarked on a journey a decade ago to ch...
records.description: Driven by a passion for promoting a plant-based lifestyle, Qatari entrepreneur Ghanim Al Sulaiti embarked on a journey a decade ago to champion organic and vegan cuisine in Qatar. Recognizing the nation's focus on health and wellness, he founded Evergreen Organics in 2016, Qatar's first vegan restaurant, blending vegan principles with local culture and flavors. Al Sulaiti emphasizes sourcing organic ingredients locally, supporting Qatar's organic farming sector while enriching the dining experience. His recent initiative, Qatar’s First Vegan Festival, showcased the country's growing vegan community, affirming the demand for plant-based options. Al Sulaiti remains committed to inspiring healthier lifestyles through education and community-building, reflecting Qatar's embrace of wellness and sustainability. His vision and dedication are transforming the culinary landscape, nurturing a healthier and more compassionate future for Qatar and beyond.
records.institution: Evergreen Organics

records.title: During a meeting between Qatar Chamber (QC) First Vice-Chairman Mohamed bin Ahmed bin Twar Al Kuwari and Special Envoy of the Royal Gover...
records.description: During a meeting between Qatar Chamber (QC) First Vice-Chairman Mohamed bin Ahmed bin Twar Al Kuwari and Special Envoy of the Royal Government of Cambodia H E Dr. Othsman Hassan, economic and commercial cooperation between the two countries was discussed, alongside investment opportunities in Cambodia across various sectors. Al Kuwari highlighted the importance of strengthening Qatari investment in promising sectors in Cambodia, emphasizing the Chamber's support for Qatari investors looking to explore opportunities there. He also expressed the Qatari market's openness to high-quality Cambodian products at competitive prices and proposed organizing business visits for Qatari entrepreneurs to Cambodia to further explore investment prospects in agriculture, tourism, infrastructure, food processing, and other industries. H E Dr. Othsman Hassan reiterated Cambodia's interest in promoting its economy and investment opportunities to Qatari investors, underscoring the desire to enhance cooperative relations with Qatar.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has embarked on a significant initiative to bolster its education, investment, securities trading, and sustainability sector...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has embarked on a significant initiative to bolster its education, investment, securities trading, and sustainability sectors by signing six memorandums of understanding (MoUs), aligning with the objectives outlined in Vision 2030. Among the agreements, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development and the Saudi Exchange have established a cooperation agreement to launch a Social Responsibility Index, aimed at evaluating and promoting corporate social responsibility practices within listed companies. Additionally, partnerships have been forged to support artistic initiatives, educational programs, and cultural exchanges, reflecting a commitment to nurturing a dynamic artistic landscape in the Kingdom. Another notable MoU involves Riyad Capital and E Fund, a Chinese asset management firm, fostering knowledge sharing on local investment expertise and potential collaboration in developing future investment products. Moreover, agreements have been reached to launch a Repo Trading Platform, delve into sustainability opportunities, and support forestation initiatives, demonstrating Saudi Arabia's dedication to fostering economic growth, social responsibility, and environmental sustainability.

records.title: Gulf Scientific Corporation (GSC) has taken a significant stride in expanding its regional presence with the inauguration of its new offi...
records.description: Gulf Scientific Corporation (GSC) has taken a significant stride in expanding its regional presence with the inauguration of its new office, GSC SPC, in Muscat, Oman. This strategic move not only underscores GSC's dedication to bolstering the scientific community in Oman but also reinforces its foothold across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. The Muscat office, equipped to serve as a local hub for the sales and distribution of laboratory equipment and consumables, signifies a pivotal enhancement in GSC's operational capabilities within Oman. With the appointment of an experienced manager and a dedicated team of six members, comprising sales and service professionals, GSC aims to provide prompt and efficient services directly to its clientele, which includes prominent entities such as the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Agriculture & Fisheries, Royal Oman Police, and Sultan Qaboos University Hospital. Moreover, by stocking spare parts and consumables, GSC SPC ensures the fulfillment of immediate customer requirements, thereby addressing any gaps in scientific equipment provision and contributing to the overall well-being of Omani citizens. This strategic expansion aligns with GSC's broader mission of tailored support and service provision, aimed at meeting the distinctive needs of its clientele and fostering the growth of the scientific sector in the region. With a commitment to innovation and future growth, GSC is poised to play a pivotal role in shaping the scientific landscape of the GCC region.
records.institution: Gulf Scientific Corporation (GSC)

records.title: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning in Oman has initiated a significant development phase for the Sultan Haitham City (SHC) projec...
records.description: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning in Oman has initiated a significant development phase for the Sultan Haitham City (SHC) project, signing over 35 agreements totaling RO1 billion. These agreements encompass a wide array of sectors, including engineering consulting services, real estate development, and technical cooperation, aimed at fostering urban planning and housing projects. The SHC's first phase, spanning over 5 million square meters, aims to accommodate more than 39,000 residents and feature essential infrastructure such as parks, hospitals, educational institutions, and government facilities. Additionally, partnerships with international consultants and real estate developers underscore Oman's commitment to leveraging external expertise and investment for sustainable urban development. Furthermore, initiatives supporting small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and infrastructure projects like the construction of "Singapore Street" signify Oman's multifaceted approach to socio-economic growth and family stability.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning

records.title: Saudi Arabia is positioning itself as a global leader in addressing food security challenges by pioneering innovative solutions that can...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is positioning itself as a global leader in addressing food security challenges by pioneering innovative solutions that can be implemented worldwide. Juan Carlos, CEO of Topian, NEOM's subsidiary focused on food, emphasized the urgent need for new technologies to feed the growing global population. Topian aims to introduce cutting-edge systems, such as controlled-environment production methods, to reduce water usage in agriculture significantly. The company's initiative, Future to Table, embodies its commitment to sustainable food production, focusing on agriculture, aquaculture, and food innovation. Carlos highlighted Saudi Arabia's National Strategy for Agriculture 2030 as a crucial framework for achieving sustainable food and water security while promoting economic, social, and environmental progress. Through initiatives like Future to Table, Saudi Arabia aims to revolutionize food production while minimizing environmental impact, setting a precedent for global food security efforts.
records.institution: Topian

records.description: The inaugural Regional Conference for Irrigation and Agricultural Drainage in the Middle East, organized by the Saudi Irrigation Organization (SIO) in collaboration with the International Organization for Irrigation and Drainage (ICID), is set to take place in Riyadh from February 26 to 28, 2024, attracting a diverse mix of local and international stakeholders. This conference serves as a crucial platform to address pressing challenges confronting the irrigation, drainage, and water resources management sector in the region, offering an opportunity to delve into the latest developments and practices, including climate change impacts, water scarcity, and sustainable irrigation methods. With a focus on sustainable development, the event will feature discussions on utilizing non-conventional water resources like treated wastewater and integrating technological innovations for efficient water management. Engineer Mohammad Zaid Abuhid, acting president of the SIO, emphasizes the conference's role in fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange to achieve sustainable outcomes in water resource management.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Coffee Renaissance: Transforming Global Perceptions and Boosting Sustainable Development
records.description: Saudi Arabia's coffee sector is undergoing a remarkable transformation, highlighted by a recent event in Jazan that signals a shift in global perceptions and a commitment to sustainable development. At the International Saudi Coffee Exhibition, Deputy Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Mansour Al-Mushaiti, unveiled a strategic initiative aimed at elevating the nation's coffee industry. With over 2,000 farms in Jazan producing more than 1,000 tons of coffee annually, Saudi Arabia is poised for a cultural renaissance, showcasing its agricultural diversity and dedication to sustainability. This initiative, supported by the Sustainable Rural Agricultural Development Program, reflects a broader strategy to enhance rural livelihoods and foster economic diversification. The International Saudi Coffee Exhibition has played a key role in promoting Saudi coffee globally, with the Deputy Minister acknowledging the significant improvement in quality and positioning Saudi coffee as a premier product in the international market. This shift not only promises economic benefits but also signifies a deeper appreciation for Saudi Arabia's cultural heritage and agricultural innovation on the world stage.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: WILOC, a global leader in track and trace solutions for the energy industry, has partnered with Al Ghaith Energy, a prominent service pro...
records.description: WILOC, a global leader in track and trace solutions for the energy industry, has partnered with Al Ghaith Energy, a prominent service provider in the oil and gas sector in the GCC and North Africa, aiming to capitalize on the UAE's growing emphasis on digitization and IoT technologies in its oil and gas industry. The collaboration leverages WILOC's expertise in providing compliant and streamlined solutions for operational processes, complementing Al Ghaith Energy's diversified services portfolio. With a focus on enhancing traceability and optimizing operations, the partnership underscores the industry's commitment to adopting cutting-edge technologies for sustainable growth and operational excellence in line with the UAE's Digital Government Strategy 2025.
records.institution: Al Ghaith Energy & WILOC

records.title: The UAE has unveiled the inaugural Dubatt Battery Recycling plant, the first fully integrated facility of its kind in the country, locate...
records.description: The UAE has unveiled the inaugural Dubatt Battery Recycling plant, the first fully integrated facility of its kind in the country, located in Dubai Industrial City under TECOM Group PJSC. The formal inauguration, attended by esteemed dignitaries including Cabinet Member and Minister of Economy His Excellency Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, highlights the plant's crucial role in advancing sustainable industrial practices in the UAE. Government officials, including Minister of Climate Change and Environment Her Excellency Dr. Amna Al Dahak, emphasized its alignment with the UAE Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap and Circular Economy Policy 2031, signaling a significant step towards sustainable industrial and economic development. With an initial investment of AED 120 million (US$32.67m), the Dubatt plant utilizes state-of-the-art technologies to recycle up to 80 percent of battery waste generated in the UAE, significantly contributing to the circular economy and national sustainability goals. Planned expansion with an investment of AED 96 million (US$26.14m) aims to increase the factory's lead acid battery recycling capacity to 75,000 metric tonnes per year, further supporting the UAE's sustainability objectives. Dubatt's strategic location within Dubai Industrial City, a hub for manufacturing, underscores its role in driving sustainable expansion in the manufacturing sector while aligning with national economic agendas such as Operation 300bn and Dubai Economic Agenda 'D33'. Moreover, the plant's export aspirations to the GCC, Europe, and the Far East support the Make it in the Emirates initiative, strengthening the supply chain for locally manufactured products.
records.institution: TECOM Group PJSC

records.title: The International Institute for Central Asia (IICA) hosted a meeting with Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Uzbekistan Yousef Al-Otaibi to ex...
records.description: The International Institute for Central Asia (IICA) hosted a meeting with Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Uzbekistan Yousef Al-Otaibi to explore avenues for enhancing cooperation between the two nations. Discussions revolved around the outcomes of the historic Summit of the Heads of State of Central Asia and the Cooperation Council of the Arab States of the Gulf, which catalyzed collaboration in various sectors including trade, transport, agriculture, industrial cooperation, green energy, digital economy, and innovation. Emphasis was placed on implementing initiatives proposed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, such as the Agreement on Friendship, Regional Connectivity and Cooperation, and the creation of a single visa-free tourist space "Gulf – Central Asia." Highlighting the development of partnerships in tourism, the meeting underscored the strategic significance of visa regulation innovations, including the introduction of electronic visas for Uzbekistan tourists visiting Saudi Arabia. The parties also discussed plans to increase mutual air flights from the current 28 to 50 flights per week, illustrating the commitment to bolstering bilateral relations and fostering collaboration between expert and analytical communities of Central Asia and the Gulf countries.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Masdar City, Abu Dhabi's center for sustainability and innovation, has inaugurated its indoor vertical farm in collaboration with Alesca...
records.description: Masdar City, Abu Dhabi's center for sustainability and innovation, has inaugurated its indoor vertical farm in collaboration with Alesca Technologies, an agricultural technology (AgriTech) firm, to tackle food security challenges. Utilizing automated equipment and AI software, the project grows various fresh leafy greens, lettuce, and herbs devoid of harmful chemicals, offering ready-to-eat produce. Housed in repurposed shipping containers near Masdar City's Eco-Plaza, the farm is already operational, with plans to expand further. Once fully operational, it aims to produce over 650 kilograms of leafy greens per month year-round, while consuming 90-95% less water than conventional farms. The initiative serves to educate visitors about vertical farming's potential in addressing food security challenges and minimizing environmental impact. Masdar City's collaboration with Alesca underscores its commitment to innovative climate change solutions and multifunctional land use, essential in densely populated urban areas. Alesca Technologies' involvement aligns with Masdar City's AgriTech cluster, demonstrating a concerted effort towards sustainable food production and technological advancement.
records.institution: Masdar City

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman's Environmental Authority has issued a phased plan to eliminate all forms of plastic shopping bags within a specified timeframe, acc...
records.description: Oman's Environmental Authority has issued a phased plan to eliminate all forms of plastic shopping bags within a specified timeframe, according to Decision No. 2024/8. This decision aligns with Oman's environmental protection and pollution prevention laws established by Royal Decrees No. 114/2001 and No. 106/2020, and Ministerial Decision No. 2020/23. The new regulation prohibits companies, institutions, and individuals from using single-use plastic bags and other plastic materials thinner than 50 micrometers. Violators of this regulation will face administrative fines ranging from 50 to 1,000 Omani Rials, with increased penalties for repeated offenses. This policy becomes effective the day after its publication in the official gazette, enforcing a gradual ban on plastic shopping bags according to an attached schedule.
records.institution: Omani Environment Authority

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Environment Authority (EA) of Oman has issued Decision No.
records.description: The Environment Authority (EA) of Oman has issued Decision No. 8/2024 to gradually phase out all types of plastic shopping bags by January 2027, with specific sectors targeted in six-month intervals. Starting from July 1, 2024, pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics will be required to stop using plastic bags, followed by other sectors such as shops selling fabrics, textiles, clothing, furniture, and household supplies by January 1, 2025. The decision, which has been in the works since 2012, aims to curb plastic bag usage and promote environmentally friendly alternatives. EA has collaborated with various authorities to facilitate the transition, including initiatives to distribute eco-friendly bags and raise public awareness. Violators of the ban will face fines ranging from RO50 to RO1,000, with penalties doubling for repeat offenses. The phased approach aligns with Oman Vision 2040's goal of achieving sustainable development and fostering a cleaner, healthier environment for future generations.
records.institution: Omani Environment Authority

records.title: In the past five years (2019 - 2023), Saudi Arabia's non-oil exports to Africa have surged to more than SAR128 billion ($34.1 billion), w...
records.description: In the past five years (2019 - 2023), Saudi Arabia's non-oil exports to Africa have surged to more than SAR128 billion ($34.1 billion), with the chemicals and polymers sector leading the list with exports exceeding SAR83 billion ($22 billion), as reported by SPA. Following closely, the construction-materials sector recorded exports exceeding SAR10 billion, while the packaging sector followed with exports of over SAR9 billion. Key exported products include polypropylene, polyethylene, and fertilizers, with Egypt, Algeria, South Africa, Morocco, Sudan, Kenya, and Nigeria among the top importers of Saudi products from a list of 55 African countries. The strategic, commercial, and economic relations between Saudi Arabia and Africa are robust and deeply rooted, driven by mutual interests in progress and prosperity. To further enhance these ties, the Saudi Exports Development Authority (Saudi Exports) is actively engaging with African markets, organizing trade missions and participating in specialized international exhibitions across the continent to promote Saudi products and services and facilitate commercial partnerships.
records.institution: The Saudi Exports Development Authority

records.title: Saudi Arabia has recently deposited $250 million as the second tranche of economic aid to the legitimate Yemeni government, part of a lar...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has recently deposited $250 million as the second tranche of economic aid to the legitimate Yemeni government, part of a larger $1.2 billion package aimed at alleviating Yemen's economic struggles. This aid, directed by King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, targets the budget deficit, salaries, wages, operating expenses, and economic reforms, reflecting Saudi Arabia's commitment to Yemen's security, stability, and development. With previous economic aid totaling around $11.2 billion from 2012 to 2023, Saudi Arabia's ongoing support has significantly impacted Yemen's economy, stabilizing prices, boosting GDP growth, and strengthening the Yemeni riyal. Additionally, Saudi Arabia has provided grants for oil derivatives to generate electricity, creating job opportunities and supporting logistical movement, while implementing numerous development projects through the Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen to enhance vital sectors and government capabilities.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.title: Salman Fazlur Rahman, the private industry and investment adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, revealed Saudi Arabia's interest i...
records.description: Salman Fazlur Rahman, the private industry and investment adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, revealed Saudi Arabia's interest in establishing a special economic zone (SEZ) in Payra, located in the Patuakhali district of Bangladesh's Barisal division. During his recent three-day visit to Saudi Arabia, Rahman stated that Bangladesh is also eager to reciprocate by offering Saudi Arabia an economic zone within its borders. He mentioned that Saudi Arabia's investment minister has expressed interest in developing an economic zone in Payra. Additionally, Rahman announced Bangladesh's plans to establish a urea fertilizer factory in Saudi Arabia through a joint venture, with the intention of importing all fertilizer produced there.
records.institution: Saudi Government

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Omani-Scottish waste-to-value startup X2E is poised to invest $1.6 billion in projects across the alternative fuel value chain, including...
records.description: Omani-Scottish waste-to-value startup X2E is poised to invest $1.6 billion in projects across the alternative fuel value chain, including biodiesel and Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), over the next two years. CEO John Jones revealed plans to cultivate Camelina seeds for biofuel production initially, with future expansion into SAF. The company aims for vertical integration, with separate entities managing feedstock cultivation, water treatment, seed extraction, and refinery operations. X2E is collaborating with partners for each venture, with investments earmarked for various stages of the value chain, from agriculture to biodiesel and SAF production. The first capital close is expected in the second quarter of 2024, with construction projected to take another 18 months. Additionally, X2E plans to acquire biodiesel plants globally, with expansions aimed at tripling current capacity. Discussions for contract farming of Camelina are underway in Africa and Malaysia, signaling X2E's global ambitions in the alternative fuel sector.
records.institution: Omani-Scottish X2E

records.title: Bühler, a renowned provider of milling and food processing technologies, is eyeing promising rice processing opportunities in Saudi Arabia.
records.description: Bühler, a renowned provider of milling and food processing technologies, is eyeing promising rice processing opportunities in Saudi Arabia. Mohamed Jebabra, Bühler's Country Manager in Saudi Arabia, highlighted the growing interest among existing customers and new investors in leveraging the immense potential of the rice processing market. With Saudi Arabia being one of the largest importers of rice globally, at 1.35 million tonnes annually, and facing concerns about food security amid rising global rice prices, there is a pressing need to diversify food strategies. Jebabra emphasized the demand for Bühler's state-of-the-art rice processing technology, particularly in light of the government's initiatives to localize food production and enhance food security. Bühler's comprehensive storage solutions and advanced technology, coupled with their longstanding presence and local capabilities in Saudi Arabia since 1978, position them as a reliable partner in meeting the evolving needs of the market. Moreover, Bühler offers tailored customer service and performance assessment workshops, underscoring their commitment to supporting efficiency enhancement and sustainable growth in rice processing operations.
records.institution: Bühler

records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture announced that Saudi Arabia has lifted restrictions on importing strawberries from Egypt, effective...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture announced that Saudi Arabia has lifted restrictions on importing strawberries from Egypt, effective February 1. The decision comes after Saudi Arabia placed a temporary hold on issuing import permits for Egyptian strawberries. The ministry clarified that the previous measure was an internal regulatory action by the Kingdom, applicable to various agricultural imports from all countries, and was not specifically targeted at Egyptian strawberries. The decision aimed to regulate the domestic market in Saudi Arabia based on supply and demand dynamics, rather than concerns related to quarantine or health issues with Egyptian strawberries.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation
