records.title: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) has launched a Millet Demo Farm in alignment with the objectives of the Interna...
records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) has launched a Millet Demo Farm in alignment with the objectives of the International Year of Millets and COP28 on climate action, sustainable agriculture, food security, and nutrition. Established in partnership with the SELCO Foundation, the Millet Demo Farm aims to demonstrate the complete value chain of millets, from seed production to consumption, with a focus on raising awareness about the benefits of millets in adapting to climate change in agriculture. Dr. Tarifa Alzaabi, Director General of ICBA, emphasized the importance of embracing neglected and underutilized crops like millets to build sustainable and resilient agrifood systems. The initiative also aims to promote millet production and consumption in the Middle East North Africa and other regions through technology transfer and capacity development. ICBA has been a pioneer in the research and development of climate-resilient and nutritious crops suitable for arid and salt-affected environments for over two decades, and this initiative is part of their commitment to advancing sustainable agriculture globally.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: During the China-Saudi Investment Conference in Beijing, over 60 memorandums of understanding and agreements were signed, amounting to a...
records.description: During the China-Saudi Investment Conference in Beijing, over 60 memorandums of understanding and agreements were signed, amounting to a total value of $25 billion. These agreements span various sectors, including energy, agriculture, tourism, mining, financial services, logistics, infrastructure, technology, and healthcare. Notable deals include an $8.5 billion agreement between the Saudi Esports Federation and Chinese esports tournament operator VSPO in the information and communication technology sector, as well as a $7.5 billion collaboration between China's Oriental Energy Co. and Saudi Arabia's Ajlan & Bros Holding Group Co. in manufacturing. The conference also saw nine Chinese companies receive licenses to open regional headquarters in Saudi Arabia. These developments are expected to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two nations.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Investment

records.title: Qatari private sector exports to Jordan have experienced robust growth, increasing by more than 11.7% during the first nine months of 202...
records.description: Qatari private sector exports to Jordan have experienced robust growth, increasing by more than 11.7% during the first nine months of 2023 compared to the same period in the previous year. The total value of Qatari private sector exports to Jordan from January to September 2023 amounted to approximately $136 million, a notable increase from the $120 million recorded in the same period in 2022. These exports from the Qatari private sector to Jordan covered a wide range of products, including organic fertilizer, iron bars, medical solutions, food items, chemical materials, chemical fertilizers, plastic bags, and car engine oils. The Qatar Chamber of Commerce and Industry's report for the third quarter of 2023 revealed that the volume of Qatari private sector exports during that period amounted to about 3.25 billion Qatari riyals, equivalent to $892.8 million.
records.institution: Qatari Chamber of Commerce and Industry

records.title: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agritech company, has acquired Red Sea's controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) production facili...
records.description: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agritech company, has acquired Red Sea's controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) production facility near Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as part of its expansion strategy. Pure Harvest will assume operations of the farm in January 2024 and will invest capital to enhance production and climate control capabilities. The deal also allows Pure Harvest to benefit from Red Sea's SecondSky technology, a heat-blocking roofing solution that improves energy efficiency, reduces water consumption, and enhances crop health in greenhouses. As part of the transaction, Pure Harvest will secure a 40-hectare land bank co-located with the existing production facility, positioning the company to expand its franchised farm footprint in the region.
records.institution: Pure Harvest Smart Farms

records.title: Jazan City Completes 53 Key Projects Valued at $2.39bn
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Jazan City for Basic and Transformative Industries has completed 53 capital projects valued at over SR9 billion ($2.39 billion), according to Saudi Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Bandar Alkhorayef. These projects span multiple sectors, including infrastructure, public facilities, housing, and other services. Private sector investments in Jazan City have exceeded SR32 billion, with discussions ongoing for future projects estimated at around SR10 billion. These developments align with national strategies and demonstrate the economic viability of the region's projects, fostering economic and industrial growth.
records.institution: Jazan City

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s NEOM: $500 bln Mega-Project Unveils New Food Company Topian
records.description: NEOM, Saudi Arabia's ambitious $500 billion mega-project, has unveiled Topian, the NEOM Food Company, aimed at redefining food production, distribution, and consumption with a focus on sustainability. Topian will work across five vertical pillars: climate-proof agriculture, regenerative aquaculture, novel foods, personalized nutrition, and sustainable food supply and ESG. Supported by the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, this initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals for food security, climate change mitigation, and achieving net-zero emissions by 2060. Topian aims to introduce innovative solutions to address global food system challenges related to population growth, climate change, and resource depletion.
records.institution: Saudi NEOM

records.title: Saudi FDI Reforms Poised to Deliver Transformative Impact
records.description: Saudi Arabia remains committed to its reform agenda, focusing on boosting foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and diversifying investment strategies despite a recent decline in FDI, which saw a 21 percent drop in the second quarter of 2023. This decline, however, contrasts with a 94 percent increase in the number of investment licenses issued during the same period, reaching 1,819. The regional headquarters program, offering tax incentives and a 30-year corporate income tax exemption, is expected to expedite FDI. Despite the recent drop, Saudi Arabia achieved the second-highest amount of FDI in the Middle East and Africa region during the period. France, Japan, Kuwait, Malaysia, Singapore, the UAE, and the US are among the main contributors to this investment surge. Key sectors attracting FDI include chemicals, real estate, fossil fuels, automobiles, tourism, plastics, and machinery, indicating growing international investor interest and confidence in Saudi Arabia's economic landscape. The Kingdom's financial account, reflecting net values for direct investment, portfolio investment, and reserve assets, amounted to SR42.97 billion, a 70 percent decline compared to the same period last year, primarily due to increased borrowings. Despite the decline in reserves, public debt remains sustainable, staying below the 50 percent debt to gross domestic product ceiling, and the fiscal capacity remains substantial.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Finance

records.title: Saudi Fund for Development Supports Africa's Sustainable Development and Climate Resilience at COP28
records.description: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) is actively participating in initiatives to support sustainable development and climate resilience in Africa. During the 28th Conference of Parties (COP28) of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), H.E. Sultan Al-Marshad, CEO of SFD, took part in a high-level panel discussion at the Saudi Pavilion. The discussion focused on the $50 billion funding allocated by the Arab Coordination Group (ACG) to promote sustainable development in Africa until 2030. This funding pledge was announced during the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference in Riyadh in November 2023. The panel discussion featured experts from ACG institutions, emphasizing their commitment to building resilient and inclusive societies in Africa and supporting the continent's development aspirations. SFD has played a significant role in financing projects in Africa, contributing over $11 billion to more than 400 projects in 46 African countries, aligning with ACG's commitment to the global energy transition and sustainable development.
records.institution: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: At the COP28 climate summit in Dubai, the United States and the United Arab Emirates announced that funding for the Agriculture Innovatio...
records.description: At the COP28 climate summit in Dubai, the United States and the United Arab Emirates announced that funding for the Agriculture Innovation Mission for Climate (AIM for Climate) has grown to over $17 billion. AIM for Climate, launched in 2021 at COP26, receives funding from governments, companies, and non-governmental organizations. It aims to address climate-friendly farming practices globally, as food and farming contribute to approximately one-third of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. The initiative has announced nearly 80 projects since 2021, with goals to expand agricultural research, promote sustainable farming practices, and reduce methane emissions. The funding has increased from $8 billion at COP27 to the current $17 billion, including $12 billion from governments and $5 billion from non-government parties such as companies and humanitarian organizations. The projects announced at COP28 range from $150,000 to $500 million in size and include initiatives to expand regenerative agriculture practices. Agriculture is a major focus at this year's climate summit, with a dedicated day on food and farming topics.
records.institution: The Agriculture Innovation Mission for Climate (AIM for Climate)

records.title: International Center for Biosaline Agriculture & Schneider Electric Advance Youth & Women Roles in Sustainability at COP28
records.description: Schneider Electric has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) at COP28 to collaborate on empowering youth and women in sustainability. The MoU encompasses several initiatives, such as educational tours and social mentorship programs, aiming to foster environmental leadership and green education. By joining forces with ICBA, Schneider Electric seeks to equip future sustainability leaders with the skills and knowledge necessary to tackle climate change impacts and drive innovation, contributing to global food security, climate action, and social empowerment in line with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals.
records.institution: Schneider Electric

records.title: Silal and Bayer Partners to Strengthen the Agricultural Landscape in the UAE
records.description: Silal, the UAE's leading Agri-Tech Food Company, has formed a strategic partnership with Bayer, a global leader in life sciences with a focus on healthcare and nutrition, to strengthen the agricultural landscape in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) while addressing climate change as a central concern. The collaboration was announced during the World Agri-Tech Innovation Summit in Dubai on December 4th, 2023, and it aims to enhance the capabilities of local agronomists, fostering an environment conducive to agricultural innovation and excellence. This partnership will leverage Bayer's BayG.A.P. capacity-building program to advance best-in-class agricultural practices, especially under the challenging climatic conditions of the UAE. Both Silal and Bayer are committed to mitigating climate change and enhancing resilience in the agricultural sector, recognizing its critical role in addressing global warming. The program includes modules on Integrated Pest Management, Safe Use, Crop Protection Products, Application Technology, and Irrigation, and it will follow a train-the-trainer approach to reach growers in the UAE. This collaboration represents a significant step in advancing sustainable agriculture and addressing climate change challenges in the UAE and beyond.
records.institution: Silal

records.title: Government and business leaders from Saudi Arabia and France convened in Riyadh to discuss economic cooperation, global aid initiatives,...
records.description: Government and business leaders from Saudi Arabia and France convened in Riyadh to discuss economic cooperation, global aid initiatives, and human rights. Dr. Abdullah Al-Rabeeah, supervisor-general of KSrelief, highlighted Saudi Arabia's global efforts, including 2,625 projects in 94 countries worth over $6 billion. Discussions also included ways to improve cooperation in the realm of human rights. The conference, titled "France 2030 and Vision 2030: Toward Energy and Industry Transformation," featured over 40 French companies, 16 governmental entities from both countries, and 90 Saudi Arabian firms. The collaboration will extend to skills training and support for startups.
records.institution: Saudi KSrelief, Business and Trade Officials

records.title: Indonesia's state-owned electricity company, PLN, is collaborating with Saudi Arabia's energy firm, ACWA Power, to construct two floating...
records.description: Indonesia's state-owned electricity company, PLN, is collaborating with Saudi Arabia's energy firm, ACWA Power, to construct two floating solar power plants in West Sumatra's Lake Singkarak and West Java's Saguling Reservoir. These projects take advantage of Indonesia's substantial solar potential and abundant lakes and reservoirs to promote renewable energy. The Singkarak floating solar farm, covering 0.26% of Lake Singkarak's total area, is expected to have a capacity of up to 77 MWp, while the Saguling floating solar farm, occupying 1.69% of the Saguling Reservoir, will have a capacity of up to 92 MWp. The electricity generated will contribute to regional power systems.
records.institution: ACWA Power

records.title: COP28: CGIAR Secures Over US$890 Million to Combat Global Food and Climate Crises
records.description: CGIAR, a global agricultural research network, has secured over US$890 million to address the ongoing global food and climate crises. These funds will be used to support smallholder farmers in low- and middle-income countries and build more resilient, sustainable, and equitable food systems. The investments were announced during COP28 at a pledging event hosted by the UAE, with commitments from countries like the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, the United States, the World Bank, and Norway. CGIAR has laid out a case for US$4 billion in investments for its 2025-2027 research portfolio, highlighting the importance of increased investment in agricultural R&D to address food and climate challenges. The organization aims to support innovations and technologies that benefit smallholder farmers, vulnerable communities, and ecosystems, with a focus on climate resilience and sustainable agriculture.
records.institution: CGIAR

records.title: U.S. and UAE-Backed Initiative Announces $9 Billion More for Agricultural Innovation Projects
records.description: An additional $9 billion in funding to address agriculture's role in the climate crisis has been announced on the sidelines of the United Nations climate talks. The Agriculture Innovation Mission (AIM) for Climate, led by the United States and the United Arab Emirates, now has a total of $17 billion to invest in agriculture and food systems innovation. Food systems contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. This funding comes at a time when the COP28 climate summit is emphasizing the importance of addressing farming's impact on climate change. The projects funded by AIM cover various areas, including regenerative agriculture, food manufacturing, and reducing synthetic nitrogen use, with a focus on low- and middle-income countries.
records.institution: The Agriculture Innovation Mission (AIM) for Climate

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Qatar have solidified their bilateral cooperation by signing multiple agreements and memorandums of understanding during...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Qatar have solidified their bilateral cooperation by signing multiple agreements and memorandums of understanding during the visit of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to attend the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit and the Saudi-Qatari Coordination Council's seventh meeting. In a joint statement, both nations expressed deep concern over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, condemning Israeli actions and emphasizing the need to stop military operations and protect civilians according to international law. They reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing bilateral cooperation across various sectors, including politics, security, sports, culture, trade, investment, energy, infrastructure, and media, reflecting their determination to strengthen ties and contribute to regional stability and development.
records.institution: The Saudi-Qatari Coordination Council

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has designated $3 billion for investments across various sectors in Iraq, as announced by Sau...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has designated $3 billion for investments across various sectors in Iraq, as announced by Saudi Ambassador to Iraq Abdulaziz Al-Shammari. This allocation is part of an effort to enhance economic cooperation between the two nations. The PIF, in conjunction with the Iraq Fund for Development, is currently identifying investment opportunities in areas such as infrastructure, mining, agriculture, real estate development, and financial services. These endeavors reflect the improved diplomatic relations between Iraq and Saudi Arabia and the desire to strengthen economic ties, particularly following Saudi pledges of investment in various Iraqi sectors.
records.institution: Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF)

records.title: Saudi Environment Ministry Initiates Programs to Propel Agricultural Sector Growth
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has initiated various programs to stimulate the growth of the agricultural sector and enhance its contribution to the country's GDP. These efforts include comprehensive training programs aimed at localizing agricultural professions, such as fishing, livestock management, beekeeping, and honey production. Legislative decisions have been implemented to enforce high-quality standards for Saudi products, including food quality certificates and streamlined agricultural licensing procedures. The ministry provides support through subsidies and soft agricultural loans via the Agricultural Development Fund. Distinct labels like "Organic," "Fish," "Saudi Dates," and "Saudi Qab" certification have been introduced to promote and export agricultural products, ensuring quality and safety standards. These initiatives align with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives for food security and sustainable agricultural development, resulting in significant contributions to the GDP and increased food production in the country.
records.institution: Saudi Arabian Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: A consortium called ReFarm in the United Arab Emirates, formed by SSK Enterprises and Christof Global Impact (CGI), is partnering with Du...
records.description: A consortium called ReFarm in the United Arab Emirates, formed by SSK Enterprises and Christof Global Impact (CGI), is partnering with Dubai's FoodTech Valley to create a circular, closed-loop "GigaFarm" aimed at enhancing food security and reducing the carbon footprint of the UAE's food industry. Vertical farming technology firm Intelligent Growth Solutions (IGS) will provide the infrastructure for the farm, which is set to grow 2 billion plants annually, replacing 1% of the country's fresh produce imports. The project integrates IGS' vertical towers with five other technologies to create a closed-loop system capable of recycling over 50,000 tonnes of food waste annually. It aims to generate water without desalination or rain, divert waste from landfills, and achieve a return rate of 20-25%. The GigaFarm will utilize solar energy and low-voltage direct current to minimize carbon usage and be nearly 98% more water-efficient than field farming. Labor costs will be reduced as the IGS system eliminates the need for human intervention in the growing area. The project could set a precedent for food security strategies worldwide, with IGS planning to roll out similar systems across four continents. The UAE government has prioritized diversification and sustainability in its economic growth strategy, making innovative, low-carbon agriculture a key focus.
records.institution: UAE ReFarm

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai-based Amea Power has signed two agreements during the Cop28 climate conference to develop renewable energy projects in Africa.
records.description: Dubai-based Amea Power has signed two agreements during the Cop28 climate conference to develop renewable energy projects in Africa. The company plans to build a $600 million wind farm in Ethiopia, potentially generating 300 megawatts of energy. It is in discussions with organizations such as the African Development Bank, the International Finance Corporation, and the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) for financing. Ethiopia aims to increase its hydropower capacity to 13.5 gigawatts by 2040 to meet rising electricity demand. Amea Power is also partnering with Zimbabwe's state-owned power utility Zesa to create a solar plant with an initial capacity of 30 megawatts, with the potential to expand. The project aligns with the UAE's initiative to invest $4.5 billion in clean energy projects in Africa.
records.institution: UAE Amea Power

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has made a significant investment in the UK's wind energy sector by acquiring a 49% stake in the East Angl...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has made a significant investment in the UK's wind energy sector by acquiring a 49% stake in the East Anglia Three offshore wind farm from Spanish developer Iberdrola. This move follows another recent deal in which UAE's state-backed company, Masdar, purchased 49% of the £11 billion Dogger Bank South project in the North Sea. The UK's wind energy industry has faced financial challenges due to historical agreements that locked in low electricity prices, while costs have surged by over 40% due to inflation. Masdar's investment reflects the increasing overseas ownership of key renewable energy assets in the UK, with the company having a decade-long presence in the country's wind energy sector.
records.institution: Masdar

records.title: Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen their cooperation in marine environment...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen their cooperation in marine environmental protection. This agreement was reached at the Saudi Green Initiative forum during the UN Climate Change Conference. The MoU will facilitate collaboration between the two nations in various aspects of marine environmental protection, including monitoring, evaluation, preservation, and biodiversity conservation. Additionally, the countries will work together to reduce pollution in Saudi Arabia's territorial waters. The agreement underscores their commitment to climate change science and efforts to enhance the marine ecosystem in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia's selection to the 40-member council of the International Maritime Organization for 2024-2025 reflects its dedication to marine environmental preservation and sustainable maritime transport.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Leaders from Africa and the Middle East have introduced the $10 billion SAFE Initiative, a public-private-partnership initiative announce...
records.description: Leaders from Africa and the Middle East have introduced the $10 billion SAFE Initiative, a public-private-partnership initiative announced during COP28 to address climate-induced food insecurity in the region. The initiative, spearheaded by the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), will mobilize at least $10 billion to implement climate-smart agricultural practices, including regenerative agriculture, soil fertility management, and solar-powered irrigation. SAFE aims to attract strategic investments from both public and private sectors to enhance food security, improve livelihoods, and create green jobs. African and Middle Eastern leaders stressed the importance of tackling climate change and food security together, emphasizing the need for international collaboration and support to address these interconnected challenges.
records.institution: The SAFE Initiative of the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI)

records.title: Tadweer has launched a $2.5 million pilot project in partnership with Aquagrain, a company specializing in soil-enhancing technology usin...
records.description: Tadweer has launched a $2.5 million pilot project in partnership with Aquagrain, a company specializing in soil-enhancing technology using organic waste to reduce water and fertilizer usage by up to 50 percent in arid land and sandy soils. Supported by an AED 100 million research and development fund from ADQ, this initiative is part of ADQ Growth Lab's efforts to drive innovation and sustainability in the UAE. The project involves constructing Abu Dhabi's first commercial-scale Aquagrain facility, converting organic waste into a biodegradable polymer that acts as a water reservoir for plants, ultimately reducing carbon emissions and enhancing land utilization. This collaboration underscores the commitment to circular waste management and sustainable practices in the UAE, aligning with global goals of environmental responsibility and food security.
records.institution: Tadweer

records.title: UAE’s ADQ Announces Co-Investment Platform with Kazakhstan’s QIC
records.description: Abu Dhabi's investment company, ADQ, has announced a co-investment platform partnership with Kazakhstan's Qazaqstan Investment Corp. This collaboration will focus on sectors with substantial growth potential, including food and agriculture, mobility, healthcare, energy transformation, clean technology, financial services technology, and education technology. The platform aims to identify and capitalize on investment opportunities not only in Kazakhstan but also across Central Asia and the Caucasus region. Both ADQ and QIC have committed to providing equal financial and operational support for each investment under this partnership, aiming to contribute to the economic growth of the UAE, Kazakhstan, and the wider region. This initiative strengthens bilateral relations between the UAE and Kazakhstan, dating back to 1992.
records.institution: UAE ADQ

records.title: FarmERP, a leading Agri-Tech company with a presence in over 30 countries, has announced plans to expand its footprint into the Saudi Ara...
records.description: FarmERP, a leading Agri-Tech company with a presence in over 30 countries, has announced plans to expand its footprint into the Saudi Arabian market. The company is establishing a registered regional office as part of its growth strategy. FarmERP is already providing technology solutions to major agricultural and food supply chain companies in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Oman. It is also exploring collaborations with government entities and private stakeholders in the region. FarmERP aims to leverage advanced data science and technology, including AI and ML, to enhance food security, address climate change, optimize resource management, monitor crop and soil health, and digitize agriculture in Saudi Arabia. The company plans to expand its clientele by 200% annually, establish a registered office in Saudi Arabia, and target a 3x increase in revenue through these expansion initiatives.
records.institution: FarmERP

records.title: Banks in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have made a significant commitment at the COP28 climate talks by pledging to mobilize 1 trillion...
records.description: Banks in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have made a significant commitment at the COP28 climate talks by pledging to mobilize 1 trillion dirhams, equivalent to approximately $270 billion, in green finance. This announcement, made during the finance-focused day of the event in Dubai, reflects the UAE's ambition and commitment to addressing climate change. The funds will support various initiatives, including renewable energy projects and efforts to improve soil quality for farmers.
records.institution: UAE Banking Federation

records.title: WEF's First Movers Coalition for Food supported by Bain & Company
records.description: The World Economic Forum (WEF), in partnership with the Government of the UAE and more than 20 corporate and research partners, including Bain & Company, has launched the First Movers Coalition for Food during the COP28 climate change conference. This initiative aims to drive market demand for sustainable and low-emission agricultural products. The coalition plans to use its collective procurement power to accelerate the adoption of sustainable farming practices and innovations in the food sector, potentially reaching a value of $10 billion to $20 billion by 2030. Participating companies, with a combined revenue of $2.1 trillion, aim to shape the future of sustainable food production and contribute to global climate goals, reducing emissions and the environmental impact of food systems.
records.institution: The World Economic Forum

records.title: The Transport General Authority of Saudi Arabia has announced that Saudi Arabia has secured a seat on the International Maritime Organiza...
records.description: The Transport General Authority of Saudi Arabia has announced that Saudi Arabia has secured a seat on the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Council for the years 2024-2025. This consecutive membership in the IMO Council reflects the country's dedication to promoting secure and environmentally friendly maritime transport on a global scale. It also highlights Saudi Arabia's commitment to fostering growth and innovation in the global maritime ecosystem. Saudi Arabia's participation in the IMO Council will enable the country to enhance its support for the organization's projects and contribute to global maritime transportation initiatives, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. The IMO, a United Nations entity with 175 member nations, plays a vital role in establishing international standards for maritime security and environmental protection. Saudi Arabia's maritime fleet, ranking twentieth globally, contributes significantly to the country's status as a leading logistics hub. Prince Khalid bin Bandar bin Sultan has been proposed to lead the 33rd IMO Assembly meetings in London, further demonstrating Saudi Arabia's active involvement in the global maritime transportation sector. The Kingdom has also been making strides in green initiatives, empowering women in the maritime sector, and developing maritime expertise as part of its commitment to a sustainable maritime future.
records.institution: Saudi Transport General Authority

records.title: Gates Foundation Announces Partnership with United Arab Emirates to Accelerate Action on Climate and Strengthen Food Systems Through Investment in Agricultural Innovation
records.description: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has partnered with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to invest a total of $200 million in innovations aimed at helping smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia adapt to climate change. The announcement was made at the World Climate Action Summit, with the foundation committing $100 million to support organizations like CGIAR, which focuses on developing agricultural innovations. The funding will also support the AIM4Scale climate adaptation initiative launched by the UAE. The goal is to reach 500 million farmers by 2030 and reduce emissions from the agriculture sector by 1 gigaton per year.
records.institution: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is focusing its investments in Pakistan on various sectors, including agriculture, ports and logistics, po...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is focusing its investments in Pakistan on various sectors, including agriculture, ports and logistics, power, and more. During Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar's recent visit to the UAE, the two countries signed memorandums of understanding (MoUs) worth up to $25 billion, indicating significant investment opportunities. The UAE is committed to supporting Pakistan's development in multiple areas, and the investment is expected to enhance bilateral economic cooperation. These agreements are seen as mutually beneficial, and the UAE also expressed interest in private sector investments in sectors like food security, health, and education. Additionally, an export hub in Karachi and logistic support for remote areas of Pakistan's Balochistan and Sindh provinces are planned as part of the UAE's investment in the country.
records.institution: UAE Government

records.title: Saudi Arabia Implements Stringent Visa Rules for Foreign Domestic Workers
records.description: Saudi Arabia has recently implemented updated regulations for issuing work visas to foreign domestic workers, part of a broader push to modernize its labor market and foster equitable relationships between employers and domestic staff. The Ministry of Human Resources has raised the visa standards for hiring foreign domestic workers, particularly emphasizing individuals aged 24 and above to ensure a more responsible workforce. Eligibility for visas extends to Saudi citizens, Gulf nationals, foreign wives of Saudi men, their mothers, and holders of Saudi premium residency permits, contingent upon the employer's financial capacity. The Musaned platform, spearheaded by the Ministry, serves as a digital system educating users about rights and responsibilities, managing visa applications, recruitment, and financial transactions via apps like STC Pay and Urpay. Encompassing various domestic worker categories, from housekeepers to nannies, these regulations aim to enhance transparency, efficiency in recruitment, and establish a solid dispute resolution framework, aligning with Saudi Arabia's drive for a modernized, fair domestic labor market.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Human Resources

records.title: Oman's Khazaen Economic City is poised to host a $97 million animal feed factory, a pivotal move by the Omani Bioproducts Company—formed...
records.description: Oman's Khazaen Economic City is poised to host a $97 million animal feed factory, a pivotal move by the Omani Bioproducts Company—formed through a collaboration between the Omani Mills Group and Nakheel Oman Development Company. Located in Khazaen, the factory aims to produce specialized feeds for aquatic organisms, bolstering Oman's sustainability and agricultural endeavors. Spanning three phases with an investment cost of OMR 37 million, construction tendering began in June, with the construction contract slated for approval by year-end. Nine local companies have bid for the project, and machinery is already on-site. The factory will convert agricultural and biological by-products into value-added products, recycling date by-products like kernels, pulp, and palm fronds. It plans to annually produce 100,000 tonnes of grass feed from agricultural residues enhanced with dates, along with 300,000 tonnes of marine life feed for shrimp and fish cultivation in cages. The use of local raw materials will support food security projects, covering red meat, dairy products, aquaculture, and marine agriculture, aiming to serve domestic and export markets. This aligns with the "Oman 2040" vision, focusing on circular and bioeconomy concepts, promoting environmentally friendly and sustainable production. The collaborative efforts involve various entities, including companies under the Oman Investment Authority, partnerships with "be’ah," and support from the Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources.
records.institution: Omani Bioproducts Company

records.title: Oman saw a significant 13% drop in its producer price index during the third quarter of 2023, compared to the same period in 2022.
records.description: Oman saw a significant 13% drop in its producer price index during the third quarter of 2023, compared to the same period in 2022. Data from the Omani National Center for Statistics and Information revealed a consistent decrease in the PPI, measuring the price changes of goods leaving the producer. The report detailed a 13.7% decrease in oil and gas product prices and an 8.2% decrease in non-oil products. This decline was influenced by various factors such as lowered costs associated with crude oil and natural gas (16% decrease), manufacturing industry expenses (10.2% dip), and reduced prices in several categories including transportation, food, beverages, textiles, and specific metal products. Conversely, some product prices like woven fabric, shoes, and clothing experienced slight increases.
records.institution: Omani National Center for Statistics and Information

records.title: Oman's Consul General in Karachi, Engineer Sami Abdullah Salim Al Khanjari, expressed discontent with the limited trade between Oman and...
records.description: Oman's Consul General in Karachi, Engineer Sami Abdullah Salim Al Khanjari, expressed discontent with the limited trade between Oman and Pakistan, highlighting the substantial potential for stronger ties. Despite their proximity, trade is predominantly limited to exports of rice, mangoes, and potatoes from Pakistan to Oman. Engineer Khanjari urged for the exploration of additional exports such as onions, chillies, carrots, and other agricultural produce, emphasizing their freshness and proximity as key advantages. He encouraged the Karachi business community to diversify exports, particularly in fruits, vegetables, and textiles, aiming to boost bilateral trade volumes. Highlighting Oman's substantial port infrastructure and significant investments from various countries, he stressed the need for increased Pakistani presence in Oman's trade and investment landscape. The Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) President, Iftikhar Ahmed Sheikh, echoed the call for fostering deeper bilateral relationships, extending full support for augmenting trade and investment collaborations.
records.institution: Omani Consul General in Karachi

records.title: The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD) unveiled a pioneering air quality modeling system, a sophisticated toolset aimed at augmenting t...
records.description: The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD) unveiled a pioneering air quality modeling system, a sophisticated toolset aimed at augmenting the region’s air quality monitoring endeavors. This system, tailored for Abu Dhabi, holds the capacity to evaluate cumulative air quality impacts anticipated from new infrastructures and urban projects. Its primary objectives encompass mitigating public exposure to air pollutants, fortifying air quality across the region, and gauging the effectiveness of future environmental strategies. This innovation is poised to pinpoint pollution hotspots, create detailed air quality maps, and contribute to environmental assessments. Engineer Faisal Al Hammadi, EAD's Executive Director of the Environmental Quality Sector, emphasized the criticality of evidence-based tools to manage air quality effectively, citing the system's pivotal role in fostering a balance between economic growth, environmental conservation, and societal well-being. The system's scope extends to supporting compliance evaluation, air quality forecasts, public awareness, and emergency response, championing a healthier environment and quality of life. Additionally, the initiative will bolster collaboration with key partners, including the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the Abu Dhabi Executive Office, health and law enforcement departments, and various governmental bodies, reaffirming a concerted effort toward improving air quality.
records.institution: The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD)

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s Economic Reforms are Boosting M&A Activity
records.description: Saudi Arabia's economic reforms are proving to be a catalyst for increased mergers and acquisitions (M&A) activities in the country. The nation's economic growth, buoyed by non-oil sectors, has generated favorable conditions for robust M&A activity. Amid a global economic slowdown and various geopolitical tensions worldwide, the region's economic reforms, including those in Saudi Arabia, are expected to spur this trend further. The Kingdom's economy, among the largest in the region and one of the fastest-growing globally, presents a promising landscape for investors. Despite forecasts of a slowdown in the GCC's growth due to a decrease in contributions from hydrocarbons, the momentum in non-hydrocarbon sectors is anticipated to persist. Saudi Arabia has seen a substantial increase in outbound investment, with figures for the first half of 2023 reaching $10.9 billion, part of a projected MENA total of $31.9 billion. This upswing in M&A activity is not limited to Saudi Arabia alone but extends across the MENA region, showcasing an active and diverse investor base. Economic diversification efforts in sectors like technology, renewable energy, e-commerce, and infrastructure have bolstered the country's attractiveness for investment. The Saudi Public Investment Fund's ventures, including acquisitions in various sectors and a significant stake in a Japanese gaming giant, exemplify the nation's openness to global investment and collaboration. The Saudi government's initiatives, such as Vision 2030 and the Public Investment Fund, serve as key indicators of Saudi Arabia's commitment to inviting global investors and fostering economic growth. This upward trajectory in M&A activity and economic diversification signals a promising future not only for Saudi Arabia but also for the entire region, showcasing substantial potential for further growth and expansion.
records.institution: Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF)

records.title: Pakistan's Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar is poised to ink seven MoUs valued at $10 billion during an upcoming visit to Kuwait, as ap...
records.description: Pakistan's Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar is poised to ink seven MoUs valued at $10 billion during an upcoming visit to Kuwait, as approved in a recent federal cabinet meeting. These memoranda, born from the efforts of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), aim to bolster Pakistan's economy by inviting investments from Kuwait across various sectors including agriculture, mining, IT, defense production, energy, and food security. These initiatives underscore Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment, particularly from Gulf nations, to navigate challenging economic conditions. The proposed projects encompass endeavors like expanding water reservoirs, enhancing mining facilities, fortifying mangrove forests along coastal areas, and investment schemes in the information technology sector. Pakistan and Kuwait, rooted in shared cultural and faith-based values, seek to strengthen their economic ties beyond existing diplomatic relations, with the aspiration to elevate mutual trade to $1 billion annually within the next few years, marking a significant milestone in their growing economic partnership.
records.institution: Pakistani Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC)

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Planning and Economic Development, Dr.
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Planning and Economic Development, Dr. Hala El-Said, and Oman's Minister of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion, Qais bin Mohammed Musa Al-Yousef, recently convened to bolster collaboration between their nations. Their focus lies in establishing a joint fund aimed at investing in specific sectors like agricultural industries, food processing, and pharmaceuticals. Dr. El-Said commended Oman's Sovereign Investment Fund's efforts, citing Egypt's keenness to learn from Oman's experience in setting up the Egyptian Sovereign Fund. Al-Yousef echoed the sentiment, emphasizing the importance of reciprocal discussions to strengthen economic ties, culminating in agreements to form technical teams to explore industrial integration, discuss free trade agreements, and strategize around incentives and industrial strategies for mutual benefit. This meeting underscores the burgeoning economic and investment bonds between Egypt and Oman, signifying a shared commitment to expanding collaboration in vital sectors through the proposed joint fund.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: ACWA Power, a prominent developer and operator of power generation and desalinated water plants based in Saudi Arabia, has successfully c...
records.description: ACWA Power, a prominent developer and operator of power generation and desalinated water plants based in Saudi Arabia, has successfully clinched a contract to establish a substantial 200 MW wind power plant across Uzbekistan's Karaozak and Beruniy districts. The endeavor, financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, saw stiff competition with two bidders vying for the project. ACWA Power's offer, priced at $4.09 per kWh for both electricity generation and storage, outpaced its competitor, Masdar, whose bid stood at $4.99. This new project marks ACWA Power's continued expansion in Uzbekistan, following its prior success in securing the country's initial wind power plant contract. Their earlier 100 MW facility in Karaozak was secured with a winning bid of $2.57 per kWh of electricity. ACWA Power's robust commitment to renewable energy extends globally, with projects spanning diverse regions like Azerbaijan and Egypt, showcasing their pivotal role in accelerating the shift towards sustainable energy sources. These endeavors not only contribute to reducing carbon emissions but also stimulate economic growth within the regions they operate in, reinforcing their position as key players in fostering the renewable energy transition.
records.institution: ACWA Power

records.title: Reef Saudi has initiated a significant venture by establishing bee clinics in major Saudi cities—Jeddah, Jazan, Madinah, and Abha—dedicat...
records.description: Reef Saudi has initiated a significant venture by establishing bee clinics in major Saudi cities—Jeddah, Jazan, Madinah, and Abha—dedicated to beekeepers. These clinics offer crucial services encompassing examination, diagnosis, guidance, and assistance, thereby empowering small-scale producers. The clinics' objectives include safeguarding the nation's bee population from diseases and pests, fostering self-sufficiency by increasing local bee colonies, and deploying mobile clinics to directly aid beekeepers on-site. The initiative, backed by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, received appreciation from beekeepers like Hasan Al-Qarni, who underscored the clinics' role in diagnosing diseases, providing guidance, and devising sustainable solutions for beekeepers in the Kingdom. This support has translated into significant achievements, such as Al-Qarni winning top honors in an Arab honey competition, further highlighting the Ministry's backing for local beekeepers. Reef Saudi, focusing on enhancing the honey sector, has substantially bolstered food security, showcasing a 49 percent progress rate toward self-sufficiency, notably increasing honey production from 2,100 tons in 2020 to 3,748 tons in 2023. Moreover, since the launch of the bee clinics, over 6,000 samples have been processed, enabling examinations and the development of a comprehensive database for diseases and pests impacting bees in the region. Reef Saudi's overarching aim remains to bolster farmers' capabilities, enhance agricultural productivity, and elevate the living standards of rural families by facilitating market access and agricultural resources. This program continues to play a pivotal role in advancing crop cultivation throughout Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Reef Saudi

records.title: DANA Global and Rivulis, two influential entities in the sustainable agriculture domain, have joined forces to establish an innovative de...
records.description: DANA Global and Rivulis, two influential entities in the sustainable agriculture domain, have joined forces to establish an innovative demo farm in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi. This groundbreaking collaboration aims to exhibit and educate farmers on sustainable farming solutions tailored for extreme weather and arid environments. By leveraging advanced micro irrigation systems and climate farming models, Rivulis will demonstrate efficient crop production methods that combat climate change effects, water scarcity, biodiversity loss, and enhance food security while ensuring sustainable livelihoods for growers. The initiative, part of Masdar City's beta site, emphasizes the transition to more sustainable farming practices by showcasing Rivulis' cutting-edge irrigation and fertigation systems, echoing DANA's commitment to fostering sustainable agricultural practices in the region. The partnership's focus on fostering innovative solutions aligns with the UAE's National Food Security Strategy, marking a significant step towards addressing critical agricultural challenges posed by climate change in the Middle East and Africa. Furthermore, Rivulis is pioneering socio-economic initiatives like Impact Financing and Rivulis Climate programs, aiming to democratize sustainable farming by empowering small-scale farmers and promoting accessibility to advanced technologies for all growers.
records.institution: DANA Global & Rivulis

records.title: Dubai has opened a trade office in Lagos, Nigeria, to enhance cross-border trade and investment opportunities between the two countries.
records.description: Dubai has opened a trade office in Lagos, Nigeria, to enhance cross-border trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. The office will serve as a platform for communication and collaboration, facilitating business matchmaking and networking events. Dubai sees Nigeria as a strategically important market, offering access to the broader West African region. In turn, Nigeria views the UAE as a key gateway to the Middle East. The establishment of the trade office is expected to strengthen economic ties and boost bilateral trade.
records.institution: Dubai Chambers

records.title: UAE Launches Power, Water Saving Project in Public Buildings
records.description: The UAE has initiated a collaborative project aiming to significantly curtail power and water consumption across over 400 federal government buildings in its first phase, as announced by Sharif Al-Olama, Undersecretary of the Energy and Infrastructure Ministry for Energy Affairs. The initiative, developed in partnership with the private sector, is geared towards reducing electricity usage by 20 percent and water consumption by 30 percent within these buildings. Al-Olama emphasized that this undertaking aligns with a broader strategy aimed at long-term energy management and water security in the UAE, slated until 2036, and is an integral component of the nation's 2050 national energy program. The project's expansion plan extends beyond federal buildings to encompass government facilities across the emirates, including agricultural entities grappling with energy and water cost challenges, signifying a concerted effort toward sustainability and resource optimization.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure

records.title: Tetra Pak's collaboration with HSA Group in Yemen brings fortified flavored milk to 10,000 school children, addressing nutritional challe...
records.description: Tetra Pak's collaboration with HSA Group in Yemen brings fortified flavored milk to 10,000 school children, addressing nutritional challenges amidst conflict-related food insecurity. The initiative, starting in the Taiz governorate, aims to bolster students' health and regular attendance, crucial in a country deeply affected by prolonged conflict, disrupting essential services and food access. Tetra Pak's aseptic packaging ensures freshness for up to 12 months, pivotal in Yemen's compromised infrastructure. Local production by HSA Group fortifies UHT milk, battling nutritional deficiencies. Overseen by HSA's Humanitarian Development Program, this effort engages various stakeholders, including the Ministry of Education and UN agencies, ensuring safe delivery, storage, and awareness campaigns. Notably, this venture integrates recycling education, emphasizing environmental consciousness. The collaboration's broader vision includes enhancing food systems, aiding farmers, and expanding nutrition access, with plans to diversify food offerings for children, aiming for sustainable impact and future growth through partnership expansion.
records.institution: Tetra Pak & Hayel Saeed Anam (HSA) Group

records.title: Sugar prices in the UAE have soared by as much as eight percent in recent months, stemming from a global surge due to reduced supplies fo...
records.description: Sugar prices in the UAE have soared by as much as eight percent in recent months, stemming from a global surge due to reduced supplies following droughts impacting harvests in India and Thailand, two major exporters. However, the outlook appears promising as India prepares to resume exports through the National Cooperative for Exports Ltd (NCEL). This initiative seeks to bypass intermediaries by facilitating direct dealings between the government and farmers, potentially leading to a decline in sugar prices in the UAE. Dr. Dhananjay Datar, chairman of Al Adil Trading, highlighted that the current market stock primarily originates from Brazil, signaling a potential shift once Indian sugar enters the local market. Kamal Vachani from Al Maya Group noted that besides traditional suppliers like Brazil and Thailand, the UAE can explore importing from countries like Mexico, Australia, and Africa, which have been ramping up sugar production. With potential openings in markets like Thailand and Germany, there's optimism about diversifying sugar imports and stabilizing prices in the UAE.
records.institution: Indian National Cooperative for Exports Ltd (NCEL)

records.title: The inaugural International Forum and Exhibition for Sustainable Agriculture in Riyadh gathered over 55 speakers from 35 nations, conveni...
records.description: The inaugural International Forum and Exhibition for Sustainable Agriculture in Riyadh gathered over 55 speakers from 35 nations, convening experts and researchers to facilitate knowledge exchange and cultivate networks within the field. Hosted by the National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture and inaugurated by Minister Abdulrahman Al-Fadhley of the Kingdom’s Environment, Water, and Agriculture Ministry, the three-day event aimed to foster innovation and closer professional ties. The agenda focused on leveraging natural resources in agricultural production, featuring discussions led by experts like Naser Eddin Al-Obaid on sustainable water use, soil enhancement techniques, and the utilization of wild plant species for increased productivity. Subsequent days delved into the realm of digital agriculture, with sessions led by David Muath and Abdulaziz Al-Malik, addressing smart agriculture and environmental aspects. The forum also highlighted marketing strategies and sustainable food value chains, supported by an exhibition showcasing cutting-edge products and innovations from over 35 companies and organizations dedicated to sustainable agriculture.
records.institution: Saudi National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture

records.title: At the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference, a pivotal Saudi-African Summit convened to fortify economic and trade connections between...
records.description: At the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference, a pivotal Saudi-African Summit convened to fortify economic and trade connections between Saudi Arabia and Africa. Both regions share parallel economic sectors, offering vast opportunities across mining, industry, tourism, finance, and more, with a combined economy of $4 trillion. Positioned at the crossroads of three continents, Saudi Arabia has the potential to emerge as a vital economic hub for Africa. Africa, as the second-largest continent globally, boasts a $3 trillion economy and houses five of the world's fastest-growing economies. With the Saudi economy ranking as the largest in the MENA region, valued at over $1 trillion and experiencing rapid growth, bilateral trade between Saudi Arabia and African countries has exceeded SR74 billion in 2003, favoring Saudi Arabia in terms of trade balance. Non-oil exports from Saudi Arabia to Africa have shown substantial growth, reaching SR31.94 billion last year, and Saudi investments in Africa over the past decade have reached SR49.5 billion, with 47 Saudi companies presently operating in the continent. The recent conference witnessed the signing of over 50 agreements and MoUs, spanning various sectors like tourism, investment, finance, energy, mining, agriculture, and more, reflecting a shared commitment to mutual development aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 and Africa’s Agenda 2063. This deeper economic and trade collaboration is anticipated to yield mutual benefits for both regions and their respective developmental frameworks.
records.institution: Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference

records.title: The collaboration between a UAE-based virtual assets consultancy, PXDX, and a Pakistani software house intends to introduce healthcare se...
records.description: The collaboration between a UAE-based virtual assets consultancy, PXDX, and a Pakistani software house intends to introduce healthcare services into the Saudi market, initially targeting the healthcare sector before expanding into other domains. The founding CEO of PXDX, Dr. Rehan Al Taji, highlighted their collaboration during The Future Summit in Karachi, emphasizing the importation of services from the Pakistani software house into Saudi Arabia. While specific details were not disclosed, Dr. Al Taji expressed admiration for Pakistani startups, acknowledging their innovation and potential in expanding business under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. This initiative aims to diversify the Saudi economy and enhance sectors like health, education, infrastructure, recreation, and tourism. Additionally, Dana Al Salem, a Kuwaiti tech entrepreneur, stressed the importance of countries projecting a clear purpose to attract investors, citing the significance of Pakistan refining its global image and focusing on leveraging its agricultural sector to address food scarcity concerns.
records.institution: PXDX

records.title: Paris-based agribusiness giant InVivo is set to establish a marketing office in Saudi Arabia's port of Dammam early next year, strategica...
records.description: Paris-based agribusiness giant InVivo is set to establish a marketing office in Saudi Arabia's port of Dammam early next year, strategically positioning itself to capitalize on evolving global grain demand, particularly in the Middle East. In an interview with Reuters, InVivo CEO Thierry Blandinieres underscored the office's pivotal role in securing grain supplies for local feed makers in Saudi Arabia amid shifting dynamics in the grain market. Traditional markets like Algeria have seen a decline in French wheat exports, yet Blandinieres remains optimistic, highlighting potential sales growth in China and renewed interest from Egypt. While emphasizing the fluctuating nature of market demand, particularly in China, InVivo is actively exploring alternative markets and eyeing expansion into West African territories. Aman Sethi, leading the Saudi office from Dubai, brings extensive experience, emphasizing InVivo’s focus not just on the Middle East but also on securing West African markets. Moreover, InVivo’s recent acquisition of Australia’s United Malt Group strengthens its position as the world's largest maltster, marking a significant milestone in its strategic growth trajectory. This expansion illustrates InVivo's commitment to a diversified global presence and its proactive stance in responding to evolving market dynamics.
records.institution: InVivo

records.title: Oman Investment Authority completed six major projects valued at $10.3 billion, aiming to diversify the economy, foster regional growth,...
records.description: Oman Investment Authority completed six major projects valued at $10.3 billion, aiming to diversify the economy, foster regional growth, attract investments, and create job opportunities, particularly for SMEs. The Duqm Refinery and Petrochemical Industries project, the most significant endeavor, is set to transform Duqm into a key industrial hub with a 230,000-barrel-per-day refinery and storage facilities. Other projects include the Ras Markaz Crude Oil Storage Terminal, Duqm Integrated Power and Water Project, Rabt project for electricity transmission, Khuweimah Shrimp Farm for food security, and JW Marriott Hotel Muscat to boost tourism. Additionally, Oman launched three digital platforms to enhance its investment climate and facilitate business processes, signaling a push towards modernizing the economy and fostering a more efficient business environment.
records.institution: Oman Investment Authority

records.title: Saudi aid agency KSrelief extended assistance to Afghan quake victims by distributing 1,000 food packages in Zinda Jan District, benefitt...
records.description: Saudi aid agency KSrelief extended assistance to Afghan quake victims by distributing 1,000 food packages in Zinda Jan District, benefitting 375 families and 6,000 individuals. This aid followed the recent provision of 550 winter bags to 3,850 individuals in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. The relief efforts align with KSrelief's global humanitarian assistance program. Additionally, discussions between KSrelief and the EU's special representative for the Horn of Africa focused on supporting humanitarian efforts in the east African peninsula region.
records.institution: KSRelief

records.title: PepsiCo, a global food and beverage giant, has unveiled plans to invest over 200 million Saudi Riyals (US$53.3 million) in expanding its...
records.description: PepsiCo, a global food and beverage giant, has unveiled plans to invest over 200 million Saudi Riyals (US$53.3 million) in expanding its snack facility at the Dammam plant in Saudi Arabia. The initiative, shared during the Future Investment Initiative conference in Riyadh, aligns with PepsiCo's commitment to sustainable agricultural practices in Saudi Arabia and supports the Kingdom's food production goals outlined in Vision 2030. This investment aims to bolster the plant's production capacity, marking a significant step toward enhancing the Saudi agricultural sector and fostering sustainable food production. The expansion is set to be completed by next year and represents PepsiCo's ongoing efforts to reinforce its presence in the region, where it manufactures brands like Lay’s, Doritos, Quaker Oats, and the local crisp brand Tasali. This substantial investment highlights PepsiCo's dedication to promoting sustainable agriculture and strengthening its foothold in the food and beverage industry, reinforcing its commitment to sustainable practices in Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: PepsiCo
